question: Name the movie with the most ratings.

question: What is the average rating for movie titled 'When Will I Be Loved'?

question: What is the percentage of the ratings were rated by user who was a subcriber?
evidence: user is a subscriber refers to user_subscriber = 1; percentage of ratings = DIVIDE(SUM(user_subscriber = 1), SUM(rating_score)) as percent;

gold: SELECT (COUNT(CASE WHEN user_subscriber = 1 THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage_of_subscriber_ratings FROM ratings;

question: How much is the popularity of the movie that has the highest popularity between 1920 to 1929 and when did the movie received its first rating score of 1 from the users who were a paying subscriber when they rated the movie ?

SQL: WITH HighestPopularity AS (SELECT movie_id, movie_popularity FROM movies WHERE movie_release_year BETWEEN 1920 AND 1929 ORDER BY movie_popularity DESC LIMIT 1) SELECT movie_popularity, (SELECT MIN(rating_timestamp_utc) FROM ratings WHERE movie_id = HighestPopularity.movie_id AND rating_score = 1 AND user_has_payment_method = 1) FROM HighestPopularity;
gold: SELECT MAX(movie_popularity), (SELECT MIN(rating_timestamp_utc) FROM ratings WHERE movie_id = (SELECT movie_id FROM movies WHERE movie_release_year BETWEEN 1920 AND 1929 ORDER BY movie_popularity DESC LIMIT 1) AND rating_score = 1 AND user_has_payment_method = 1) FROM movies WHERE movie_release_year BETWEEN 1920 AND 1929;

question: Which year has the least number of movies that was released and what is the title of the movie in that year that has the highest number of rating score of 1?

question: How many users who created a list in the February of 2016 were eligible for trial when they created the list? Indicate the user id of the user who has the most number of followers in his list in February of 2016.

question: How many directors have directed atleast 10 movies between 1960 to 1985? Indicate the name of the movie in those years of each director that received the highest amount of 5 rating score.
evidence: directed at least 10 movies refers to count(direct_name)>10; 1960 to 1985 refer to movie_release_year
SQL: WITH EligibleDirectors AS (SELECT director_name FROM movies WHERE movie_release_year BETWEEN 1960 AND 1985 GROUP BY director_name HAVING COUNT(movie_id) >= 10), TopMovies AS (SELECT movie_id, COUNT(rating_id) AS five_star_ratings FROM ratings WHERE rating_score = 5 GROUP BY movie_id ORDER BY five_star_ratings DESC LIMIT 1) SELECT M.director_name, M.movie_title FROM movies M JOIN TopMovies TM ON M.movie_id = TM.movie_id WHERE M.director_name IN (SELECT director_name FROM EligibleDirectors);
gold: WITH EligibleDirectors AS (SELECT director_name FROM movies WHERE movie_release_year BETWEEN 1960 AND 1985 GROUP BY director_name HAVING COUNT(movie_id) >= 10), TopMovies AS (SELECT movie_id, COUNT(rating_id) AS five_star_ratings FROM ratings WHERE rating_score = 5 GROUP BY movie_id ORDER BY five_star_ratings DESC LIMIT 1) SELECT M.director_name, M.movie_title FROM movies M JOIN TopMovies TM ON M.movie_id = TM.movie_id WHERE M.director_name IN (SELECT director_name FROM EligibleDirectors);

SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.rating_score = 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.user_id) FROM ratings AS T1 INNER JOIN movies AS T2 ON T1.movie_id = T2.movie_id WHERE T2.movie_title = 'Go Go Tales'
gold: SELECT (COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.rating_score = 5 THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(T2.rating_score)) AS percentage FROM movies T1 JOIN ratings T2 ON T1.movie_id = T2.movie_id WHERE T1.movie_title = 'Go Go Tales';

question: Give the percentage of subscribers who rated who rated the movie "G.I. Jane".
evidence: movie "G.I. Jane" refers to movie_title = 'G.I. Jane'; subscribers refers to user_subscriber = 1; percentage refers to DIVIDE(COUNT(user_subscriber = 1),COUNT(user_subscriber))*100
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T3.user_subscriber = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(*) FROM ratings AS T1 INNER JOIN movies AS T2 ON T1.movie_id = T2.movie_id INNER JOIN lists_users AS T3 ON T1.user_id = T3.user_id WHERE T2.movie_title = 'G.I. Jane'
gold: SELECT (COUNT(CASE WHEN user_subscriber = 1 THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage FROM ratings WHERE movie_id = (SELECT movie_id FROM movies WHERE movie_title = 'G.I. Jane');

question: For all the users who gave "A Shot in the Dark" a rating, how many percent of them is a paying subscriber?

SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.user_has_payment_method = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(*) FROM ratings AS T1 INNER JOIN movies AS T2 ON T1.movie_id = T2.movie_id INNER JOIN lists_users AS T3 ON T1.user_id = T3.user_id WHERE T2.movie_title = 'A Shot in the Dark'
gold: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T3.user_has_payment_method = 1 THEN T2.user_id END) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT T2.user_id)) AS percentage_paying_subscribers FROM movies T1 JOIN ratings T2 ON T1.movie_id = T2.movie_id JOIN ratings_users T3 ON T2.user_id = T3.user_id WHERE T1.movie_title = 'A Shot in the Dark';

question: Name the store with the highest quantity in sales? What is the least quantity title from the store's sale?
evidence: qty is abbreviation for quantity; highest quantity refers to MAX(qty); least quantity refers to MIN(qty)
SQL: SELECT T2.stor_name, MIN(T1.qty) AS least_qty FROM sales T1 JOIN stores T2 ON T1.stor_id = T2.stor_id WHERE T1.stor_id = (SELECT stor_id FROM sales GROUP BY stor_id ORDER BY SUM(qty) DESC LIMIT 1) GROUP BY T1.title_id ORDER BY least_qty ASC LIMIT 1;
gold: WITH StoreSales AS (SELECT stor_id, SUM(qty) AS TotalQty FROM sales GROUP BY stor_id), MaxStore AS (SELECT stor_id FROM StoreSales WHERE TotalQty = (SELECT MAX(TotalQty) FROM StoreSales)) SELECT stores.stor_name, MIN(sales.qty) AS MinQty FROM sales JOIN stores ON sales.stor_id = stores.stor_id WHERE sales.stor_id IN (SELECT stor_id FROM MaxStore) GROUP BY sales.title_id ORDER BY MinQty LIMIT 1;

gold: SELECT T1.title, T2.pub_name, T3.royalty FROM titles T1 JOIN publishers T2 ON T1.pub_id = T2.pub_id JOIN roysched T3 ON T1.title_id = T3.title_id WHERE T1.title_id = 'BU 2075';

question: Name the store with ID 7066 and calculate the percentage of the the quantity ordered that were on 'Net 30' payment terms.
evidence: store with ID 7066 refers to stor_ID = '7066'; 'Net 60' payment terms refers to payterm = 'Net 60'; qty is abbreviation for quantity; percentage = DIVIDE(payterms = 'Net 60', sum(qty))*100
SQL: SELECT (SUM(CASE WHEN payterms = 'Net 30' THEN qty ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / SUM(qty)) AS percentage_net30 FROM sales WHERE stor_id = '7066';

question: For all the complaint callers on 2017/3/27, what percentage of the clients are females?

SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM callcenterlogs T1 JOIN client T2 ON T1."rand client" = T2.client_id WHERE T2.email LIKE '%gmail.com' AND T1."Date received" BETWEEN '2017-02-01' AND '2017-02-28';
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM callcenterlogs T1 JOIN client T2 ON T1."rand client" = T2.client_id WHERE T2.email LIKE '%gmail.com' AND T1."Date received" BETWEEN '2017-02-01' AND '2017-02-28';

question: What is the average number of stars given by Oregon clients in their reviews?
evidence: average = DIVIDE(SUM(State = 'Oregon'), COUNT(district_id)); Oregon refers to state = 'Oregon';
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(T3.Stars) AS REAL) / COUNT(T3.Stars) AS average FROM state AS T1 INNER JOIN district AS T2 ON T1.StateCode = T2.state_abbrev INNER JOIN reviews AS T3 ON T2.district_id = T3.district_id WHERE T1.State = 'Oregon'
gold: SELECT AVG(R.Stars) FROM reviews R JOIN client C ON R.district_id = C.district_id JOIN district D ON C.district_id = D.district_id JOIN state S ON D.state_abbrev = S.StateCode WHERE S.State = 'Oregon';

question: What percentage of clients who sent their complaints by postal mail are age 50 and older?
evidence: percentage = MULTIPLY(DIVIDE(SUM("Submitted via" = 'Postal mail'), COUNT(client_id)), 1.0); sent their complaints by refers to "Submitted via"; age > 50;
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.age > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T2.`Submitted via`) FROM client AS T1 INNER JOIN events AS T2 ON T1.client_id = T2.Client_ID WHERE T2.`Submitted via` = 'Postal mail'
gold: SELECT (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.age >= 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS FLOAT) / COUNT(T1.Client_ID)) * 100 AS percentage FROM events T1 JOIN client T2 ON T1.Client_ID = T2.client_id WHERE T1."Submitted via" = 'Postal mail';

question: Compute the average time in minute for each age group
evidence: teenager refers to 13 < age < = 19; adult refers to 19 < age < = 65; elder refers to age < = 65; highest average time per complaint = max(divide(sum(ser_time), count(ser_time)))
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.age > 13 AND T1.age <= 19 THEN 60 * strftime('%H', ser_time) + strftime('%M', ser_time) + strftime('%S', ser_time) / 60 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN T1.age > 13 AND T1.age <= 19 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS teenagerAverageMins, CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.age > 19 AND T1.age <= 65 THEN 60 * strftime('%H', ser_time) + strftime('%M', ser_time) + strftime('%S', ser_time) / 60 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN T1.age > 19 AND T1.age <= 65 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS adultAverageMins , CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.age > 65 THEN 60 * strftime('%H', ser_time) + strftime('%M', ser_time) + strftime('%S', ser_time) / 60 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN T1.age > 65 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS elderAverageMins FROM client AS T1 INNER JOIN callcenterlogs AS T2 ON T1.client_id = T2.`rand client`
gold: SELECT CASE WHEN age > 65 THEN 'elder' WHEN age > 19 THEN 'adult' ELSE 'teenager' END AS age_group, AVG(CAST(ser_time AS INTEGER)) AS avg_time FROM client JOIN callcenterlogs ON client.client_id = callcenterlogs."rand client" GROUP BY age_group;

question: What is the social number of the client who has the longest delay in his/her complaint? Calculate the days of delay and state the company's response to the consumer.
evidence: social number refers to social; longest delay = max(subtract(Date sent to company, Date received)); days of delay = subtract(Date sent to company, Date received); company's response refers to 'Company response to consumer'
SQL: SELECT T1.social , 365 * (strftime('%Y', T2.`Date sent to company`) - strftime('%Y', T2.`Date received`)) + 30 * (strftime('%M', T2.`Date sent to company`) - strftime('%M', T2.`Date received`)) + (strftime('%d', T2.`Date sent to company`) - strftime('%d', T2.`Date received`)), T2.`Company response to consumer` FROM client AS T1 INNER JOIN events AS T2 ON T1.client_id = T2.Client_ID ORDER BY 365 * (strftime('%Y', T2.`Date sent to company`) - strftime('%Y', T2.`Date received`)) + 30 * (strftime('%M', T2.`Date sent to company`) - strftime('%M', T2.`Date received`)) + (strftime('%d', T2.`Date sent to company`) - strftime('%d', T2.`Date received`)) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T3.social, T1."Company response to consumer" FROM events T1 JOIN client T3 ON T1.Client_ID = T3.client_id ORDER BY (julianday(T1."Date sent to company") - julianday(T1."Date received")) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: Find the difference in percentage of the movies under keywords of "woman director" and "independent film".
evidence: under keywords of "woman director" and "independent film" refers to keyword_name = 'woman director' and keyword_name = 'independent film'; difference in percentage = divide(subtract(count(movie_id) when keyword_name = 'woman director', count(movie_id) when keyword_name = 'independent film'), count(movie_id)) as percentage

gold: SELECT ((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T2.keyword_name = 'woman director' THEN T1.movie_id END) - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T2.keyword_name = 'independent film' THEN T1.movie_id END)) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT T1.movie_id)) AS percentage_difference FROM movie_keywords T1 JOIN keyword T2 ON T1.keyword_id = T2.keyword_id;

SQL: SELECT (MAX(CAST(SUBSTR(T2.screentime, 3, 2) AS REAL)) - MIN(CAST(SUBSTR(T2.screentime, 3, 2) AS REAL))) * 100 / MIN(CAST(SUBSTR(T2.screentime, 3, 2) AS REAL)) FROM movie AS T1 INNER JOIN characters AS T2 ON T1.MovieID = T2.MovieID WHERE T1.Title = 'Batman'
gold: SELECT ((MAX(CAST(screentime AS INTEGER)) - MIN(CAST(screentime AS INTEGER))) * 100.0 / MIN(CAST(screentime AS INTEGER))) AS PercentageDifference FROM characters WHERE MovieID = (SELECT MovieID FROM movie WHERE Title = 'Batman');

SQL: SELECT T2.City FROM (SELECT LocationID, COUNT(TweetID) AS tweet_count FROM twitter GROUP BY LocationID) AS T1 JOIN location AS T2 ON T1.LocationID = T2.LocationID WHERE T2.City IN ('Bangkok', 'Chiang Mai') ORDER BY T1.tweet_count DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T2.City FROM (SELECT LocationID, COUNT(TweetID) AS tweet_count FROM twitter GROUP BY LocationID) AS T1 JOIN location AS T2 ON T1.LocationID = T2.LocationID WHERE T2.City IN ('Bangkok', 'Chiang Mai') ORDER BY T1.tweet_count DESC LIMIT 1

question: Please list the top 3 cities with the most number of tweets posted in Canada.
evidence: "Canada" is the Country; city with most number of tweets refers to City where Max(Count(TweetID))
SQL: SELECT location.City FROM location JOIN (SELECT LocationID, COUNT(TweetID) AS TweetCount FROM twitter GROUP BY LocationID) AS tweet_count ON location.LocationID = tweet_count.LocationID WHERE location.Country = 'Canada' ORDER BY tweet_count.TweetCount DESC LIMIT 3;
gold: SELECT T2.City FROM twitter T1 JOIN location T2 ON T1.LocationID = T2.LocationID WHERE T2.Country = 'Canada' GROUP BY T2.City ORDER BY COUNT(T1.TweetID) DESC LIMIT 3;

question: Among all the tweets sent by male users in Argentina, what is the text of the one with the most number of likes?

SQL: SELECT T2.text FROM user AS T1 INNER JOIN twitter AS T2 ON T1.UserID = T2.UserID INNER JOIN location AS T3 ON T2.LocationID = T3.LocationID WHERE T3.Country = 'Argentina' AND T1.Gender = 'Male' ORDER BY T2.Likes DESC LIMIT 1

question: What is the average number of likes for a tweet posted by a male user on Mondays?
evidence: male user refers to Gender = 'Male'; 'Monday' is the Weekday; average number of likes = Divide (Sum(Likes), Count(TweetID))
SQL: SELECT AVG(T2.Likes) AS AverageLikes FROM twitter T2 JOIN user T1 ON T2.UserID = T1.UserID WHERE T1.Gender = 'Male' AND T2.Weekday = 'Monday';

question: Tweets posted from which city has a higher number of average likes, Bangkok or Chiang Mai?
evidence: "Bangkok" and "Chiang Mai" are both City; average number of like = Divide (Sum(Likes), Count(TweetID))
SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T2.City = 'Bangkok' THEN Likes ELSE NULL END) / COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.City = 'Bangkok' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS bNum , SUM(CASE WHEN City = 'Chiang Mai' THEN Likes ELSE NULL END) / COUNT(CASE WHEN City = 'Chiang Mai' THEN TweetID ELSE NULL END) AS cNum FROM twitter AS T1 INNER JOIN location AS T2 ON T1.LocationID = T2.LocationID WHERE T2.City IN ('Bangkok', 'Chiang Mai')
gold: SELECT T2.City, AVG(T1.Likes) AS AverageLikes FROM twitter T1 JOIN location T2 ON T1.LocationID = T2.LocationID WHERE T2.City IN ('Bangkok', 'Chiang Mai') GROUP BY T2.City

question: What is the difference in the average GPA of students who took the hardest and easiest courses?
evidence: difference in the average gpa = SUBTRACT(AVG(gpa WHERE MAX(diff)), AVG(gpa where min(diff))); difficulty of the course refers to diff; hardest course refers to MAX(diff); easiest course refers to MIN(diff);
SQL: SELECT ABS((SELECT AVG(S.gpa) FROM student S JOIN registration R ON S.student_id = R.student_id JOIN course C ON R.course_id = C.course_id WHERE C.diff = (SELECT MAX(diff) FROM course)) - (SELECT AVG(S.gpa) FROM student S JOIN registration R ON S.student_id = R.student_id JOIN course C ON R.course_id = C.course_id WHERE C.diff = (SELECT MIN(diff) FROM course))) AS difference;
gold: SELECT ABS((SELECT AVG(gpa) FROM student WHERE student_id IN (SELECT student_id FROM registration WHERE course_id IN (SELECT course_id FROM course WHERE diff = (SELECT MAX(diff) FROM course)))) - (SELECT AVG(gpa) FROM student WHERE student_id IN (SELECT student_id FROM registration WHERE course_id IN (SELECT course_id FROM course WHERE diff = (SELECT MIN(diff) FROM course))))) AS difference;

question: Calculate the average age of patients with prediabetes care plan.
evidence: SUBTRACT(SUM(deathdate), SUM(birthdate)), COUNT(patient) where REASONDESCRIPTION = 'Prediabetes' from careplans;
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.deathdate IS NULL THEN strftime('%Y', T2.STOP) - strftime('%Y', T1.birthdate) ELSE strftime('%Y', T1.deathdate) - strftime('%Y', T1.birthdate) END) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT T1.patient) FROM patients AS T1 INNER JOIN careplans AS T2 ON T1.patient = T2.PATIENT WHERE T2.REASONDESCRIPTION = 'Prediabetes'

question: How long did Isadora Moen's allergy last? Tell me what kind of allergy she has.

question: Give me the reason, name of the drug, and duration of medication under encounter ID 23c293ec-dbae-4a22-896e-f12cf3c8bac3. Tell me if the patient is still alive.

SQL: SELECT T2.REASONDESCRIPTION, T2.DESCRIPTION , strftime('%J', T2.STOP) - strftime('%J', T2.START) AS days , CASE WHEN T1.deathdate IS NULL THEN 'alive' ELSE 'dead' END FROM patients AS T1 INNER JOIN medications AS T2 ON T1.patient = T2.PATIENT WHERE T2.ENCOUNTER = '23c293ec-dbae-4a22-896e-f12cf3c8bac3'

question: List out 5 most common conditions for underweight patient.

SQL: SELECT T2.DESCRIPTION FROM conditions T2 JOIN (SELECT PATIENT FROM observations WHERE DESCRIPTION = 'Body Mass Index' AND VALUE = (SELECT MIN(VALUE) FROM observations WHERE DESCRIPTION = 'Body Mass Index')) T1 ON T1.PATIENT = T2.PATIENT GROUP BY T2.DESCRIPTION ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 5;

question: What is the care plan, procedure, medication and the patient's full name for encounter 6f2e3935-b203-493e-a9c0-f23e847b9798?

SQL: SELECT T3.DESCRIPTION AS care_plan, T4.DESCRIPTION AS procedure, T5.DESCRIPTION AS medication, T2.first || ' ' || T2.last AS full_name FROM encounters T1 JOIN careplans T3 ON T1.ID = T3.ENCOUNTER JOIN procedures T4 ON T1.ID = T4.ENCOUNTER JOIN medications T5 ON T1.ID = T5.ENCOUNTER JOIN patients T2 ON T1.PATIENT = T2.patient WHERE T1.ID = '6f2e3935-b203-493e-a9c0-f23e847b9798'

question: How many male patients are diagnosed with hypertension as compared to female patients?
evidence: male refers to gender = 'M'; diagnosed with hypertension refers to conditions.DESCRIPTION = 'Hypertension'; female refers to gender = 'F'; number of male patients with hypertension = count(patient WHERE gender = 'M' AND conditions.DESCRIPTION = 'Hypertension'); number of female patients with hypertension = count(patient WHERE gender = 'F' AND conditions.DESCRIPTION = 'Hypertension');
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T2.gender = 'M' THEN T2.patient END) AS Male , COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T2.gender = 'F' THEN T2.patient END) AS Female FROM conditions AS T1 INNER JOIN patients AS T2 ON T1.PATIENT = T2.patient WHERE T1.DESCRIPTION = 'Hypertension'
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN gender = 'M' THEN patients.patient END) AS Male_Patients, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN gender = 'F' THEN patients.patient END) AS Female_Patients FROM patients JOIN conditions ON patients.patient = conditions.PATIENT WHERE DESCRIPTION = 'Hypertension';

question: What is the average body mass index for patients with higher total cholesterol?
evidence: average body mass index = DIVIDE(SUM(observations.VALUE), COUNT(PATIENT) WHERE observations.DESCRIPTION = 'Body Mass Index'); body mass index refers to observations.DESCRIPTION = 'Body Mass Index'; higher total cholesterol refers to observations.DESCRIPTION = 'Total Cholesterol' and observations.VALUE > = 200;
SQL: SELECT SUM(T1.VALUE) / COUNT(T1.PATIENT) FROM observations AS T1 INNER JOIN ( SELECT DISTINCT PATIENT FROM observations WHERE DESCRIPTION = 'Total Cholesterol' AND VALUE > 200 ) AS T2 ON T1.PATIENT = T2.PATIENT WHERE T1.DESCRIPTION = 'Body Mass Index'
gold: SELECT AVG(BMI.VALUE) AS average_bmi FROM observations AS BMI WHERE BMI.PATIENT IN (SELECT DISTINCT TC.PATIENT FROM observations AS TC WHERE TC.DESCRIPTION = 'Total Cholesterol' AND TC.VALUE >= 200) AND BMI.DESCRIPTION = 'Body Mass Index';

question: What is the difference between average glucose reading for patients in the 20s and 50s?
evidence: sum(case when t2.DATE-t1.birthdate between 20 and 29 then t2.VALUE else 0 end)/count(case when t2.DATE-t1.birthdate between 20 and 29 then t2.PATIENT else null end)-sum(case when t2.DATE-t1.birthdate between 50 and 59 then t2.VALUE else 0 end)/count(case when t2.DATE-t1.birthdate between 50 and 59 then t2.PATIENT else null end)
SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN ROUND((strftime('%J', T2.DATE) - strftime('%J', T1.birthdate)) / 365) BETWEEN 20 AND 30 THEN T2.VALUE ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(CASE WHEN ROUND((strftime('%J', T2.DATE) - strftime('%J', T1.birthdate)) / 365) BETWEEN 20 AND 30 THEN T2.PATIENT END) - SUM(CASE WHEN ROUND((strftime('%J', T2.DATE) - strftime('%J', T1.birthdate)) / 365) BETWEEN 50 AND 60 THEN T2.VALUE ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(CASE WHEN ROUND((strftime('%J', T2.DATE) - strftime('%J', T1.birthdate)) / 365) BETWEEN 50 AND 60 THEN T2.PATIENT END) AS difference FROM patients AS T1 INNER JOIN observations AS T2 ON T1.patient = T2.PATIENT WHERE T2.DESCRIPTION = 'Glucose'
gold: SELECT (SUM(CASE WHEN (strftime('%Y', o.DATE) - strftime('%Y', p.birthdate)) BETWEEN 20 AND 29 THEN o.VALUE ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(CASE WHEN (strftime('%Y', o.DATE) - strftime('%Y', p.birthdate)) BETWEEN 20 AND 29 THEN o.PATIENT ELSE NULL END)) - (SUM(CASE WHEN (strftime('%Y', o.DATE) - strftime('%Y', p.birthdate)) BETWEEN 50 AND 59 THEN o.VALUE ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(CASE WHEN (strftime('%Y', o.DATE) - strftime('%Y', p.birthdate)) BETWEEN 50 AND 59 THEN o.PATIENT ELSE NULL END)) AS difference FROM observations o JOIN patients p ON o.PATIENT = p.patient WHERE o.DESCRIPTION = 'glucose'

question: What is the percentage of the most common conditions for patients age 60 and above?
evidence: most common condition refers to MAX(COUNT(conditions.DESCRIPTION)); age 60 and above refers to SUBTRACT(conditions.START, birthdate) > 60; percentage = MULTIPLY(DIVIDE(SUM(patients.patient WHERE MAX(COUNT(conditions.DESCRIPTION)) AND SUBTRACT(conditions.START, birthdate) > 60))), COUNT(patients.patient WHERE MAX(COUNT(conditions.DESCRIPTION)), 10);
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T5.DESCRIPTION = T3.DESCRIPTION THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T3.patient) FROM ( SELECT T2.DESCRIPTION, T1.patient FROM patients AS T1 INNER JOIN conditions AS T2 ON T1.patient = T2.PATIENT WHERE ROUND((strftime('%J', T2.START) - strftime('%J', T1.birthdate)) / 365) > 60 GROUP BY T2.DESCRIPTION ORDER BY COUNT(T2.DESCRIPTION) DESC LIMIT 1 ) AS T3 INNER JOIN patients AS T4 ON T3.patient = T4.patient INNER JOIN conditions AS T5 ON T4.patient = T5.PATIENT WHERE ROUND((strftime('%J', T5.START) - strftime('%J', T4.birthdate)) / 365) > 60
gold: SELECT (CAST(MAX(cnt) AS FLOAT) / CAST(SUM(cnt) AS FLOAT)) * 100 AS percentage FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM conditions T1 JOIN patients T2 ON T1.PATIENT = T2.patient WHERE (strftime('%Y', T1.START) - strftime('%Y', T2.birthdate)) >= 60 GROUP BY T1.DESCRIPTION) T3;

question: Which two products has the highest and lowest expected profits? Determine the total price for each product in terms of the largest quantity that was ordered.

question: List the restaurant's ID that has a review greater than the 70% of average review of all American restaurants with street number greater than 2000.

question: Among the restaurants located on the street number ranges from 1000 to 2000, what is the percentage of Afghani restaurants are there?

SQL: SELECT T2.Match_Date, T4.Role_Desc FROM Player T1 JOIN Player_Match T3 ON T1.Player_Id = T3.Player_Id JOIN Match T2 ON T3.Match_Id = T2.Match_Id JOIN Rolee T4 ON T3.Role_Id = T4.Role_Id WHERE T1.DOB = (SELECT MAX(DOB) FROM Player) AND T2.Match_Date = (SELECT MIN(Match_Date) FROM Match JOIN Player_Match ON Match.Match_Id = Player_Match.Match_Id WHERE Player_Match.Player_Id = T1.Player_Id);
gold: SELECT T2.Match_Date, T4.Role_Desc FROM Player T1 JOIN Player_Match T3 ON T1.Player_Id = T3.Player_Id JOIN Match T2 ON T3.Match_Id = T2.Match_Id JOIN Rolee T4 ON T3.Role_Id = T4.Role_Id WHERE T1.DOB = (SELECT MAX(DOB) FROM Player) AND T2.Match_Date = (SELECT MIN(Match_Date) FROM Match JOIN Player_Match ON Match.Match_Id = Player_Match.Match_Id WHERE Player_Match.Player_Id = T1.Player_Id);

question: From 2011 to 2012, how many Australian players became the "Man of the Match"?

gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.Man_of_the_Match) FROM Match T1, Player T2, Country T3 WHERE T1.Man_of_the_Match = T2.Player_Id AND T2.Country_Name = T3.Country_Id AND T1.Match_Date >= '2011-01-01' AND T1.Match_Date <= '2012-12-31' AND T3.Country_Name = 'Australia';

question: Calculate the run rate at the end of 17 overs of the match ID 335987 on 4/18/2008.
evidence: 4/18/2008 refers to Match_Date = 4/18/2008; end of 17 overs refers to count(Toss_Name = 'field' ) = 17; run rate = divide(sum(Runs_Scored) when Toss_Name = 'bat', sum(Over_Id) when Toss_Name = 'field')
SQL: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T1.Toss_Name = 'bat' THEN T3.Runs_Scored ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN T1.Toss_Name = 'field' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM Toss_Decision AS T1 INNER JOIN Match AS T2 ON T1.Toss_Id = T2.Toss_Decide INNER JOIN Batsman_Scored AS T3 ON T2.Match_Id = T3.Match_Id WHERE T2.Match_Id = 335987 AND T2.Match_Date = '2008-04-18' GROUP BY T3.Over_Id HAVING COUNT(T1.Toss_Name = 'field') = 17
gold: SELECT SUM(BS.Runs_Scored) / 17.0 AS Run_Rate FROM Match M JOIN Batsman_Scored BS ON M.Match_Id = BS.Match_Id WHERE M.Match_Date = '2008-04-18' AND M.Match_Id = 335987 AND BS.Over_Id <= 17;

question: Compute the run rate at the end of 16 overs of the match ID 335999. Please include the name of the "Man of_the Match".
evidence: end of 16 overs refers to count(Toss_Name = 'field' ) = 16; run rate = divide(count(Runs_Scored) when Toss_Name = 'bat', sum(Over_Id)when Toss_Name = 'field'); name refers to Player_Name
SQL: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T1.Toss_Name = 'bat' THEN T3.Runs_Scored ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN T1.Toss_Name = 'field' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM Toss_Decision AS T1 INNER JOIN Match AS T2 ON T1.Toss_Id = T2.Toss_Decide INNER JOIN Batsman_Scored AS T3 ON T2.Match_Id = T3.Match_Id WHERE T2.Match_Id = 335987 AND T2.Match_Date = '2008-04-18' GROUP BY T3.Over_Id HAVING COUNT(T1.Toss_Name = 'field') = 16
gold: SELECT SUM(T1.Runs_Scored)/16.0 AS Run_Rate, T3.Player_Name FROM Batsman_Scored T1 JOIN Match T2 ON T1.Match_Id = T2.Match_Id JOIN Player T3 ON T2.Man_of_the_Match = T3.Player_Id WHERE T1.Match_Id = 335999 AND T1.Over_Id <= 16 GROUP BY T1.Match_Id

SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T2.SeriesCode)  FROM Footnotes AS T1 INNER JOIN Series AS T2 ON T1.Seriescode = T2.SeriesCode WHERE T1.Year IN ('YR2001', 'YR2002', 'YR2003') AND T2.Periodicity = 'Annual' AND T2.AggregationMethod = 'Sum'

question: What is the ratio between country with the highest number of infant deaths in 1971 and the lowest number of infant deaths in 1971? List the country with the highest number of infant deaths in 1971 and the lowest number of infant deaths in 1971.

SQL: SELECT CAST(MAX(value) AS REAL) / MIN(value) FROM indicators WHERE indicatorname = 'Number of infant deaths' AND year = '1971' UNION ALL SELECT countryname FROM ( SELECT countryname, MAX(value) FROM indicators WHERE indicatorname = 'Number of infant deaths' AND year = '1971' ) UNION SELECT countryname FROM ( SELECT countryname, MIN(value) FROM indicators WHERE indicatorname = 'Number of infant deaths' AND year = '1971' )

SQL: SELECT DISTINCT T2.Sales / (1 - T2.Discount) FROM people AS T1 INNER JOIN central_superstore AS T2 ON T1.`Customer ID` = T2.`Customer ID` INNER JOIN product AS T3 ON T3.`Product ID` = T2.`Product ID` WHERE T1.`Customer Name` = 'Aimee Bixby' AND T3.`Product Name` = 'Xerox 1952' AND T2.`Order Date` = '2014-09-10'
gold: SELECT Sales / (1 - Discount) AS Original_Price FROM (SELECT * FROM central_superstore UNION SELECT * FROM east_superstore UNION SELECT * FROM south_superstore UNION SELECT * FROM west_superstore) WHERE `Order Date` = '2014-09-10' AND `Customer ID` = (SELECT `Customer ID` FROM people WHERE `Customer Name` = 'Aimee Bixby') AND `Product ID` = (SELECT `Product ID` FROM product WHERE `Product Name` = 'Xerox 1952');

question: What was the total cost of Xerox 1952 ordered by Aimee Bixby on 2014/9/10?
evidence: Xerox 1952 is a "Product Name"; ordered by Aimee Bixby refers to "Customer Name" = 'Aimee Bixby'; on 2014/9/10 refers to "Order Date" = date('2014-09-10'); total cost refers to SUTRACT(MULTIPLY(DIVIDE(Sales, SUTRACT(1, discount)), Quantity), Profit)
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT (T2.Sales / (1 - T2.discount)) * T2.Quantity - Profit FROM people AS T1 INNER JOIN central_superstore AS T2 ON T1.`Customer ID` = T2.`Customer ID` INNER JOIN product AS T3 ON T3.`Product ID` = T2.`Product ID` WHERE T1.`Customer Name` = 'Aimee Bixby' AND T3.`Product Name` = 'Xerox 1952' AND T2.`Order Date` = '2014-09-10'
gold: SELECT (SUM(Sales / (1 - Discount) * Quantity) - SUM(Profit)) AS Total_Cost FROM central_superstore WHERE `Order Date` = '2014-09-10' AND `Customer ID` IN (SELECT `Customer ID` FROM people WHERE `Customer Name` = 'Aimee Bixby') AND `Product ID` IN (SELECT `Product ID` FROM product WHERE `Product Name` = 'Xerox 1952')

SQL: SELECT DISTINCT T2.`Product Name`, T1.`Ship Mode` FROM west_superstore AS T1 INNER JOIN product AS T2 ON T1.`Product ID` = T2.`Product ID` WHERE T2.Region = 'West' ORDER BY T1.`Ship Date` - T1.`Order Date` LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T2."Product Name", T1."Ship Mode" FROM west_superstore T1 JOIN product T2 ON T1."Product ID" = T2."Product ID" AND T1.Region = T2.Region WHERE (JULIANDAY(T1."Ship Date") - JULIANDAY(T1."Order Date")) = (SELECT MIN(JULIANDAY("Ship Date") - JULIANDAY("Order Date")) FROM west_superstore);

question: What is the name of the corporate customer from Rhode Island who had the highest number of orders in 2016 from the east superstore?
evidence: corporate customer refers to Segment = 'Corporate'; Rhode Island refers to State = 'Rhode Island'; in 2016 refers to "Order Date" BETWEEN '2016-01-01' AND '2016-12-31'; east superstore refers to Region = 'East'; highest number of orders refers to max(order_number); name of corporate customer refers to "Customer Name"
SQL: SELECT T1."Customer Name" FROM people T1 JOIN east_superstore T2 ON T1."Customer ID" = T2."Customer ID" AND T1.Region = T2.Region WHERE T1.Segment = 'Corporate' AND T1.State = 'Rhode Island' AND T2."Order Date" BETWEEN '2016-01-01' AND '2016-12-31' AND T2.Region = 'East' GROUP BY T1."Customer ID" ORDER BY COUNT(T2."Order ID") DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T1."Customer Name" FROM people T1 INNER JOIN east_superstore T2 ON T1."Customer ID" = T2."Customer ID" AND T1.Region = T2.Region WHERE T1.Segment = 'Corporate' AND T1.State = 'Rhode Island' AND T2."Order Date" >= '2016-01-01' AND T2."Order Date" <= '2016-12-31' AND T2.Region = 'East' GROUP BY T1."Customer ID" HAVING COUNT(T2."Order ID") = (SELECT MAX(order_count) FROM (SELECT COUNT(T2."Order ID") AS order_count FROM east_superstore T2 JOIN people T1 ON T1."Customer ID" = T2."Customer ID" AND T1.Region = T2.Region WHERE T1.Segment = 'Corporate' AND T1.State = 'Rhode Island' AND T2."Order Date" BETWEEN '2016-01-01' AND '2016-12-31' AND T2.Region = 'East' GROUP BY T1."Customer ID"))

SQL: SELECT STRFTIME('%Y', date) FROM incidents WHERE subject_weapon = 'Handgun' GROUP BY STRFTIME('%Y', date) ORDER BY COUNT(case_number) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT strftime('%Y', date) AS year FROM incidents WHERE subject_weapon = 'Handgun' GROUP BY year ORDER BY COUNT(case_number) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: Among the cases dismissed by the grand jury disposition, what percentage of cases is where the subject is injured?
evidence: dismissed by the grand jury disposition refers to grand_jury_disposition = 'No Bill'; the subject is injured refers to subject_statuses = 'injured'; percentage = divide(count(incidents where subject_statuses = 'injured'), count(incidents)) where grand_jury_disposition = 'No Bill' * 100%
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(subject_statuses = 'Injured') AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(case_number) FROM incidents WHERE grand_jury_disposition = 'No Bill'
gold: SELECT (COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE subject_statuses = 'injured') * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage FROM incidents WHERE subject_statuses LIKE '%No Bill%'

question: Did the number of cases with Vehicle as subject weapon increase or decrease from year 2007 to 2008. State the difference.
evidence: number of cases refers to count(case_number); with Vehicle as subject weapon refers to subject_weapon = 'Vehicle'; year 2007 refers to date between '2007-01-01' and '2007-12-31'; year 2008 refers to date between '2008-01-01' and '2008-12-31'
SQL: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incidents WHERE subject_weapon = 'Vehicle' AND date LIKE '2008%') - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incidents WHERE subject_weapon = 'Vehicle' AND date LIKE '2007%') AS difference;
gold: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incidents WHERE subject_weapon = 'Vehicle' AND date LIKE '2008%') - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incidents WHERE subject_weapon = 'Vehicle' AND date LIKE '2007%') AS difference;

question: Among the 'Handgun' weapon used by subject, how many percent were 'Shoot and Miss'?
evidence: 'Handgun' weapon refers to subject_weapon = 'Handgun'; 'Shoot and Miss' refers to subject_statuses = 'Shoot and Miss'; percent = divide(count(incidents where subject_statuses = 'Shoot and Miss'), count(incidents)) where subject_weapon = 'Handgun' * 100%
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(subject_statuses = 'Shoot and Miss') AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(case_number) FROM incidents WHERE subject_weapon = 'Handgun'
gold: SELECT (COUNT(CASE WHEN subject_statuses = 'Shoot and Miss' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage FROM incidents WHERE subject_weapon = 'Handgun';

question: Who are the officers involved in cases that are voted as 'No Bill'. List their last name and gender.

gold: SELECT O.last_name, O.gender FROM officers O INNER JOIN incidents I ON O.case_number = I.case_number;

question: Which are the cases where the subject are female. List the case number, subject status and weapon.

question: What is the percentage of subject who are female used the Vehicle as weapon?
evidence: female refers to gender = 'F'; use Vehicle as weapon refers to subject_weapon = 'Vehicle'; percentage = divide(count(case_number where subject_weapon = 'Vehicle'), count(case_number)) where gender = 'F' * 100%

question: From the 'Injured' statuses of the subject, what is the ratio of weapons used are knife against handgun?

SQL: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incidents WHERE subject_statuses LIKE '%Injured%' AND subject_weapon = 'Knife') * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incidents WHERE subject_statuses LIKE '%Injured%' AND subject_weapon = 'Handgun') AS ratio FROM incidents WHERE subject_statuses LIKE '%Injured%' LIMIT 1;
gold: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incidents WHERE subject_statuses LIKE '%Injured%' AND subject_weapon = 'Knife') * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incidents WHERE subject_statuses LIKE '%Injured%' AND subject_weapon = 'Handgun') AS ratio FROM incidents WHERE subject_statuses LIKE '%Injured%' LIMIT 1;

question: Among the genes with nucleic acid metabolism defects, how many of them can be found in the vacuole?

gold: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Genes WHERE Function = 'nucleic acid metabolism defects' AND Localization = 'vacuole';

question: Please list the location of the genes that have the most chromosomes.

gold: SELECT Localization FROM Genes WHERE Chromosome = (SELECT Chromosome FROM Genes GROUP BY Chromosome ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1)

question: Among the pairs of genes that are both located in the nucleus, what is the highest expression correlation score?
SQL: SELECT T2.Expression_Corr FROM Genes AS T1 INNER JOIN Interactions AS T2 ON T1.GeneID = T2.GeneID1 INNER JOIN Genes AS T3 ON T3.GeneID = T2.GeneID2 WHERE T1.Localization = 'nucleus' AND T3.Localization = 'nucleus' ORDER BY T2.Expression_Corr DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT MAX(I.Expression_Corr) FROM Interactions I JOIN Classification C1 ON I.GeneID1 = C1.GeneID JOIN Classification C2 ON I.GeneID2 = C2.GeneID WHERE C1.Localization = 'nucleus' AND C2.Localization = 'nucleus';

question: What are the functions of the pair of genes that have the lowest expression correlation score?a
SQL: SELECT T1.Function FROM Genes AS T1 INNER JOIN Interactions AS T2 ON T1.GeneID = T2.GeneID1 ORDER BY T2.Expression_Corr ASC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T2.Function, T3.Function FROM Interactions T1 JOIN Genes T2 ON T1.GeneID1 = T2.GeneID JOIN Genes T3 ON T1.GeneID2 = T3.GeneID WHERE T1.Expression_Corr = (SELECT MIN(Expression_Corr) FROM Interactions);

question: Among the pairs of genes that are not from the class of motorproteins, how many of them are negatively correlated?
evidence: If Expression_Corr < 0, it means the negatively correlated
SQL: WITH NonMotorProteins AS (SELECT GeneID FROM Genes WHERE Class != 'Motorproteins') SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Interactions WHERE Expression_Corr < 0 AND GeneID1 IN (SELECT GeneID FROM NonMotorProteins) AND GeneID2 IN (SELECT GeneID FROM NonMotorProteins);
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Interactions AS I WHERE I.Expression_Corr < 0 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Genes AS G WHERE G.GeneID = I.GeneID1 AND G.Class = 'Motorproteins') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Genes AS G WHERE G.GeneID = I.GeneID2 AND G.Class = 'Motorproteins');

question: For the pairs of genes with one having 8 chromosomes and the other having 6 chromosomes, what is the highest expression correlation score?
SQL: SELECT T2.Expression_Corr FROM Genes AS T1 INNER JOIN Interactions AS T2 ON T1.GeneID = T2.GeneID1 WHERE T1.Chromosome = 6 OR T1.Chromosome = 8 ORDER BY T2.Expression_Corr DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT MAX(I.Expression_Corr) FROM Interactions I JOIN Genes G1 ON I.GeneID1 = G1.GeneID JOIN Genes G2 ON I.GeneID2 = G2.GeneID WHERE (G1.Chromosome = 8 AND G2.Chromosome = 6) OR (G1.Chromosome = 6 AND G2.Chromosome = 8);

question: For the non-essential genes whose functions are transcription, how many of them are not located in the cytoplasm?

gold: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Genes WHERE Essential = 'Non-Essential' AND Function LIKE 'transcription' AND NOT Localization = 'cytoplasm';

question: How many pairs of positively correlated genes are both non-essential?
evidence: If Expression_Corr > 0, it means the expression correlation is positive
SQL: SELECT COUNT(T2.GeneID2) FROM Genes AS T1 INNER JOIN Interactions AS T2 ON T1.GeneID = T2.GeneID1 WHERE T2.Expression_Corr > 0 AND T1.Essential = 'Non-Essential'
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Interactions I WHERE I.Expression_Corr > 0 AND (SELECT Essential FROM Genes WHERE GeneID = I.GeneID1) = 'Non-Essential' AND (SELECT Essential FROM Genes WHERE GeneID = I.GeneID2) = 'Non-Essential';

question: If a pair of genes is positively correlated, what is the possibility of it being composed of two genes both with over 10 chromosomes?
evidence: Positively correlated means Expression_Corr > 0; Possibility = count(the pairs of genes with both chromosomes over 20) / count(pairs of genes that are positively correlated)
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Interactions WHERE Expression_Corr > 0) FROM Interactions I JOIN Genes G1 ON I.GeneID1 = G1.GeneID JOIN Genes G2 ON I.GeneID2 = G2.GeneID WHERE I.Expression_Corr > 0 AND G1.Chromosome > 10 AND G2.Chromosome > 10;
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Interactions WHERE Expression_Corr > 0) FROM Interactions I JOIN Genes G1 ON I.GeneID1 = G1.GeneID JOIN Genes G2 ON I.GeneID2 = G2.GeneID WHERE I.Expression_Corr > 0 AND G1.Chromosome > 10 AND G2.Chromosome > 10;

question: For the pairs of genes both from the class ATPases, what is the average expression correlation score?
SQL: SELECT AVG(I.Expression_Corr) FROM Interactions I JOIN Genes G1 ON I.GeneID1 = G1.GeneID JOIN Genes G2 ON I.GeneID2 = G2.GeneID WHERE G1.Class = 'ATPases' AND G2.Class = 'ATPases';
gold: SELECT AVG(Expression_Corr) FROM Interactions WHERE GeneID1 IN (SELECT GeneID FROM Genes WHERE Class = 'ATPases') AND GeneID2 IN (SELECT GeneID FROM Genes WHERE Class = 'ATPases');

question: Lists all genes by identifier number located in the cytoplasm and whose function is metabolism.

gold: SELECT GeneID FROM Genes WHERE Localization LIKE 'cytoplasm' AND Function LIKE 'metabolism';

question: How many different genes do we have if we add those located in the plasma and in the nucleus?
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT GeneID) FROM Classification WHERE Localization LIKE 'plasma' OR Localization LIKE 'nucleus';
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT GeneID) FROM Classification WHERE Localization IN ('plasma', 'nucleus');

question: What kind of expression correlation occurs in physical type interacting gene pairs and what percentage of these are negatively correlated?
evidence: If the Expression_Corr value is negative then it's negatively correlated. Percentage of Negative Correlation = count(negative Expression_Corr physical type) / count(Expression_Corr physical type) * 100%
SQL: SELECT Expression_Corr FROM Interactions WHERE Type = 'Physical' UNION ALL SELECT CAST(SUM(Expression_Corr < 0) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(*) FROM Interactions WHERE Type = 'Physical'
gold: SELECT COUNT(CASE WHEN Expression_Corr < 0 THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) AS Percentage_Negatively_Correlated FROM Interactions WHERE Type = 'Physical';

question: What percentage of genes located in the cytoskeleton are of unknown class? And of these, how many are not conditional phenotypes?
evidence: Percentage = count(genes located in the cytoskeleton unknown class) / count(genes located in the cytoskeleton) * 100%
SQL: SELECT SUM(Localization = 'cytoskeleton' AND Phenotype = 'Conditional phenotypes') , CAST(SUM(Localization = 'cytoskeleton') AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(GeneID) FROM Genes;
gold: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Genes WHERE Localization = 'cytoskeleton' AND Class = 'Unknown') * 100.0 / COUNT(*) AS percentage, COUNT(CASE WHEN Class = 'Unknown' AND Phenotype != '?' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS non_conditional_count FROM Genes WHERE Localization = 'cytoskeleton';

question: What type of interactions occurs in genes whose function is cellular transport and transport medicine and are classified as non-essential?
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT T2.Type FROM Genes T1 JOIN Interactions T2 ON T1.GeneID = T2.GeneID1 WHERE T1.Essential = 'Non-Essential' AND T1.Function = 'cellular transport and transport medicine';
gold: SELECT DISTINCT T2.Type FROM Genes T1 JOIN Interactions T2 ON T1.GeneID = T2.GeneID1 WHERE T1.Essential = 'Non-Essential' AND T1.Function = 'cellular transport and transport medicine';

question: List all genes whose interaction is with genes located in the nucleus in which it is positively correlated.

gold: SELECT DISTINCT T1.GeneID1 FROM Interactions T1 JOIN Classification T2 ON T1.GeneID2 = T2.GeneID WHERE T2.Localization = 'nucleus' AND T1.Expression_Corr > 0;

question: Taking all the essential genes of the transcription factors class located in the nucleus as a reference, how many of them carry out a genetic-type interaction with another gene? List them.
SQL: SELECT T2.GeneID1 FROM Genes AS T1 INNER JOIN Interactions AS T2 ON T1.GeneID = T2.GeneID1 WHERE T1.Localization = 'nucleus' AND T1.Class = 'Transcription factors' AND T1.Essential = 'Essential' AND T2.Expression_Corr != 0
gold: SELECT DISTINCT T1.GeneID FROM Genes T1 JOIN Interactions T2 ON T1.GeneID = T2.GeneID1 WHERE T1.Essential = 'Essential' AND T1.Class = 'Transcription factors' AND T1.Localization = 'nucleus' AND T2.Type = 'Genetic'

question: Of all the nonessential genes that are not of the motorprotein class and whose phenotype is cell cycle defects, how many do not have a physical type of interaction?
SQL: SELECT COUNT(T1.GeneID) FROM Genes AS T1 INNER JOIN Interactions AS T2 ON T1.GeneID = T2.GeneID1 WHERE T2.Type != 'Physical' AND T1.Phenotype = 'Cell cycle defects' AND T1.Class != 'Motorproteins' AND T1.Essential = 'Non-Essential'
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT GeneID) FROM Genes WHERE Essential = 'Non-Essential' AND Class <> 'Motorproteins' AND Phenotype = 'cell cycle defects' AND GeneID NOT IN (SELECT GeneID1 FROM Interactions WHERE Type = 'Physical');

question: Of the genes whose phenotype and motif are nucleic acid metabolism defects, PS00107, what percentage perform positive interaction with another gene?
evidence: Percentage of no interaction = [count(nucleic acid metabolism, PS00107, no interaction) / count(nucleic acid metabolism, PS00107) * 100%
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(IIF(T2.Expression_Corr > 0, 1, 0)) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T2.GeneID1) FROM Genes AS T1 INNER JOIN Interactions AS T2 ON T1.GeneID = T2.GeneID1 WHERE T1.Phenotype = 'Nucleic acid metabolism defects' AND T1.Motif = 'PS00107'

question: Which negatively correlated, genetically interacting genes are non-essential? What percentage do they represent with respect to those that are essential?

SQL: SELECT CAST(COUNT(T1.GeneID) AS REAL) * 100 / ( SELECT COUNT(T1.GeneID) FROM Genes AS T1 INNER JOIN Interactions AS T2 ON T1.GeneID = T2.GeneID1 WHERE T2.Expression_Corr < 0 ) FROM Genes AS T1 INNER JOIN Interactions AS T2 ON T1.GeneID = T2.GeneID1 WHERE T2.Expression_Corr < 0 AND T1.Essential = 'Non-Essential'
gold: SELECT (CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Interactions I NATURAL JOIN Genes G WHERE I.Expression_Corr < 0 AND I.Type = 'Genetic' AND G.Essential = 'Non-Essential') * 100) AS Percentage FROM Interactions I NATURAL JOIN Genes G WHERE I.Expression_Corr < 0 AND I.Type = 'Genetic' AND G.Essential = 'Essential';

SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.Sentiment = 'Positive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN T2.Sentiment = 'Negative' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), T1.`Current Ver` FROM playstore AS T1 INNER JOIN user_reviews AS T2 ON T1.App = T2.App WHERE T1.App = 'Fate/Grand Order (English)' AND T1.`Current Ver` = '1.18.0'
gold: SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN Sentiment = 'Positive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / SUM(CASE WHEN Sentiment = 'Negative' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Percentage_Ratio FROM user_reviews WHERE App = 'Fate/Grand Order (English)';

question: Indicate the number of installs and include the percentage of positive sentiments of FREEDOME VPN Unlimited anonymous Wifi Security.
evidence: FREEDOME VPN Unlimited anonymous Wifi Security is the App; percentage = MULTIPLY(DIVIDE((SUM(Sentiment = 'Positive')), (COUNT(*))), 100)
SQL: SELECT T1.Installs, (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.Sentiment = 'Positive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS FLOAT) / COUNT(T2.Sentiment) * 100) AS PositiveSentimentPercentage FROM playstore T1 JOIN user_reviews T2 ON T1.App = T2.App WHERE T1.App = 'FREEDOME VPN Unlimited anonymous Wifi Security' GROUP BY T1.Installs;
gold: SELECT Installs, (100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN Sentiment = 'Positive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*)) AS PositiveSentimentPercentage FROM playstore JOIN user_reviews ON playstore.App = user_reviews.App WHERE playstore.App = 'FREEDOME VPN Unlimited anonymous Wifi Security' GROUP BY Installs;

question: For the Honkai Impact 3rd App, what is the highest sentiment polarity score and what genre does it belong to?

question: What is the rating of Dragon Ball Legends and how many users dislike this App?

gold: SELECT p.Rating, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_reviews WHERE App = 'Dragon Ball Legends' AND Sentiment_Polarity < -0.5) AS Dislike_Count FROM playstore p WHERE p.App = 'Dragon Ball Legends'

question: What is the average rating of Apps falling under the racing genre and what is the percentage ratio of positive sentiment reviews?

question: Describe the customer names and lasting delivery periods for the product of "Bedroom Furniture" by wholesale channel in 2019.

SQL: SELECT T3."Customer Names", julianday(T1.DeliveryDate) - julianday(T1.OrderDate) AS DeliveryPeriod FROM 'Sales Orders' AS T1 INNER JOIN Products AS T2 ON T1._ProductID = T2.ProductID INNER JOIN Customers AS T3 ON T1._CustomerID = T3.CustomerID WHERE T1."Sales Channel" = 'Wholesale' AND T2."Product Name" = 'Bedroom Furniture' AND SUBSTR(T1.OrderDate, 7, 2) = '19';
gold: SELECT T3."Customer Names", julianday(T1.DeliveryDate) - julianday(T1.OrderDate) AS DeliveryPeriod FROM 'Sales Orders' AS T1 INNER JOIN Products AS T2 ON T1._ProductID = T2.ProductID INNER JOIN Customers AS T3 ON T1._CustomerID = T3.CustomerID WHERE T1."Sales Channel" = 'Wholesale' AND T2."Product Name" = 'Bedroom Furniture' AND SUBSTR(T1.OrderDate, 7, 2) = '19';

SQL: SELECT `Sales Channel` FROM `Sales Orders` WHERE OrderDate LIKE '1/%/20' GROUP BY `Sales Channel` ORDER BY COUNT(`Sales Channel`) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT "Sales Channel" FROM "Sales Orders" WHERE SUBSTR(OrderDate, -2) = '20' AND SUBSTR(OrderDate, 1, INSTR(OrderDate, '/') - 1) = '1' GROUP BY "Sales Channel" ORDER BY COUNT(OrderNumber) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: Identify the store location and sales team who processed the sales order 'SO - 0001004'.

SQL: SELECT T3.`Sales Team`, T1.`City Name` FROM `Store Locations` AS T1 INNER JOIN `Sales Orders` AS T2 ON T2._StoreID = T1.StoreID INNER JOIN `Sales Team` AS T3 ON T3.SalesTeamID = T2._SalesTeamID WHERE T2.OrderNumber = 'SO - 0001004'
gold: SELECT T2."City Name", T3."Sales Team" FROM "Sales Orders" T1 JOIN "Store Locations" T2 ON T1._StoreID = T2.StoreID JOIN "Sales Team" T3 ON T1._SalesTeamID = T3.SalesTeamID WHERE T1.OrderNumber = 'SO - 0001004';

question: What is the most consecutive games tied by Ebbsfleet as an away team in the 2008 season?

SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM matchs WHERE season = 2008 AND AwayTeam = 'Ebbsfleet' AND FTR = 'D'
gold: SELECT MAX(consecutive) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) as consecutive FROM (SELECT Date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY Date) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY FTR ORDER BY Date) as grp FROM matchs WHERE AwayTeam = 'Ebbsfleet' AND season = 2008 AND FTR = 'D') GROUP BY grp);

question: Of all the divisions in the world, what percentage of them belong to England?
evidence: DIVIDE(COUNT(division where country = 'England'), COUNT(division)) as percentage;
SQL: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN country = 'England' THEN division ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(division) FROM divisions
gold: SELECT (COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE country = 'England') * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage FROM divisions;

question: What percentage of games won, games lost and games drawn does Cittadella have as a home team in total?
evidence: Percentage of games won = DIVIDE(COUNT(FTR = 'H' where HomeTeam = 'Cittadella'), COUNT(Div where HomeTeam = 'Cittadella')) as percentage; Percentage of games lost = DIVIDE(COUNT(FTR = 'A' where HomeTeam = 'Cittadella')), COUNT(Div where HomeTeam = 'Cittadella') as percentage; percentage of games drawn = DIVIDE(SUM(FTR = 'D'where HomeTeam = 'Cittadella'), COUNT(Div where HomeTeam = 'Cittadella')) as percentage;
SQL: SELECT (COUNT(CASE WHEN FTR = 'H' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage_won, (COUNT(CASE WHEN FTR = 'A' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage_lost, (COUNT(CASE WHEN FTR = 'D' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage_drawn FROM matchs WHERE HomeTeam = 'Cittadella';
gold: SELECT (COUNT(CASE WHEN FTR = 'H' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage_won, (COUNT(CASE WHEN FTR = 'A' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage_lost, (COUNT(CASE WHEN FTR = 'D' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage_drawn FROM matchs WHERE HomeTeam = 'Cittadella';

question: From the Spanish LaLiga division in the 2017 season, which team won the most times as a local team and by what percentage?

SQL: SELECT T1.HomeTeam HWHT , CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T1.FTR = 'H' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(HomeTeam) FROM matchs AS T1 INNER JOIN divisions AS T2 ON T1.Div = T2.division WHERE T2.name = 'LaLiga' AND T2.country = 'Spain' AND T1.season = 2017

question: How many teams that played in the 2012 season belong to any of the English divisions and what percentage play in each of the divisions?
evidence: matches = Div
SQL: SELECT ( SELECT COUNT(T1.Div) AS total FROM matchs T1 INNER JOIN divisions T2 ON T2.division = T1.Div WHERE T2.country = 'England' AND T1.season = 2012 ) AS num , CASE WHEN 1 THEN T.result END AS percentage FROM ( SELECT 100.0 * COUNT(T1.Div) / ( SELECT COUNT(T1.Div) FROM matchs T1 INNER JOIN divisions T2 ON T2.division = T1.Div WHERE T2.country = 'England' AND T1.season = 2012 ) AS result FROM matchs T1 INNER JOIN divisions T2 ON T2.division = T1.Div WHERE T2.country = 'England' AND T1.season = 2012 GROUP BY T2.division ) AS T
gold: SELECT T2.division, COUNT(DISTINCT T1.HomeTeam) AS TeamsCount, (COUNT(DISTINCT T1.HomeTeam) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT HomeTeam) FROM matchs WHERE season = 2012 AND Div IN (SELECT division FROM divisions WHERE country = 'England'))) AS Percentage FROM matchs T1 JOIN divisions T2 ON T1.Div = T2.division WHERE T1.season = 2012 AND T2.country = 'England' GROUP BY T2.division;

SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.HomeTeam) FROM matchs AS T1 INNER JOIN divisions AS T2 ON T1.Div = T2.division WHERE T2.name = 'Eredivisie' AND T1.season = 2008

question: What's the home win ratio of the Bundesliga division in 2021?
evidence: home win refers to FTR = 'H', where H stands for home victory; season = '2021'; Bundesliga is a name of division; DIVIDE(COUNT(Div where FTR = 'H, season = '2021' and name = 'Bundesliga'), COUNT(Div where season = '2021' and name = 'Bundesliga')) as percentage;
SQL: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T1.FTR = 'H' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.FTR) FROM matchs AS T1 INNER JOIN divisions AS T2 ON T1.Div = T2.division WHERE T1.season = 2021 AND T2.name = 'Bundesliga'
gold: SELECT (COUNT(*) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM matchs T1 JOIN divisions T2 ON T1.Div = T2.division WHERE T2.name = 'Bundesliga' AND T1.season = 2021)) AS home_win_ratio FROM matchs T1 JOIN divisions T2 ON T1.Div = T2.division WHERE T2.name = 'Bundesliga' AND T1.season = 2021 AND T1.FTR = 'H';

question: For all the games ended up with 1-1, what percentage of them are from Liga NOS division?
evidence: 1-1 is a score where FTHG = '1' and FTAG = '1'; Liga NOS is the name of division; DIVIDE(COUNT(Div where FTHG = '1', FTAG = '1', name = 'Liga NOS'), COUNT(Div where FTHG = '1' and FTAG = '1')) as percentage;
SQL: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.name = 'Liga NOS' THEN T1.Div ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.Div) FROM matchs AS T1 INNER JOIN divisions AS T2 ON T1.Div = T2.division WHERE T1.FTHG = 1 AND FTAG = 1
gold: SELECT (COUNT(*) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM matchs T1 INNER JOIN divisions T2 ON T1.Div = T2.division WHERE T1.FTHG = 1 AND T1.FTAG = 1)) AS percentage FROM matchs T1 INNER JOIN divisions T2 ON T1.Div = T2.division WHERE T1.FTHG = 1 AND T1.FTAG = 1 AND T2.name = 'Liga NOS';

question: How many home victories does the Bundesliga division have in more or less than the Premier League division in the 2021 season?
evidence: Bundesliga and the Premier League are names of division; home victories refer to FTR = 'H', where H stands for home victory; SUBTRACT(COUNT(FTR = 'H' where season = 2021, name = 'Bundesliga'), COUNT(FTR = 'H' where season = 2021, name = 'Premier League'));

question: What's the winning rate of Club Brugge in the 2021 Premier League?
evidence: Premier League is name of division; season = 2021; Club Brugge is name of team; Club Brugge wins implies HomeTeam = 'Club Brugge' and FTR = 'H' and AwayTeam = 'Club Brugge' and FTR = 'A'; DIVIDE(SUM(COUNT(FTR = 'H' where HomeTeam = 'Club Brugge', name = 'Premier League', season = 2021), COUNT(FTR = 'A'where AwayTeam = 'Club Brugge', name = 'Premier League', season = 2021)), COUNT(Div where name = 'Premier League', season = 2021));

gold: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN (HomeTeam = 'Club Brugge' AND FTR = 'H') OR (AwayTeam = 'Club Brugge' AND FTR = 'A') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS FLOAT) / COUNT(*) AS WinningRate FROM matchs JOIN divisions ON matchs.Div = divisions.division WHERE divisions.name = 'Premier League' AND matchs.season = 2021;

question: Who is the longest serving coach from year 1970 to 1980. List the coach ID and the team(s) he served.

SQL: SELECT coachID, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT tmID) AS teams FROM coaches WHERE year BETWEEN 1970 AND 1980 GROUP BY coachID ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT year) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: Which team(s) had 90% games won. List the coach ID for the team and year played.

question: What is the percentage of player who won "All-Defensive First Team" from 1980 - 2000 is from 'NY'.

question: What division did the team coached by the winner of the 1977 NBA Coach of the Year award play in in 1976?

SQL: SELECT divID FROM teams WHERE tmID IN (SELECT tmID FROM coaches WHERE coachID IN (SELECT coachID FROM awards_coaches WHERE year = 1977 AND award = 'NBA Coach of the Year') AND year = 1976)
gold: SELECT T3.divID FROM awards_coaches T1 JOIN coaches T2 ON T1.coachID = T2.coachID AND T1.year = T2.year + 1 JOIN teams T3 ON T2.tmID = T3.tmID AND T2.year = T3.year WHERE T1.year = 1977 AND T1.award = 'NBA Coach of the Year' AND T2.year = 1976

question: Which coach of the Chicago Bulls during the year 1981 won the NBA Coach of the Year award in the 1970s?

SQL: SELECT DISTINCT T2.coachID FROM coaches AS T1 INNER JOIN awards_coaches AS T2 ON T1.coachID = T2.coachID INNER JOIN teams AS T3 ON T3.tmID = T1.tmID WHERE T2.award = 'NBA Coach of the Year' AND T2.year BETWEEN 1970 AND 1979 AND T1.year = 1981 AND T3.name = 'Chicago Bulls'
gold: SELECT DISTINCT C.coachID FROM coaches C JOIN teams T ON C.tmID = T.tmID AND C.year = T.year JOIN awards_coaches A ON C.coachID = A.coachID WHERE T.name = 'Chicago Bulls' AND C.year = 1981 AND A.award = 'NBA Coach of the Year' AND A.year BETWEEN 1970 AND 1979;

question: In what year did the only team to beat the Houston in the final round of postseason series games earn its lowest ranking?

question: In which league did the player who weighs 40% less than the heaviest player and whose height is 80 inches play?
evidence: weigh 40% less than the heaviest player refers to weight = Multiply(Max (weight), 0.6); league refers to lgID

SQL: SELECT firstName FROM players WHERE playerID IN (SELECT playerID FROM players_teams WHERE lgID = 'NBL' AND PF IS NOT NULL GROUP BY playerID HAVING SUM(PF) = (SELECT MAX(totalPF) FROM (SELECT SUM(PF) AS totalPF FROM players_teams WHERE lgID = 'NBL' AND PF IS NOT NULL GROUP BY playerID)))
gold: SELECT firstName FROM players WHERE playerID IN (SELECT playerID FROM players_teams WHERE lgID = 'NBL' AND PF IS NOT NULL GROUP BY playerID HAVING SUM(PF) = (SELECT MAX(totalPF) FROM (SELECT SUM(PF) AS totalPF FROM players_teams WHERE lgID = 'NBL' AND PF IS NOT NULL GROUP BY playerID)))

question: What is the average height of an East conference All-star player?

question: Among the coaches who won the 'ABA Coach of the Year' award, which is the coach with the highest number of won games?
evidence: "ABA Coach of the Year" is the award; highest number of won games refers to Max(Count(won))
SQL: SELECT T1.coachID FROM coaches AS T1 INNER JOIN awards_coaches AS T2 ON T1.coachID = T2.coachID WHERE T2.award = 'ABA Coach of the Year' GROUP BY T1.coachID, T1.won ORDER BY T1.won DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T1.coachID FROM awards_coaches T1 JOIN coaches T2 ON T1.coachID = T2.coachID AND T1.year = T2.year WHERE T1.award = 'ABA Coach of the Year' AND T2.won IS NOT NULL GROUP BY T1.coachID ORDER BY SUM(T2.won) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: What is the full name of the team that the 'NBA Coach of the Year' 1992 winner coached?

SQL: SELECT name FROM teams AS T1 INNER JOIN coaches AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year INNER JOIN awards_coaches AS T3 ON T2.coachID = T3.coachID AND T2.year = T3.year WHERE T3.year = 1992 AND award = 'NBA Coach of the Year'
gold: SELECT name FROM teams WHERE (year, tmID) IN (SELECT year, tmID FROM coaches WHERE (coachID, year) IN (SELECT coachID, year FROM awards_coaches WHERE year = 1992 AND award = 'NBA Coach of the Year'));

question: What is the first and last name of the player with the highest field goal made rate in 1973?

SQL: SELECT T1.firstName, T1.lastName FROM players AS T1 INNER JOIN players_teams AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE year = 1973 ORDER BY CAST(T2.fgMade AS REAL) / T2.fgAttempted DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T2.firstName, T2.lastName FROM players_teams T1 JOIN players T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T1.year = 1973 AND T1.fgAttempted IS NOT NULL AND T1.fgMade IS NOT NULL ORDER BY CAST(T1.fgMade AS REAL) / T1.fgAttempted DESC LIMIT 1;

question: What is the percentage of coaches in 1969 who were awarded "NBA Coach of the Year"?

question: What were the difference of the CHS team's winning rate between 1946 and 1947 in the post-season series games? Please provide your answer in percentages.

SQL: SELECT DISTINCT T1.firstName, T1.middleName, T1.lastName FROM players AS T1 INNER JOIN player_allstar AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.season_id = 1997 ORDER BY T2.steals DESC LIMIT 5
gold: SELECT P.firstName || ' ' || P.middleName || ' ' || P.lastName AS fullName FROM players_teams PT JOIN players P ON PT.playerID = P.playerID WHERE PT.year = 1997 GROUP BY PT.playerID ORDER BY SUM(PT.steals) DESC LIMIT 5

question: From 1980 to 1983, how many of the NBA All-Star players have more than 60% three point rate?

question: Of the players drafted in NBA between 1990 and 2000, who has the most points in all-star? List the player's first name and last name.
evidence: NBA refers to lgID = 'NBA'; between 1990 and 2000 refers to year between 1990 and 2000; the most points refers to max(points)
SQL: SELECT T3.firstName, T3.lastName FROM (SELECT T1.playerID, SUM(T2.points) AS total_points FROM draft T1 JOIN player_allstar T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T1.lgID = 'NBA' AND T1.draftYear BETWEEN 1990 AND 2000 GROUP BY T1.playerID) AS T4 JOIN players T3 ON T4.playerID = T3.playerID ORDER BY T4.total_points DESC LIMIT 1;
gold: SELECT T3.firstName, T3.lastName FROM (SELECT T1.playerID, SUM(T2.points) AS total_points FROM draft T1 JOIN player_allstar T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T1.lgID = 'NBA' AND T1.draftYear BETWEEN 1990 AND 2000 GROUP BY T1.playerID) AS T4 JOIN players T3 ON T4.playerID = T3.playerID ORDER BY T4.total_points DESC LIMIT 1;

question: Which player from Wake Forest college did the most offensive rebounds than defensive rebounds in the all-star? Please mention the full name of the player including the middle name if have any.
evidence: Wake Forest college refers to highSchool = 'Wake Forest college'; did the most offensive rebounds than defensive rebounds refers to max(subtract(sum(oRebounds), sum(dRebounds))); full name refers to first_name, middle_name, last_name
SQL: SELECT T1.firstName, T1.middleName, T1.lastName FROM players AS T1 INNER JOIN player_allstar AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T1.college = 'Wake Forest' AND T2.o_rebounds > T2.d_rebounds
gold: SELECT T2.first_name || ' ' || T2.last_name AS full_name FROM players T1 JOIN player_allstar T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T1.college = 'Wake Forest' GROUP BY T2.playerID HAVING SUM(T2.o_rebounds) > SUM(T2.d_rebounds) ORDER BY SUM(T2.o_rebounds) - SUM(T2.d_rebounds) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: What is the difference in the average age of players when they are drafted in the ABA vs when they are drafted in the NBA between the years 1970 and 1970?
evidence: ABA refers to lgID = 'ABA'; NBA refers to lgID = 'NBA'; between the years 1970 and 1970 refers to draftYear between 1970 and 1970; difference = subtract(avg(subtract(1970, year(birthDate)) where lgID = 'ABA'), avg(subtract(1970, year(birthDate)) where lgID = 'NBA'))
SQL: SELECT (SELECT AVG(1970 - strftime('%Y', birthDate)) FROM players WHERE playerID IN (SELECT playerID FROM draft WHERE draftYear = 1970 AND lgID = 'ABA')) - (SELECT AVG(1970 - strftime('%Y', birthDate)) FROM players WHERE playerID IN (SELECT playerID FROM draft WHERE draftYear = 1970 AND lgID = 'NBA')) AS AgeDifference;
gold: SELECT (SELECT AVG(1970 - strftime('%Y', birthDate)) FROM players WHERE playerID IN (SELECT playerID FROM draft WHERE draftYear = 1970 AND lgID = 'ABA')) - (SELECT AVG(1970 - strftime('%Y', birthDate)) FROM players WHERE playerID IN (SELECT playerID FROM draft WHERE draftYear = 1970 AND lgID = 'NBA')) AS AgeDifference;

question: How much did the win rate increase for the team after getting the No.1 NBA draft pick in the 2003 season than previous season?
evidence: No.1 draft pick refers to draftRound = 1; in the 2003 season refers to draftyear = 2003; increase = subtract(divide(sum(won), add(sum(won), sum(lost))) where draftyear = 2004, divide(sum(won), add(sum(won), sum(lost))) where draftyear = 2003)
SQL: SELECT (CAST(T2.won AS FLOAT) / (T2.won + T2.lost)) - (CAST(T1.won AS FLOAT) / (T1.won + T1.lost)) AS win_rate_increase FROM draft D JOIN teams T1 ON D.tmID = T1.tmID AND T1.year = 2003 JOIN teams T2 ON D.tmID = T2.tmID AND T2.year = 2004 WHERE D.draftYear = 2003 AND D.draftOverall = 1;
gold: SELECT (T2.won / CAST((T2.won + T2.lost) AS FLOAT)) - (T1.won / CAST((T1.won + T1.lost) AS FLOAT)) AS win_rate_increase FROM draft D LEFT JOIN teams T1 ON D.tmID = T1.tmID AND T1.year = 2003 LEFT JOIN teams T2 ON D.tmID = T2.tmID AND T2.year = 2004 WHERE D.draftYear = 2003 AND D.draftOverall = 1;

question: How many percent of points were scored by NBA players who belonged to 'LAL' team and had performed steals movement.
evidence: NBA refers to lgID = 'NBA'; 'LAL' team refers to tmID = 'LAL'; performed steals movement refers to steals > 0; percent = divide(count(playerID where steals > 0), count(playerID)) where lgID = 'NBA' and tmID = 'LAL' * 100%
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(IIF(T2.steals IS NOT NULL AND T1.tmID = 'LAL', 1, 0)) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.tmID) FROM teams AS T1 INNER JOIN players_teams AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year

question: From the total amount of donation to projects, what is the percentage of the amount is for school projects located in the rural area?

SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.school_metro = 'rural' THEN T1.donation_to_project ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(donation_to_project) FROM donations AS T1 INNER JOIN projects AS T2 ON T1.projectid = T2.projectid

question: Name the project that costs the most. How much has been collected from donation and what is the percentage amount still lacking?
evidence: project name refers to title; costs the most refers to max(total_price_excluding_optional_support); amount collected from donation refers to sum(donation_to_project); percentage amount refers to divide(subtract(total_price_excluding_optional_support, sum(donation_to_project)), sum(donation_to_project))*100%
SQL: SELECT T1.title, SUM(T3.donation_to_project), CAST((T2.total_price_excluding_optional_support - SUM(T3.donation_to_project)) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(T3.donation_to_project) FROM essays AS T1 INNER JOIN projects AS T2 ON T1.projectid = T2.projectid INNER JOIN donations AS T3 ON T2.projectid = T3.projectid ORDER BY T2.total_price_excluding_optional_support DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T3.title, SUM(T2.donation_to_project) AS collected_donations, ((MAX(T1.total_price_excluding_optional_support) - SUM(T2.donation_to_project)) / MAX(T1.total_price_excluding_optional_support)) * 100 AS percentage_lacking FROM projects T1 LEFT JOIN donations T2 ON T1.projectid = T2.projectid LEFT JOIN essays T3 ON T1.projectid = T3.projectid GROUP BY T1.projectid HAVING T1.total_price_excluding_optional_support = (SELECT MAX(total_price_excluding_optional_support) FROM projects)

question: What percentage of donations are given via a giving or campaign page? List the primary area of those donations.
evidence: given via a giving or campaign page refers to via_giving_page = 't'; percentage refers to DIVIDE(count(case when via_giving_page = 't' then donationid else null end),count(donationid))*100; primary area of donation refers to primary_focus_area
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.via_giving_page = 't' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(donation_total), ( SELECT T2.primary_focus_area FROM donations AS T1 INNER JOIN projects AS T2 ON T1.projectid = T2.projectid WHERE T1.via_giving_page = 't' GROUP BY T2.primary_focus_area ORDER BY SUM(T1.donation_total) DESC LIMIT 1 ) result FROM donations AS T1 INNER JOIN projects AS T2 ON T1.projectid = T2.projectid
gold: SELECT T2.primary_focus_area, (COUNT(CASE WHEN T1.via_giving_page = 't' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage FROM donations T1 JOIN projects T2 ON T1.projectid = T2.projectid GROUP BY T2.primary_focus_area;

question: Among the technology items, what percentage of them are from Best Buy for Business? Provide the date of the project related to those items.

SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.vendor_name = 'Best Buy for Business' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.projectid) FROM resources AS T1 INNER JOIN projects AS T2 ON T1.projectid = T2.projectid WHERE T1.project_resource_type = 'Technology' UNION ALL SELECT DISTINCT T1.date_posted FROM projects AS T1 INNER JOIN resources AS T2 ON T1.projectid = T2.projectid WHERE T2.vendor_name = 'Best Buy for Business' AND T2.project_resource_type = 'Technology'
gold: SELECT T2.date_posted, (COUNT(CASE WHEN T1.vendor_name = 'Best Buy for Business' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(T1.projectid)) AS percentage FROM resources T1 JOIN projects T2 ON T1.projectid = T2.projectid WHERE T1.project_resource_type = 'Technology' GROUP BY T2.date_posted;

question: How many more games were sold on game platform ID 50 than on game platform ID 51 in region ID 1?

SQL: SELECT T1.chronname, T1.unitid FROM institution_details AS T1 INNER JOIN state_sector_grads AS T2 ON T2.state = T1.state WHERE T2.state_abbr = 'KY' AND T1.level = '4-year' AND T1.control = 'Private for-profit' GROUP BY T1.chronname ORDER BY SUM(T1.grad_150_value) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T1.unitid FROM institution_details T1 WHERE T1.state = 'KY' AND T1.level = '4-year' AND T1.control = 'Private for-profit' AND T1.grad_150_value = (SELECT MAX(T2.grad_150_value) FROM institution_details T2 WHERE T2.state = 'KY' AND T2.level = '4-year' AND T2.control = 'Private for-profit');

question: What is the percentage of the number of 4-year public schools from Madison Area Technical College's home state in the Alabama?
evidence: percentage = MULTIPLY(DIVIDE(SUM(chronname = 'Madison Area Technical College'), SUM(state = 'Alabama')), 100); 4-year refers to level = '4-year'; public refers to control = 'Public'; Madison Area Technical College refers to chronname = 'Madison Area Technical College'; home state in the United States refers to state;
SQL: SELECT CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T1.state = ( SELECT T1.state FROM institution_details AS T1 INNER JOIN state_sector_details AS T2 ON T2.state = T1.state WHERE T1.chronname = 'Madison Area Technical College' ) AND T1.level = '4-year' AND T1.control = 'Public' THEN T1.chronname ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T2.state = 'Alabama' THEN T1.chronname ELSE NULL END) FROM institution_details AS T1 INNER JOIN state_sector_details AS T2 ON T2.state = T1.state
gold: SELECT 100.0 * (SELECT SUM(schools_count) FROM state_sector_details WHERE state = (SELECT state FROM institution_details WHERE chronname = 'Madison Area Technical College') AND level = '4-year' AND control = 'Public') / (SELECT SUM(schools_count) FROM state_sector_details WHERE state = 'Alabama') AS percentage;

question: Find out which hotel and travel business having the most review? Calculate the standard deviation of the review star for this business.

SQL: WITH CategoryID AS (SELECT category_id FROM Categories WHERE category_name = 'Hotels & Travel'), BusinessInCategory AS (SELECT business_id FROM Business_Categories WHERE category_id = (SELECT category_id FROM CategoryID)), ReviewStats AS (SELECT business_id, COUNT(*) AS review_count, AVG(review_stars) AS avg_stars FROM Reviews WHERE business_id IN (SELECT business_id FROM BusinessInCategory) GROUP BY business_id), MaxReview AS (SELECT MAX(review_count) AS max_review FROM ReviewStats) SELECT business_id, (SUM((review_stars - (SELECT avg_stars FROM ReviewStats WHERE business_id = Reviews.business_id)) * (review_stars - (SELECT avg_stars FROM ReviewStats WHERE business_id = Reviews.business_id))) / COUNT(review_stars)) AS std_dev FROM Reviews WHERE business_id IN (SELECT business_id FROM ReviewStats WHERE review_count = (SELECT max_review FROM MaxReview)) GROUP BY business_id;
gold: WITH CategoryID AS (SELECT category_id FROM Categories WHERE category_name = 'Hotels & Travel'), BusinessInCategory AS (SELECT business_id FROM Business_Categories WHERE category_id = (SELECT category_id FROM CategoryID)), ReviewStats AS (SELECT business_id, COUNT(*) AS review_count, AVG(review_stars) AS avg_stars FROM Reviews WHERE business_id IN (SELECT business_id FROM BusinessInCategory) GROUP BY business_id), MaxReview AS (SELECT MAX(review_count) AS max_review FROM ReviewStats) SELECT business_id, (SUM((review_stars - (SELECT avg_stars FROM ReviewStats WHERE business_id = Reviews.business_id)) * (review_stars - (SELECT avg_stars FROM ReviewStats WHERE business_id = Reviews.business_id))) / COUNT(review_stars)) AS std_dev FROM Reviews WHERE business_id IN (SELECT business_id FROM ReviewStats WHERE review_count = (SELECT max_review FROM MaxReview)) GROUP BY business_id;

SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN user_fans = 'None' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(user_id) FROM Users WHERE user_average_stars >= 4

question: Identify the operating hours of businesses in Black Canyon City with review count greater than average.

question: What is the ratio of good to bad business star for a businesses that are opened all the time?

question: How many business are opened for more than 8 hour in Mesa and what is the percentage of the active businesses?
evidence: business are opened for more than 8 hours refer to business_id where SUBTRACT(closing_time, opening_time) > 8; DIVIDE(COUNT(business_id where active = 'true' and city = 'Mesa' and SUBTRACT(closing_time, opening_time) > 8), COUNT(business_id where city = 'Mesa' and SUBTRACT(closing_time, opening_time) > 8)) as percentage;
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS Total_Opened_More_Than_8_Hours, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Business B INNER JOIN Business_Hours BH ON B.business_id = BH.business_id WHERE B.city = 'Mesa' AND B.active = 'True' AND (strftime('%H:%M', BH.closing_time) - strftime('%H:%M', BH.opening_time)) > 8) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) AS Percentage_Active FROM Business B INNER JOIN Business_Hours BH ON B.business_id = BH.business_id WHERE B.city = 'Mesa' AND (strftime('%H:%M', BH.closing_time) - strftime('%H:%M', BH.opening_time)) > 8;
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) AS Total_Opened_More_Than_8_Hours, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Business B INNER JOIN Business_Hours BH ON B.business_id = BH.business_id WHERE B.city = 'Mesa' AND B.active = 'True' AND (strftime('%H:%M', BH.closing_time) - strftime('%H:%M', BH.opening_time)) > 8) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) AS Percentage_Active FROM Business B INNER JOIN Business_Hours BH ON B.business_id = BH.business_id WHERE B.city = 'Mesa' AND (strftime('%H:%M', BH.closing_time) - strftime('%H:%M', BH.opening_time)) > 8;

question: Among the working days from Monday to Saturday, which businesses with the category names work the most days?

question: How many businesses have the category named food? List those businesses and find the percentage of businesses with less than 2 stars.
evidence: businesses have the category named food refer to business_id where category_name = 'Food'; DIVIDE(COUNT(business_id where category_name = 'Food' and stars < 2), COUNT(business_id where category_name = 'Food')) as percentage;
SQL: SELECT T3.business_id, CAST((( SELECT COUNT(business_id) FROM Business WHERE stars < 2 ) - ( SELECT COUNT(business_id) FROM Business WHERE stars > 2 )) AS REAL) * 100 / ( SELECT COUNT(stars) FROM Business ) FROM Business_Categories AS T1 INNER JOIN Categories AS T2 ON T1.category_id = T2.category_id INNER JOIN Business AS T3 ON T1.business_id = T3.business_id WHERE T2.category_name = 'Food'
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.business_id) AS total_food_businesses, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Business WHERE business_id IN (SELECT business_id FROM Business_Categories WHERE category_id = (SELECT category_id FROM Categories WHERE category_name = 'Food')) AND stars < 2) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT T1.business_id) AS percentage_below_2_stars FROM Business T1 JOIN Business_Categories T2 ON T1.business_id = T2.business_id JOIN Categories T3 ON T2.category_id = T3.category_id WHERE T3.category_name = 'Food';

question: What is the percentage of businesses with "Good for Kids" attribute over the other attributes?

question: Calculate the percentage of users with a high number of fans who were elite in 2011.

question: List the closing time and day of week of active businesses in Goodyear with stars greater than the 80% of average age of star rating.
evidence: active business ID refers to active = 'true'; Goodyear is a city; Calculation = AVG(stars) * 0.8; businesses with stars greater than 80% of average star rating refers to stars > AVG(stars) * 0.8
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT T2.closing_time, T3.day_of_week FROM Business AS T1 INNER JOIN Business_Hours AS T2 ON T1.business_id = T2.business_id INNER JOIN Days AS T3 ON T2.day_id = T3.day_id WHERE T1.active = 'true' AND T1.city = 'Goodyear' AND T1.stars > ( SELECT AVG(stars) * 0.8 FROM Business WHERE active = 'true' AND city = 'Goodyear' )
gold: SELECT T3.day_of_week, T2.closing_time FROM Business AS T1 JOIN Business_Hours AS T2 ON T1.business_id = T2.business_id JOIN Days AS T3 ON T2.day_id = T3.day_id WHERE T1.active = 'True' AND T1.city = 'Goodyear' AND T1.stars > (SELECT 0.8 * AVG(stars) FROM Business)

question: Among all the citation, what is the percentage of paper ID under the Agents classification?
evidence: classification refers to class_label; class_label = 'Agents'; percentage = (divide(count(paper_id where class_label = 'Agents')), (count(paper_id)))*100;
SQL: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT T1.paper_id) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cited_paper_id) FROM cites)) AS percentage FROM paper AS T1 WHERE T1.class_label = 'Agents' AND T1.paper_id IN (SELECT cited_paper_id FROM cites);
gold: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT T1.paper_id) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cited_paper_id) FROM cites)) AS percentage FROM paper AS T1 WHERE T1.class_label = 'Agents' AND T1.paper_id IN (SELECT cited_paper_id FROM cites);

gold: WITH CitationCounts AS (SELECT word_cited_id, COUNT(paper_id) AS citation_count FROM content GROUP BY word_cited_id) SELECT word_cited_id, citation_count FROM CitationCounts WHERE citation_count = (SELECT MAX(citation_count) FROM CitationCounts);

question: What is the percentage ratio between uncredited and credited roles on the episode that won the 2017 Jupiter Award for Best International TV Series? Please include the title of the episode and the names of the persons who were uncredited alongside their role in that episode.
evidence: uncredited refers to credited = ''; credited refers to credited = 'true'; won refers to result = 'Winner'; 2017 is the year; 'Jupiter Award' is the award_category; 'Best International TV Series' is the award; percentage ratio = Divide (SUM(credited = ''), SUM(credited = 'true')) * 100
SQL: SELECT E.title, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Credit WHERE credited = 'false' AND episode_id = E.episode_id) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Credit WHERE credited = 'true' AND episode_id = E.episode_id) AS percentage_ratio, C.person, C.role FROM Award A JOIN Episode E ON A.episode_id = E.episode_id JOIN Credit C ON E.episode_id = C.episode_id WHERE A.year = 2017 AND A.award = 'Best International TV Series' AND A.result = 'Winner' AND C.credited = 'false' GROUP BY E.title, C.person, C.role
gold: SELECT E.title, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Credit WHERE credited = 'false' AND episode_id = E.episode_id) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Credit WHERE credited = 'true' AND episode_id = E.episode_id) AS percentage_ratio, C.person, C.role FROM Award A JOIN Episode E ON A.episode_id = E.episode_id JOIN Credit C ON E.episode_id = C.episode_id WHERE A.year = 2017 AND A.award = 'Best International TV Series' AND A.result = 'Winner' AND C.credited = 'false' GROUP BY E.title, C.person, C.role
