SQL: SELECT T3.rate, T4.person, T4.award, T5.title, T4.role FROM ( SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.result = 'Winner' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN T1.result IN ('Winner', 'Nominee') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rate , T1.person, T1.award, T2.title, T1.role FROM Award AS T1 INNER JOIN Episode AS T2 ON T1.episode_id = T2.episode_id WHERE SUBSTR(T1.year, 1, 4) = '2010' ) AS T3 INNER JOIN Award AS T4 INNER JOIN Episode AS T5 ON T4.episode_id = T5.episode_id WHERE T4.year = 2010 AND T4.result = 'Winner';
gold: SELECT T1.person, T1.award, T2.title, T1.role, (SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS FLOAT) FROM Award WHERE year = 2010 AND result = 'Winner') / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Award WHERE year = 2010) AS winning_rate FROM Award T1 JOIN Episode T2 ON T1.episode_id = T2.episode_id WHERE T1.year = 2010 AND T1.result = 'Winner';

SQL: SELECT T2.votes FROM Keyword AS T1 INNER JOIN Vote AS T2 ON T1.episode_id = T2.episode_id WHERE T2.stars = 10 AND T1.keyword = 'reference to the fantastic four';
gold: SELECT T2.votes FROM Keyword T1 JOIN Vote T2 ON T1.episode_id = T2.episode_id WHERE T1.keyword = 'reference to the fantastic four' AND T2.stars = 10;

question: What is the difference between the number of votes for 1-star vs. 10-star for the episode "The Burns and the Bees"?
evidence: 1-star refers to stars = 1; 10-star refers to stars = 10; episode "The Burns and the Bees" refers to title = 'The Burns and the Bees'; difference refers to SUBTRACT(votes when stars = 1, votes when stars = 10)
SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T2.stars = 10 THEN T2.votes ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN T2.stars = 1 THEN T2.votes ELSE 0 END) AS Difference FROM Episode AS T1 INNER JOIN Vote AS T2 ON T2.episode_id = T1.episode_id WHERE T1.title = 'The Burns and the Bees';
gold: SELECT (SELECT V.votes FROM Vote V JOIN Episode E ON V.episode_id = E.episode_id WHERE V.stars = 1 AND E.title = 'The Burns and the Bees') - (SELECT V.votes FROM Vote V JOIN Episode E ON V.episode_id = E.episode_id WHERE V.stars = 10 AND E.title = 'The Burns and the Bees') AS difference;

question: What are the titles of the episodes that have received more 7-star votes than the season average?

SQL: SELECT E.title FROM Episode E JOIN Vote V ON E.episode_id = V.episode_id WHERE V.stars = 7 GROUP BY E.episode_id HAVING SUM(V.votes) > (SELECT AVG(V2.votes) FROM Vote V2 WHERE V2.stars = 7 AND V2.episode_id IN (SELECT episode_id FROM Episode WHERE season = E.season))
gold: SELECT E.title FROM Episode E JOIN Vote V ON E.episode_id = V.episode_id WHERE V.stars = 7 GROUP BY E.episode_id HAVING SUM(V.votes) > (SELECT AVG(V2.votes) FROM Vote V2 WHERE V2.stars = 7 AND V2.episode_id IN (SELECT episode_id FROM Episode WHERE season = E.season))

question: What percentage of votes are from the nominated episodes?
evidence: nominated episodes refers to result = 'Nominee'; percentage of votes = DIVIDE(SUM(result = 'Nominee), SUM(Votes)) as percentage
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.result = 'Nominee' THEN T2.votes ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(T2.votes) FROM Award AS T1 INNER JOIN Episode AS T2 ON T1.episode_id = T2.episode_id;
gold: WITH NominatedVotes AS (SELECT SUM(votes) AS nominated_votes FROM Award JOIN Vote ON Award.episode_id = Vote.episode_id WHERE result = 'Nominee' AND votes IS NOT NULL), TotalVotes AS (SELECT SUM(votes) AS total_votes FROM Vote WHERE votes IS NOT NULL) SELECT (nominated_votes * 100.0 / total_votes) AS percentage FROM NominatedVotes, TotalVotes;

question: What is the percentage ratio of students who are enlisted in foreign legions that have a due payment?
evidence: have a due payment refers to bool = 'pos'; in foreign legions refers to organ = 'foreign_legion'; ratio refers to DIVIDE(COUNT(bool = 'pos'), COUNT(bool = 'neg'))
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(IIF(T1.bool = 'pos', 1, 0)) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(IIF(T1.bool = 'neg', 1, 0)) FROM no_payment_due AS T1 INNER JOIN enlist AS T2 ON T1.`name` = T2.`name` WHERE T2.organ = 'foreign_legion'
gold: SELECT (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.bool = 'pos' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS FLOAT) / COUNT(T2.bool)) * 100 AS percentage FROM enlist T1 JOIN no_payment_due T2 ON T1.name = T2.name WHERE T1.organ = 'foreign_legion';

question: What is the employment, disability, gender and school debt status for student180 and student117?
evidence: school debt status refers to bool; bool = 'pos' means has payment due; bool = 'neg' means doesn't has payment due; student appear in male.name means he is a male; student does not appear in male.name means she is a female;
SQL: SELECT ( SELECT COUNT(name) FROM disabled WHERE name IN ('student180', 'student117') ), ( SELECT COUNT(name) FROM unemployed WHERE name IN ('student180', 'student117') ), ( SELECT COUNT(name) FROM male WHERE name IN ('student180', 'student117') ), ( SELECT COUNT(name) FROM no_payment_due WHERE name IN ('student180', 'student117'))
gold: SELECT S.name, IFNULL(U.name, 'employed') AS employment, IFNULL(D.name, 'not disabled') AS disability, IFNULL(M.name, 'female') AS gender, IFNULL(P.bool, 'no debt') AS debt FROM (SELECT 'student180' AS name UNION ALL SELECT 'student117') S LEFT OUTER JOIN unemployed U ON S.name = U.name LEFT OUTER JOIN disabled D ON S.name = D.name LEFT OUTER JOIN male M ON S.name = M.name LEFT OUTER JOIN no_payment_due P ON S.name = P.name

question: Which organization has the highest number of male students? Calculate for the percentage of the male students in the said organization.

question: Find the difference between the number of female senators and representatives born between 1930 to 1970.
evidence: difference = SUBTRACT(SUM(type = 'sen' WHERE gender_bio = 'F' AND strftime('%Y', birthday_bio) between '1930' and '1970'), SUM(type = 'rep' WHERE gender_bio = 'F' AND strftime('%Y', birthday_bio) between '1930' and '1970')); female refers to gender_bio = 'F'; senators refers to type = 'sen'; representatives refers to type = 'rep'; born between 1930 to 1970 strftime('%Y', birthday_bio) between '1930' and '1970';
SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T2.type = 'sen' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN T2.type = 'rep' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM historical AS T1 INNER JOIN `historical-terms` AS T2 ON T1.bioguide_id = T2.bioguide WHERE T1.gender_bio = 'F' AND strftime('%Y', T1.birthday_bio) BETWEEN '1930' AND '1970'
gold: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM current T1 JOIN `current-terms` T2 ON T1.bioguide_id = T2.bioguide WHERE T1.gender_bio = 'F' AND T2.type = 'sen' AND strftime('%Y', T1.birthday_bio) BETWEEN '1930' AND '1970') - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM current T1 JOIN `current-terms` T2 ON T1.bioguide_id = T2.bioguide WHERE T1.gender_bio = 'F' AND T2.type = 'rep' AND strftime('%Y', T1.birthday_bio) BETWEEN '1930' AND '1970') AS difference;

question: Among the male legislators born between 1955 to 1965, what is the percentage of the legislators with an independent party?

SQL: SELECT T1.official_full_name FROM current AS T1 INNER JOIN `current-terms` AS T2 ON T1.bioguide_id = T2.bioguide WHERE T2.party = 'Independent' AND strftime('%Y', T2.start) >= '2011' AND T2.type = 'sen' AND T2.caucus = 'Democrat'
gold: SELECT official_full_name FROM current WHERE bioguide_id IN (SELECT bioguide FROM `current-terms` WHERE party = 'Independent' AND type = 'sen' AND caucus = 'Democrat' AND strftime('%Y', start) >= '2011')

question: List the official full names of all the legislators that served 13 district for 26 consecutive years.
evidence: served only one district for 26 consecutive years refers to SUBTRACT(SUM(cast(strftime('%Y', end)), CAST(strftime('%Y', start)))) = 26
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT CASE WHEN SUM(CAST(strftime('%Y', T2.end) AS int) - CAST(strftime('%Y', T2.start) AS int)) = 26 THEN T1.official_full_name END FROM current AS T1 INNER JOIN `current-terms` AS T2 ON T1.bioguide_id = T2.bioguide GROUP BY T1.official_full_name, T2.district HAVING COUNT(T1.official_full_name) = 13
gold: SELECT T4.official_full_name FROM (SELECT T1.bioguide, SUM(CAST(strftime('%Y', T1.end) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', T1.start) AS INTEGER)) AS years_served FROM `current-terms` T1 WHERE T1.district = 13 GROUP BY T1.bioguide HAVING years_served = 26 UNION SELECT T2.bioguide, SUM(CAST(strftime('%Y', T2.end) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', T2.start) AS INTEGER)) AS years_served FROM `historical-terms` T2 WHERE T2.district = 13 GROUP BY T2.bioguide HAVING years_served = 26) T3 JOIN current T4 ON T3.bioguide = T4.bioguide_id

question: In the Winter and Summer Olympics of 1988, which game has the most number of competitors? Find the difference of the number of competitors between the two games.

question: Which summer Olympic have the highest and lowest number of participants?

SQL: SELECT T3.first_name, T3.last_name FROM zip_data AS T1 INNER JOIN zip_congress AS T2 ON T1.zip_code = T2.zip_code INNER JOIN congress AS T3 ON T2.district = T3.cognress_rep_id WHERE T1.population_2020 > 30000 GROUP BY T3.first_name, T3.last_name
gold: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM congress WHERE cognress_rep_id IN (SELECT district FROM zip_congress WHERE zip_code IN (SELECT zip_code FROM zip_data WHERE population_2020 > 30000));

question: Which zip code in Massachusetts that have more than 1 area code?

SQL: SELECT T1.zip_code FROM area_code AS T1 INNER JOIN zip_data AS T2 ON T1.zip_code = T2.zip_code WHERE T2.state = 'MA' GROUP BY T1.zip_code HAVING COUNT(T1.area_code) > 1
gold: SELECT T1.zip_code FROM zip_data T1 JOIN area_code T2 ON T1.zip_code = T2.zip_code WHERE T1.state = 'Massachusetts' GROUP BY T1.zip_code HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT T2.area_code) > 1;

question: Calculate the difference between the 2020 population and the 2010 population for the districts represented by Griffin Tim.
evidence: difference = Subtract (population_2020, population_2010)
SQL: SELECT T1.population_2020 - T1.population_2010 FROM zip_data AS T1 INNER JOIN zip_congress AS T2 ON T1.zip_code = T2.zip_code INNER JOIN congress AS T3 ON T2.district = T3.cognress_rep_id WHERE T3.first_name = 'Griffin' AND T3.last_name = 'Tim'

SQL: SELECT T2.TransactionDate FROM customers AS T1 INNER JOIN `transaction` AS T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID WHERE T1.First = 'Natalie' AND T1.Last = 'Dorris' ORDER BY T2.TransactionDate LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT FirstPurchaseDate FROM customers WHERE First = 'Natalie' AND Last = 'Dorris';

question: For the root beer brand with the most 5 star ratings, what is the name of the brewery?
evidence: most 5 star ratings refers to MAX(COUNT(StarRating = 5)); name of the brewery refers to BreweryName;
SQL: SELECT T1.BreweryName FROM rootbeerbrand AS T1 INNER JOIN rootbeerreview AS T2 ON T1.BrandID = T2.BrandID WHERE T2.StarRating = 5 GROUP BY T1.BrandID ORDER BY COUNT(T2.StarRating) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT BreweryName FROM rootbeerbrand WHERE BrandID IN (SELECT BrandID FROM rootbeerreview WHERE StarRating = 5 GROUP BY BrandID HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(C) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS C FROM rootbeerreview WHERE StarRating = 5 GROUP BY BrandID)))

question: For the customer who gave a 3 star rating to Frostie brand on 2014/4/24, did the user permit the company to send regular emails to him/her?
evidence: 3 star rating refers to StarRating = 3; Frostie refers to  BrandName = 'Frostie'; if SubscribedToEmailList = 'TRUE', it means the user permit the company to send regular emails to him/her; if SubscribedToEmailList = FALSE', it means the user did not permit the company to send regular emails to him/her; rating on 2014/4/24 refers to ReviewDate = '2014-04-24';
SQL: SELECT T3.SubscribedToEmailList FROM rootbeerbrand T1 JOIN rootbeerreview T2 ON T1.BrandID = T2.BrandID JOIN customers T3 ON T2.CustomerID = T3.CustomerID WHERE T1.BrandName = 'Frostie' AND T2.StarRating = 3 AND T2.ReviewDate = '2014-04-24';
gold: SELECT T3.SubscribedToEmailList FROM rootbeerbrand T1 JOIN rootbeerreview T2 ON T1.BrandID = T2.BrandID JOIN customers T3 ON T2.CustomerID = T3.CustomerID WHERE T1.BrandName = 'Frostie' AND T2.StarRating = 3 AND T2.ReviewDate = '2014-04-24';

question: For the root beer brand which got the review with the content of "The quintessential dessert root beer. No ice cream required.", what is the current retail price of the root beer?
evidence: review with the content of "The quintessential dessert root beer. No ice cream required." refers to Review = 'The quintessential dessert root beer. No ice cream required.';
SQL: SELECT CurrentRetailPrice FROM rootbeerbrand WHERE BrandID IN (SELECT BrandID FROM rootbeerreview WHERE Review = 'The quintessential dessert root beer. No ice cream required.');
gold: SELECT CurrentRetailPrice FROM rootbeerbrand WHERE BrandID IN (SELECT BrandID FROM rootbeerreview WHERE Review = 'The quintessential dessert root beer. No ice cream required.');

question: What is the percentage of 5 star ratings River City brand root beer get?
evidence: percentage = MULTIPLY(DIVIDE(SUM(BrandID WHERE StarRating = 5), COUNT(BrandID) WHERE BrandName = 'River City'), 1.0); 5 star ratings refers to StarRating = 5; River City refers to BrandName = 'River City';
SQL: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.StarRating = 5 THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T2.StarRating) FROM rootbeerbrand AS T1 INNER JOIN rootbeerreview AS T2 ON T1.BrandID = T2.BrandID WHERE T1.BrandName = 'River City'
gold: SELECT (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.StarRating = 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS FLOAT) / COUNT(T1.BrandID)) * 100 AS Percentage FROM rootbeerreview T1 JOIN rootbeerbrand T2 ON T1.BrandID = T2.BrandID WHERE T2.BrandName = 'River City';

question: What is the average number of reviews of all the root beer brands from "CA" State?
evidence: average = DIVIDE(COUNT(CustomerID), COUNT(BrandID) WHERE state = CA);
SQL: SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT T1.BrandID) AS avgreview FROM rootbeerbrand AS T1 INNER JOIN rootbeerreview AS T2 ON T1.BrandID = T2.BrandID WHERE T1.State = 'CA'
gold: SELECT AVG(ReviewCount) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS ReviewCount FROM rootbeerreview T1 JOIN rootbeerbrand T2 ON T1.BrandID = T2.BrandID WHERE T2.State = 'CA' GROUP BY T1.BrandID);

question: What are the brands of the root beers that received 5-star ratings from no less than 5 customers?
evidence: brand of the root beer refers to BrandName; 5-star ratings refers to StarRating = 5; no less than 5 customers refers to COUNT(CustomerID) > = 5;
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT b.BrandName FROM rootbeerbrand b JOIN rootbeerreview r ON b.BrandID = r.BrandID WHERE r.StarRating = 5 GROUP BY r.BrandID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT r.CustomerID) >= 5;

question: List the brands of root beer produced by Dr Pepper Snapple Group and calculate their percentage of purchases between 2014 to 2016.
evidence: brand of root beer refers to BrandName; produced by Dr Pepper Snapple Group refers to BreweryName = 'Dr Pepper Snapple Group'; percentage of purchases = MULTIPLY(DIVIDE(SUM(BrandID WHERE PurchaseDate > = '2014-01-01' AND PurchaseDate < = '2016-12-31'), COUNT(BrandID) WHERE BreweryName = 'Dr Pepper Snapple Group'), 1.0); between 2014 to 2016 refers to PurchaseDate > = '2014-01-01' AND PurchaseDate < = '2016-12-31;
SQL: SELECT T1.BrandName , CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.PurchaseDate >= '2014-01-01' AND T2.PurchaseDate <= '2016-12-31' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / COUNT(T2.BrandID) AS purchase FROM rootbeerbrand AS T1 INNER JOIN rootbeer AS T2 ON T1.BrandID = T2.BrandID WHERE T1.BreweryName = 'Dr Pepper Snapple Group' GROUP BY T2.BrandID
gold: SELECT T1.BrandName, (COUNT(T2.BrandID) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rootbeer WHERE BrandID IN (SELECT BrandID FROM rootbeerbrand WHERE BreweryName = 'Dr Pepper Snapple Group'))) AS PurchasePercentage FROM rootbeerbrand T1 JOIN rootbeer T2 ON T1.BrandID = T2.BrandID WHERE T1.BreweryName = 'Dr Pepper Snapple Group' AND T2.PurchaseDate BETWEEN '2014-01-01' AND '2016-12-31' GROUP BY T1.BrandName;

question: Find the root beer with the most and least amount of profit per unit and list the container types in which these root beers are sold.
evidence: most amount of profit per unit refers to MAX(SUBTRACT(CurrentRetailPrice, WholesaleCost)); least amount of profit per unit refers to MIN(SUBTRACT(CurrentRetailPrice, WholesaleCost));
SQL: SELECT T2.ContainerType FROM rootbeer T2 JOIN rootbeerbrand T1 ON T2.BrandID = T1.BrandID WHERE (T1.CurrentRetailPrice - T1.WholesaleCost) = (SELECT MAX(T1.CurrentRetailPrice - T1.WholesaleCost) FROM rootbeerbrand T1) OR (T1.CurrentRetailPrice - T1.WholesaleCost) = (SELECT MIN(T1.CurrentRetailPrice - T1.WholesaleCost) FROM rootbeerbrand T1);
gold: SELECT T2.ContainerType FROM rootbeer T2 JOIN rootbeerbrand T1 ON T2.BrandID = T1.BrandID WHERE (T1.CurrentRetailPrice - T1.WholesaleCost) = (SELECT MAX(T1.CurrentRetailPrice - T1.WholesaleCost) FROM rootbeerbrand T1) OR (T1.CurrentRetailPrice - T1.WholesaleCost) = (SELECT MIN(T1.CurrentRetailPrice - T1.WholesaleCost) FROM rootbeerbrand T1);

SQL: SELECT AVG(T1.StarRating) FROM rootbeerreview T1 JOIN customers T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID WHERE T2.Gender = 'F' AND T1.BrandID = 10018 AND T1.ReviewDate BETWEEN '2015-01-25' AND '2015-03-10';
gold: SELECT AVG(T1.StarRating) FROM rootbeerreview T1 JOIN customers T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID WHERE T2.Gender = 'F' AND T1.BrandID = 10018 AND T1.ReviewDate BETWEEN '2015-01-25' AND '2015-03-10';

question: List down the brand names of root beer that gained a 5-star rating from a customer's review in 2013. Calculate the unit profit available to wholesalers for each brand.
evidence: 5-star rating refers to StarRating = 5; in 2013 refers to ReviewDate LIKE '2013%'; unit profit available to wholesalers = SUBTRACT(CurrentRetailPrice, WholesaleCost);
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT T2.BrandName, (T2.CurrentRetailPrice - T2.WholesaleCost) AS UnitProfit FROM rootbeerreview T1 JOIN rootbeerbrand T2 ON T1.BrandID = T2.BrandID WHERE T1.StarRating = 5 AND T1.ReviewDate LIKE '2013%'
gold: SELECT DISTINCT T2.BrandName, (T2.CurrentRetailPrice - T2.WholesaleCost) AS UnitProfit FROM rootbeerreview T1 JOIN rootbeerbrand T2 ON T1.BrandID = T2.BrandID WHERE T1.StarRating = 5 AND T1.ReviewDate LIKE '2013%'

question: Give me the full name of the first customer, and tell me how long ago he or she wrote his or her first review since making his or her first purchase.

SQL: SELECT T1.First, T1.Last , strftime('%J', ReviewDate) - strftime('%J', FirstPurchaseDate) AS TIMEAGO FROM customers AS T1 INNER JOIN rootbeerreview AS T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T1.First || ' ' || T1.Last AS FullName, (julianday(T2.ReviewDate) - julianday(T1.FirstPurchaseDate)) AS DaysSinceFirstPurchase FROM customers T1 JOIN rootbeerreview T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID WHERE T1.FirstPurchaseDate = (SELECT MIN(FirstPurchaseDate) FROM customers) LIMIT 1;

question: Which dish lasted longer, Anchovies or Fresh lobsters in every style?
evidence: if (SUBTRACT(last_appeared, first_appeared) WHERE name = 'Anchovies') > (SUBTRACT(last_appeared, first_appeared) WHERE name = 'Fresh lobsters in every style'), it means 'Anchovies' lasted longer; if (SUBTRACT(last_appeared , first_appeared) WHERE name = 'Fresh lobsters in every style') > (SUBTRACT(last_appeared , first_appeared) WHERE name = 'Anchovies') it means 'Fresh lobsters in every style' last longer;
SQL: SELECT CASE WHEN (SELECT last_appeared - first_appeared FROM Dish WHERE name = 'Anchovies') > (SELECT last_appeared - first_appeared FROM Dish WHERE name = 'Fresh lobsters in every style') THEN 'Anchovies' ELSE 'Fresh lobsters in every style' END AS longer_lasting_dish FROM Dish WHERE name IN ('Anchovies', 'Fresh lobsters in every style') LIMIT 1;
gold: SELECT 'Anchovies' AS dish FROM Dish WHERE name = 'Anchovies' AND (last_appeared - first_appeared) > (SELECT last_appeared - first_appeared FROM Dish WHERE name = 'Fresh lobsters in every style') UNION SELECT 'Fresh lobsters in every style' AS dish FROM Dish WHERE name = 'Fresh lobsters in every style' AND (last_appeared - first_appeared) > (SELECT last_appeared - first_appeared FROM Dish WHERE name = 'Anchovies');

question: What is the average number of dishes per menu in the Souper de Luxe menus? Identify what is the name of the dish that appeared the most in all of its menus.
evidence: average number of dishes per menu = DIVIDE(COUNT(dish_id), COUNT(menu_page_id)); Souper de Luxe is a name of menu; dish that appeared the most in all of its menus refers to MAX(COUNT(dish_id));
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*), T1.dish_id FROM MenuItem AS T1 INNER JOIN MenuPage AS T2 ON T1.menu_page_id = T2.id INNER JOIN Menu AS T3 ON T2.menu_id = T3.id INNER JOIN Dish AS T4 ON T1.dish_id = T4.id WHERE T3.name = 'Souper de Luxe' GROUP BY T3.id ORDER BY COUNT(T1.dish_id) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT AVG(dish_count) AS average_dishes_per_menu, (SELECT T4.name FROM (SELECT T3.dish_id, COUNT(*) AS dish_count FROM MenuItem T3 JOIN MenuPage T2 ON T3.menu_page_id = T2.id JOIN Menu T1 ON T2.menu_id = T1.id WHERE T1.name = 'Souper de Luxe' GROUP BY T3.dish_id ORDER BY dish_count DESC LIMIT 1) T5 JOIN Dish T4 ON T5.dish_id = T4.id) AS most_frequent_dish FROM (SELECT T1.id, COUNT(DISTINCT T3.dish_id) AS dish_count FROM Menu T1 JOIN MenuPage T2 ON T1.id = T2.menu_id JOIN MenuItem T3 ON T2.id = T3.menu_page_id WHERE T1.name = 'Souper de Luxe' GROUP BY T1.id) T6;

question: Which menu page has a bigger width, page 1 of "Zentral Theater Terrace" or page 1 of "Young's Hotel"?

question: Among all shipments placed by Sunguard Window Tinting & Truck Accessories in 2017, identify the percentage of shipments whose weight exceeded 10,000 pounds.

question: Which headquarter's truck has the highest shipments in year 2016?
evidence: in 2016 refers to CAST(ship_date AS DATE) = 2016; make = 'Peterbilt' means headquarter is 'Texas (TX)', make = 'Mack' means headquarter is 'North Carolina (NC)', make = 'Kenworth' means headquarter is 'Washington (WA)'; highest shipment refers to MAX(COUNT(ship_id))

question: Calculate the average number of shipments that Zachery Hicks shipped in year 2017.

question: How many times greater is the appearances of the biword pair "a base" than "a decimal"?
evidence: a, base AND decimal are words; wid is the ID of word; w1st is the first word of a biword pair; w2nd is the second word of a biword pair; appearances refers to biwords.occurrences; biword pair 'a base' refers to word = 'a' as w1st AND word = 'base' as w2nd; biword pair 'a decimal' refers to word = 'a' as w1st AND word = 'decimal' as w2nd; appearances of 'a base' greater than 'a decimal' refers to DIVIDE(SUBTRACT(biwords.occurrences'a base', biwords.occurrences'a decimal'), biwords.occurrences'a decimal')
SQL: SELECT CAST(occurrences AS REAL) / ( SELECT occurrences FROM biwords WHERE w1st = ( SELECT wid FROM words WHERE word = 'a' ) AND w2nd = ( SELECT wid FROM words WHERE word = 'decimal' ) ) FROM biwords WHERE w1st = ( SELECT wid FROM words WHERE word = 'a' ) AND w2nd = ( SELECT wid FROM words WHERE word = 'base' )
gold: SELECT (SELECT occurrences FROM biwords WHERE w1st = (SELECT wid FROM words WHERE word = 'a') AND w2nd = (SELECT wid FROM words WHERE word = 'base')) / (SELECT occurrences FROM biwords WHERE w1st = (SELECT wid FROM words WHERE word = 'a') AND w2nd = (SELECT wid FROM words WHERE word = 'decimal')) AS ratio;

question: For the word "grec", what is the percentage of the appearances in the "Art" Wikipedia page have among all the appearances?
evidence: grec refers to word = 'grec'; Art refers to title = 'Art'; percentage is DIVIDE(occurrences(grec), occurences(Art))*100
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T3.title = 'Art' THEN T2.occurrences ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(T2.occurrences) FROM words AS T1 INNER JOIN pages_words AS T2 ON T1.wid = T2.wid INNER JOIN pages AS T3 ON T2.pid = T3.pid WHERE T1.word = 'grec'
gold: SELECT (SELECT occurrences FROM pages_words WHERE wid = (SELECT wid FROM words WHERE word = 'grec') AND pid = (SELECT pid FROM pages WHERE page = 'Art')) * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(occurrences) FROM pages_words WHERE wid = (SELECT wid FROM words WHERE word = 'grec')) AS percentage;

question: In books authored by Abraham Lincoln, what is the percentage of the books published in 1992?

SQL: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM customer WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM cust_order WHERE order_id IN (SELECT order_id FROM order_line WHERE book_id = (SELECT book_id FROM book WHERE title = 'Fantasmas')));
gold: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM customer WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM cust_order WHERE order_id IN (SELECT order_id FROM order_line WHERE book_id = (SELECT book_id FROM book WHERE title = 'Fantasmas')));

question: How many percent of orders in 2020 used international shipping?
evidence: international shipping refers to method_name = 'International'; orders in 2020 refers to order_date = '2020%'; percentage = Divide (Sum(method_name = 'International'), Count(order_id)) * 100
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.method_name = 'International' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(*) FROM cust_order AS T1 INNER JOIN shipping_method AS T2 ON T1.shipping_method_id = T2.method_id WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.order_date) = '2020'
gold: SELECT (COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE T2.method_name = 'International') * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage FROM cust_order T1 JOIN shipping_method T2 ON T1.shipping_method_id = T2.method_id WHERE strftime('%Y', T1.order_date) = '2020';

question: What is the most common domain for the email address among all the customers?

SQL: SELECT domain FROM (SELECT SUBSTR(email, INSTR(email, '@') + 1) AS domain FROM customer) GROUP BY domain HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(count) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM customer GROUP BY SUBSTR(email, INSTR(email, '@') + 1)));
gold: SELECT domain FROM (SELECT SUBSTR(email, INSTR(email, '@') + 1) AS domain FROM customer) GROUP BY domain HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(count) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM customer GROUP BY SUBSTR(email, INSTR(email, '@') + 1)));

question: How much time does it take to update the status of order "2398"?
evidence: "2398" is the order_id; time =   Subtract(strftime('%Y', status_date), strftime('%Y', order_date)) AS "year" , Subtract(strftime('%m', status_date), strftime('%m', order_date)) AS "month", Subtract (strftime('%d', status_date), strftime('%d', order_date)) AS "day"

gold: SELECT strftime('%Y', T2.status_date) - strftime('%Y', T1.order_date) AS year, strftime('%m', T2.status_date) - strftime('%m', T1.order_date) AS month, strftime('%d', T2.status_date) - strftime('%d', T1.order_date) AS day FROM cust_order T1 JOIN order_history T2 ON T1.order_id = T2.order_id WHERE T1.order_id = 2398;

question: Name the publisher who published the most books.
evidence: published the most books refers to Max(Count(book_id)); publisher refers to publisher_name
SQL: WITH BookCounts AS (SELECT publisher_id, COUNT(book_id) AS total_books FROM book GROUP BY publisher_id) SELECT publisher_name FROM publisher JOIN BookCounts ON publisher.publisher_id = BookCounts.publisher_id WHERE total_books = (SELECT MAX(total_books) FROM BookCounts);

question: What is the title of the first book that was written by A.J. Ayer?

question: What is the percentage of books that cost greater than $10 and were ordered by customer Ruthanne Vatini?

question: Among the books purchased by less than 1 dollar, what is the difference between the number of books with less than 500 pages and books with greater than 500 pages?

SQL: SELECT CAST((T1.UnitPrice - T2.UnitPrice) AS REAL) * 100 / T1.UnitPrice FROM Products AS T1 INNER JOIN `Order Details` AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.OrderID = 10273 AND T1.ProductName = 'Ikura'
gold: SELECT 100 * (P.Price - (SELECT Price FROM OrderDetails WHERE ProductID = P.ProductID AND OrderID = 10273)) / P.Price AS PercentageLower FROM Products P WHERE P.ProductName = 'Ikura';

gold: SELECT AVG(T2.Quantity) FROM Products T1 JOIN OrderDetails T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T1.ProductName = 'Ikura';

question: For the orders of Customer "WHITC", what is the percentage of the orders were fulfilled with shipper company "United Package"?

question: How many percent more orders were fulfilled with shipper company "United Package" than with "Speedy Express"?

SQL: SELECT CAST((COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.CompanyName = 'United Package' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) - COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.CompanyName = 'Speedy Express' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END)) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.CompanyName = 'Speedy Express' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) FROM Orders AS T1 INNER JOIN Shippers AS T2 ON T1.ShipVia = T2.ShipperID
gold: SELECT ((COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.ShipperName = 'United Package' THEN T1.OrderID END) - COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.ShipperName = 'Speedy Express' THEN T1.OrderID END)) * 100.0 / COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.ShipperName = 'Speedy Express' THEN T1.OrderID END)) AS PercentageDifference FROM Orders T1 JOIN Shippers T2 ON T1.ShipperID = T2.ShipperID;

SQL: SELECT T2.CompanyName FROM Orders AS T1 INNER JOIN Shippers AS T2 ON T1.ShipVia = T2.ShipperID WHERE T1.ShipCity = 'Aachen' GROUP BY T2.CompanyName ORDER BY COUNT(T1.ShipVia) DESC LIMIT 1

question: What is the contact name and phone number of the customer who has made the most total payment on the order to date?

SQL: SELECT COUNT(T1.CustomerID) FROM Customers AS T1 INNER JOIN Orders AS T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2.OrderDate) = '1996' AND T1.Country = 'UK'
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders T1 JOIN Customers T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID WHERE strftime('%Y', T1.OrderDate) = '1996' AND T2.Country = 'UK';

question: Which company had the most orders in 1998?

gold: SELECT T2.CustomerName FROM Orders T1 JOIN Customers T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID WHERE strftime('%Y', T1.OrderDate) = '1998' GROUP BY T2.CustomerName ORDER BY COUNT(T1.OrderID) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: How many condiments were sold in 1997?
evidence: "Condiments" is the CategoryName; in 1997 refers to year(OrderDate) = 1997;
SQL: SELECT COUNT(T2.ProductID) FROM Categories AS T1 INNER JOIN Products AS T2 ON T1.CategoryID = T2.CategoryID INNER JOIN `Order Details` AS T3 ON T2.ProductID = T3.ProductID INNER JOIN Orders AS T4 ON T3.OrderID = T4.OrderID WHERE T1.CategoryName = 'Condiments' AND T1.CategoryID = 2 AND T4.OrderDate LIKE '1997%'
gold: SELECT SUM(Quantity) FROM OrderDetails JOIN Products ON OrderDetails.ProductID = Products.ProductID JOIN Categories ON Products.CategoryID = Categories.CategoryID JOIN Orders ON OrderDetails.OrderID = Orders.OrderID WHERE Categories.CategoryName = 'Condiments' AND strftime('%Y', Orders.OrderDate) = '1997';

question: Who is the customer who purchased the highest number of products in a single order?
evidence: highest number of products refers to MAX(COUNT(ProductID))
SQL: SELECT T1.CompanyName FROM Customers AS T1 INNER JOIN Orders AS T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID INNER JOIN `Order Details` AS T3 ON T2.OrderID = T3.OrderID GROUP BY T1.CompanyName ORDER BY COUNT(T3.ProductID) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T3.CustomerName FROM Customers T3 JOIN (SELECT T1.CustomerID, SUM(T2.Quantity) AS TotalQuantity FROM Orders T1 JOIN OrderDetails T2 ON T1.OrderID = T2.OrderID GROUP BY T1.OrderID) T4 ON T3.CustomerID = T4.CustomerID WHERE T4.TotalQuantity = (SELECT MAX(TotalQuantity) FROM (SELECT SUM(Quantity) AS TotalQuantity FROM OrderDetails GROUP BY OrderID) T);

question: What is the monthly average number of products shipped via Federal Shipping for the year 1996?
evidence: monthly average number of products refers to DIVIDE(SUM(OrderID), 12); shipped via Federal Shipping refers to CompanyName = 'Federal Shipping'; for the year 1996 refers to year(ShippedDate) = 1996
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(T1.ShipVia) AS REAL) / 12 FROM Orders AS T1 INNER JOIN Shippers AS T2 ON T1.ShipVia = T2.ShipperID WHERE T2.CompanyName = 'Federal Shipping' AND T1.ShippedDate LIKE '1996%'
gold: SELECT SUM(T3.Quantity) / 12 AS MonthlyAverage FROM Orders T1 JOIN Shippers T2 ON T1.ShipperID = T2.ShipperID JOIN OrderDetails T3 ON T1.OrderID = T3.OrderID WHERE T2.ShipperName = 'Federal Shipping' AND strftime('%Y', T1.OrderDate) = '1996';

question: What is the company name of the customer who made the biggest amount of purchase in a single order before discount?
evidence: biggest amount of purchase in a single order refers to MAX(MULTIPLY(UnitPrice, Quantity)); before discount refers to Discount = 0
SQL: SELECT T1.CompanyName FROM Customers AS T1 INNER JOIN Orders AS T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID INNER JOIN `Order Details` AS T3 ON T2.OrderID = T3.OrderID WHERE T3.Discount = 0 GROUP BY T1.CompanyName ORDER BY SUM(T3.UnitPrice * T3.Quantity) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT CustomerName FROM Customers WHERE CustomerID = (SELECT CustomerID FROM Orders WHERE OrderID = (SELECT OrderID FROM (SELECT OrderID, SUM(Quantity * Price) AS TotalPurchase FROM OrderDetails JOIN Products ON OrderDetails.ProductID = Products.ProductID GROUP BY OrderID ORDER BY TotalPurchase DESC LIMIT 1)));

question: What was the total amount of sales handled by Nancy Davolio in December 1996, excluding discounts?
evidence: in December 1996 refers to year(OrderDate) = 1996 AND month(OrderDate) = 12; excluding discounts refers to Discount = 0; total amount of sales refers to MULTIPLY((UnitPrice, Quantity))

gold: SELECT SUM(T4.Price * T3.Quantity) AS TotalSales FROM Employees T1 JOIN Orders T2 ON T1.EmployeeID = T2.EmployeeID JOIN OrderDetails T3 ON T2.OrderID = T3.OrderID JOIN Products T4 ON T3.ProductID = T4.ProductID WHERE T1.FirstName = 'Nancy' AND T1.LastName = 'Davolio' AND strftime('%Y', T2.OrderDate) = '1996' AND strftime('%m', T2.OrderDate) = '12'

question: What is the total amount of sales made in the year 1997?

gold: SELECT SUM(T3.Price * T2.Quantity) AS TotalSales FROM Orders T1 JOIN OrderDetails T2 ON T1.OrderID = T2.OrderID JOIN Products T3 ON T2.ProductID = T3.ProductID WHERE strftime('%Y', T1.OrderDate) = '1997';

question: What is the average annual amount of shipped sales from 1997 to 1998?

SQL: SELECT SUM(T2.UnitPrice * T2.Quantity * (1 - T2.Discount)) / 3 FROM Orders AS T1 INNER JOIN `Order Details` AS T2 ON T1.OrderID = T2.OrderID WHERE T1.ShippedDate BETWEEN '1996-01-01 00:00:00' AND '1998-12-31 23:59:59'
gold: SELECT AVG(total_sales) FROM (SELECT SUM(T2.Quantity * T3.Price) AS total_sales FROM Orders T1 JOIN OrderDetails T2 ON T1.OrderID = T2.OrderID JOIN Products T3 ON T2.ProductID = T3.ProductID WHERE T1.OrderDate BETWEEN '1997-01-01' AND '1998-12-31' GROUP BY T1.OrderID)

question: Identify the customer, which placed the largest order in terms of value.

question: What is the average value of the sales order?

SQL: SELECT T1.FirstName, T1.LastName, COUNT(T2.OrderID) FROM Employees AS T1 INNER JOIN Orders AS T2 ON T1.EmployeeID = T2.EmployeeID WHERE T1.Title = 'Sales Representative' AND STRFTIME('%Y', T1.HireDate) = '1992' GROUP BY T1.EmployeeID, T1.FirstName, T1.LastName
gold: SELECT T1.EmployeeID, COUNT(T2.OrderID) AS OrderCount FROM Employees T1 LEFT JOIN Orders T2 ON T1.EmployeeID = T2.EmployeeID GROUP BY T1.EmployeeID ORDER BY OrderCount DESC;

question: Calculate the total payment of orders for Vegie-spread product.
evidence: Vegie-spread product refers to ProductName = 'Vegie-spread'；total payment = MULTIPLY(UnitPrice, Quantity, (1-Discount))
SQL: SELECT SUM(T2.UnitPrice * T2.Quantity * (1 - T2.Discount)) AS sum FROM Products AS T1 INNER JOIN `Order Details` AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T1.ProductName = 'Vegie-spread'
gold: SELECT SUM(T1.Price * T2.Quantity) AS TotalPayment FROM Products T1 JOIN OrderDetails T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T1.ProductName = 'Vegie-spread';

question: List down the company names which supplied products for the order on 14th August, 1996.

SQL: SELECT T1.CompanyName FROM Suppliers AS T1 INNER JOIN Products AS T2 ON T1.SupplierID = T2.SupplierID INNER JOIN `Order Details` AS T3 ON T2.ProductID = T3.ProductID INNER JOIN Orders AS T4 ON T3.OrderID = T4.OrderID WHERE date(T4.OrderDate) = '1996-08-14'
gold: SELECT DISTINCT T4.SupplierName FROM Orders T1 JOIN OrderDetails T2 ON T1.OrderID = T2.OrderID JOIN Products T3 ON T2.ProductID = T3.ProductID JOIN Suppliers T4 ON T3.SupplierID = T4.SupplierID WHERE T1.OrderDate = '1996-08-14';

question: Name the shipper which had the most shipments in first quarter of 1998.
evidence: Name the shipper refers to CompanyName; most shipments refers to max(count(OrderID)); first quarter of 1998 refers to ShippedDate = 1998/1 and ShippedDate = 1998/2 and ShippedDate = 1998/3 and ShippedDate = 1998/4
SQL: SELECT T1.CompanyName FROM Shippers AS T1 INNER JOIN Orders AS T2 ON T1.ShipperID = T2.ShipVia WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2.ShippedDate) = '1998' GROUP BY T1.CompanyName ORDER BY COUNT(T2.OrderID) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T2.ShipperName FROM (SELECT ShipperID, COUNT(OrderID) AS TotalOrders FROM Orders WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', OrderDate) IN ('1998-01', '1998-02', '1998-03') GROUP BY ShipperID) AS T1 JOIN Shippers AS T2 ON T1.ShipperID = T2.ShipperID ORDER BY TotalOrders DESC LIMIT 1;

question: Clerk#000000936 dealt with a "Not Specified" order on 1995/3/13, what was the charge for the part of the order shipped by truck?

question: Calculates the profit processed by Supplier No. 7414 on order No. 817154.

SQL: SELECT (l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount) - ps_supplycost * l_quantity) AS profit FROM lineitem T1 JOIN partsupp T2 ON T1.l_partkey = T2.ps_partkey AND T1.l_suppkey = T2.ps_suppkey WHERE T1.l_suppkey = 7414 AND T1.l_orderkey = 817154;

SQL: SELECT T3.p_name, T4.s_name FROM part T3 JOIN partsupp T2 ON T3.p_partkey = T2.ps_partkey JOIN supplier T4 ON T2.ps_suppkey = T4.s_suppkey JOIN lineitem T1 ON T1.l_partkey = T2.ps_partkey AND T1.l_suppkey = T2.ps_suppkey GROUP BY T3.p_name, T4.s_name ORDER BY SUM((T1.l_extendedprice * (1 - T1.l_discount)) - (T2.ps_supplycost * T1.l_quantity)) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T3.p_name, T4.s_name FROM part T3 JOIN partsupp T2 ON T3.p_partkey = T2.ps_partkey JOIN supplier T4 ON T2.ps_suppkey = T4.s_suppkey JOIN lineitem T1 ON T1.l_partkey = T2.ps_partkey AND T1.l_suppkey = T2.ps_suppkey GROUP BY T3.p_name, T4.s_name ORDER BY SUM((T1.l_extendedprice * (1 - T1.l_discount)) - (T2.ps_supplycost * T1.l_quantity)) DESC LIMIT 1

question: What proportion of suppliers are from Asia?

SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(IIF(T1.r_name = 'ASIA', 1, 0)) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.r_regionkey) FROM region AS T1 INNER JOIN nation AS T2 ON T1.r_regionkey = T2.n_regionkey INNER JOIN supplier AS T3 ON T2.n_nationkey = T3.s_nationkey
gold: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T3.r_name = 'ASIA' THEN T1.s_suppkey END) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT T1.s_suppkey)) AS proportion FROM supplier T1 JOIN nation T2 ON T1.s_nationkey = T2.n_nationkey JOIN region T3 ON T2.n_regionkey = T3.r_regionkey;

SQL: SELECT MAX(Rate) FROM EmployeePayHistory WHERE BusinessEntityID IN (SELECT BusinessEntityID FROM Employee WHERE SalariedFlag = 1);
gold: SELECT MAX(Rate) FROM EmployeePayHistory WHERE BusinessEntityID IN (SELECT BusinessEntityID FROM Employee WHERE SalariedFlag = 1);

question: For the employees who have the highest pay frequency, please list their vacation hours.

SQL: SELECT VacationHours FROM Employee WHERE BusinessEntityID IN (SELECT BusinessEntityID FROM EmployeePayHistory WHERE PayFrequency = 2);

question: What is the pay rate of the employee who has the longest vacation hours?

gold: SELECT T2.Rate FROM Employee T1, EmployeePayHistory T2 WHERE T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID AND T1.VacationHours = (SELECT MAX(VacationHours) FROM Employee) AND T2.RateChangeDate = (SELECT MAX(RateChangeDate) FROM EmployeePayHistory WHERE BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID);

question: How many vacation hours do the male employees have on average?
evidence: employee refers to PersonType = 'EM'; Male refers to Gender = 'M'; Average = Divide( SUM(VacationHours(PersonType = 'EM'& Gender = 'M')),Count(BusinessEntityID(PersonType = 'EM' & Gender = 'M')));
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(T1.VacationHours) AS REAL) / COUNT(T1.BusinessEntityID) FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN Person AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.Gender = 'M' AND T2.PersonType = 'EM'
gold: SELECT AVG(E.VacationHours) FROM Employee E JOIN Person P ON E.BusinessEntityID = P.BusinessEntityID WHERE P.PersonType = 'EM' AND E.Gender = 'M';

question: Among the employees who are married and wish to receive e-mail promotions, how much higher is their highest pay rate from the average pay rate?

SQL: SELECT MAX(T3.Rate) - AVG(T3.Rate) FROM Employee T1 JOIN Person T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID JOIN EmployeePayHistory T3 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.MaritalStatus = 'M' AND T2.EmailPromotion = 1;
gold: SELECT MAX(T3.Rate) - AVG(T3.Rate) FROM Employee T1 JOIN Person T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID JOIN EmployeePayHistory T3 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.MaritalStatus = 'M' AND T2.EmailPromotion = 1;

question: If a married employee has a western name style, what is the probability of him or her working as a store contact?
evidence: married refers to MaritalStatus = 'M'; western name style refers to NameStyle = 0; store contact refers to PersonType = 'SC'; probability = Divide (Count (BusinessEntityID( PersonType = 'SC' & MaritalStatus = 'M')), Count (BusinessEntityID ( PersonType) & MariatlStatus = 'M'))
SQL: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Employee T2 JOIN Person T1 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T2.MaritalStatus = 'M' AND T1.NameStyle = 0 AND T1.PersonType = 'SC') / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Employee T2 JOIN Person T1 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T2.MaritalStatus = 'M' AND T1.NameStyle = 0) * 1.0 AS Probability;
gold: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.PersonType = 'SC' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS FLOAT) / COUNT(*) AS Probability FROM Employee T2 JOIN Person T1 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T2.MaritalStatus = 'M' AND T1.NameStyle = 0;

question: Among the active employees with over 10 hours of sick leave, what is the percentage of the employees with over 20 vacation hours?

SQL: SELECT (COUNT(*) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Employee WHERE CurrentFlag = 1 AND SickLeaveHours > 10)) AS Percentage FROM Employee WHERE CurrentFlag = 1 AND VacationHours > 20 AND SickLeaveHours > 10;
gold: SELECT (COUNT(*) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Employee WHERE CurrentFlag = 1 AND SickLeaveHours > 10)) AS Percentage FROM Employee WHERE CurrentFlag = 1 AND VacationHours > 20 AND SickLeaveHours > 10;

gold: SELECT SUM(LastReceiptCost) / COUNT(OnOrderQty) AS AverageLastReceiptCost FROM ProductVendor WHERE AverageLeadTime = 60 AND LastReceiptCost IS NOT NULL;

question: Average cost of purchase orders made during the first six months of 2012.
evidence: purchase orders refers to TransactionType = 'P'; first six months of 2012 refers to TransactionDate bewteen '2012-01-01'and '2012-06-30'; average = DIVIDE(ActualCost where TransactionType = 'P', count(TransactionID))

gold: SELECT AVG(ActualCost) FROM TransactionHistory WHERE TransactionType = 'P' AND TransactionDate BETWEEN '2012-01-01' AND '2012-06-30';

question: What percentage of male employees hired throughout the years 2009 are married?
evidence: male refers to Gender = 'M'; hired throughout the years 2009 refers to Year(HireDate) = 2009; married refers to MaritalStatus = 'M'; percentage = DIVIDE(count(BusinessEntityID(Gender = 'M'& Year(HireDate) = '2009& MaritalStatus = 'M')), count(BusinessEntityID(Gender = 'M'& Year(HireDate) = 2009)))
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN MaritalStatus = 'M' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(BusinessEntityID) FROM Employee WHERE SUBSTR(HireDate, 1, 4) = '2009' AND Gender = 'M'
gold: SELECT (COUNT(CASE WHEN MaritalStatus = 'M' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS Percentage FROM Employee WHERE Gender = 'M' AND strftime('%Y', HireDate) = '2009';

question: What percentage of people named Mary who wants Receive Email promotions of AdventureWorks and selected partners are store contacts?

question: What is the percentage, by number of sales order units, for orders with quantities not greater than 3 and a discount of 0.2?

gold: SELECT (COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE OrderQty <= 3 AND UnitPriceDiscount = 0.2) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS Percentage FROM SalesOrderDetail;

question: What is the credit rating of the company whose average lead time is 16 days for a standard price of 18.9900 and whose last receipt date is August 27, 2011?

question: If we discount the products that do not have any type of offer, how many different products have been sold in an amount greater than 2 units per order?

question: What is the product cost end date with the highest weight in grams?

question: What is the percentage of the total products ordered were not rejected by Drill size?
evidence: rejected quantity refers to ScrappedQty; rejected by Drill size refers to Name in ('Drill size too small','Drill size too large'); percentage = DIVIDE(SUM(ScrappedQty) where Name in('Drill size too small','Drill size too large'), OrderQty)
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.VacationHours > 20 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.BusinessEntityID) FROM EmployeePayHistory AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T2.CurrentFlag = 1 AND T2.SickLeaveHours > 10
gold: SELECT (SUM(T1.ScrappedQty) * 100.0 / SUM(T1.OrderQty)) AS Percentage FROM WorkOrder T1 JOIN ScrapReason T2 ON T1.ScrapReasonID = T2.ScrapReasonID WHERE T2.Name IN ('Drill size too small', 'Drill size too large');

question: Calculate the average of the total ordered quantity of products purchased whose shipping method was Cargo Transport 5.
evidence: shipping method was Cargo Transport 5 refers to Name = 'Cargo Transport 5'; average = DIVIDE(SUM(OrderQty where Name = 'Cargo Transport 5'), COUNT(ShipMethodID))
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(IIF(T1.ShipMethodID = 5, T3.OrderQty, 0)) AS REAL) / COUNT(T3.ProductID) FROM ShipMethod AS T1 INNER JOIN PurchaseOrderHeader AS T2 ON T1.ShipMethodID = T2.ShipMethodID INNER JOIN PurchaseOrderDetail AS T3 ON T2.PurchaseOrderID = T3.PurchaseOrderID
gold: SELECT AVG(T3.OrderQty) AS AverageOrderedQuantity FROM ShipMethod T1 JOIN PurchaseOrderHeader T2 ON T1.ShipMethodID = T2.ShipMethodID JOIN PurchaseOrderDetail T3 ON T2.PurchaseOrderID = T3.PurchaseOrderID WHERE T1.Name = 'Cargo Transport 5';

question: List the name of the rates that apply to the provinces that are in the territory that obtained the greatest increase in sales with respect to the previous year.
evidence: sales of previous year refers to SalesLastYear; SalesYTD refers to year to date sales; increase in sales = DIVIDE(SUBTRACT(SalesYTD, SalesLastYear), SalesLastYear)*100
SQL: SELECT T2.Name FROM SalesTerritory AS T1 INNER JOIN StateProvince AS T2 ON T1.CountryRegionCode = T2.CountryRegionCode INNER JOIN SalesTaxRate AS T3 ON T2.StateProvinceID = T3.StateProvinceID ORDER BY (T1.SalesYTD - T1.SalesLastYear) / T1.SalesLastYear DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T3.Name FROM SalesTerritory T1 JOIN StateProvince T2 ON T1.TerritoryID = T2.TerritoryID JOIN SalesTaxRate T3 ON T2.StateProvinceID = T3.StateProvinceID WHERE T1.TerritoryID = (SELECT TerritoryID FROM SalesTerritory ORDER BY ((SalesYTD - SalesLastYear) / SalesLastYear) DESC LIMIT 1);

question: For the document Control Assistant who was hired on 2009/1/22, what is the percentage of private documents did he/she have?
evidence: Document Control Assistant refers  to the  JobTitle = 'Document Control Assistant'; hired on 2009/1/22 means the person's hiring date is HireDate = '2009-01-22'; private documents indicate that DocumentSummary is null; DIVIDE(COUNT(DocumentSummary is null), COUNT(DocumentSummary))*100
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.DocumentSummary IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / COUNT(T1.DocumentSummary) FROM Document AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.Owner = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T2.JobTitle = 'Document Control Assistant' AND T2.HireDate = '2009-01-22'
gold: SELECT (COUNT(CASE WHEN D.DocumentSummary IS NULL THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS PercentagePrivate FROM Employee E JOIN Document D ON E.BusinessEntityID = D.Owner WHERE E.JobTitle = 'Document Control Assistant' AND E.HireDate = '2009-01-22';

question: How much is HL Grip Tape's profit ratio?

SQL: SELECT (T1.LastReceiptCost - T1.StandardPrice) / T1.StandardPrice FROM ProductVendor AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.Name = 'HL Grip Tape'
gold: SELECT (LastReceiptCost - StandardPrice) / StandardPrice AS profit_ratio FROM Product P JOIN ProductVendor PV ON P.ProductID = PV.ProductID WHERE P.Name = 'HL Grip Tape' AND LastReceiptCost IS NOT NULL AND StandardPrice IS NOT NULL;

question: For all phone numbers, what percentage of the total is cell phone?

gold: SELECT (COUNT(CASE WHEN PhoneNumberTypeID = 1 THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage FROM PhoneNumberType;

question: Who is the top sales person who achived highest percentage of projected sales quota in 2013?

question: Among the employees who wish to receive e-mail promotion from AdventureWorks, how many percent of them are female?

question: How many times is married non sales employees against single non-sales employees?

question: How much is the total bonus received by sales person and what is the percentage of it against the projected yearly sales quota in 2013?
evidence: projected yearly sales quota refers to SalesQuota; projected yearly sales quota in 2013 refers to year(QuotaDate) = 2013; percentage = (MULTIPLY(DIVIDE(SUM(Bonus)), (SUM(SalesQuota))) as percentage;
SQL: SELECT SUM(T1.Bonus) , CAST(SUM(T1.Bonus) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(T1.SalesQuota) FROM SalesPerson AS T1 INNER JOIN SalesPersonQuotaHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2.QuotaDate) = '2013'
gold: SELECT SUM(Bonus) AS TotalBonus, (SUM(Bonus) / (SELECT SUM(SalesQuota) FROM SalesPersonQuotaHistory WHERE strftime('%Y', QuotaDate) = '2013')) * 100 AS Percentage FROM SalesPerson;

question: What is the current payrate of Rob Walters? Calculate the percentage increment from his previous payrate.
evidence: current payrate refers to max(Rate); percentage increment = divide(subtract(max(Rate), min(Rate)), min(Rate))*100%
SQL: SELECT T2.Rate , (MAX(T2.Rate) - MIN(T2.Rate)) * 100 / MAX(T2.Rate) FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeePayHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.FirstName = 'Rob' AND T1.LastName = 'Walters'
gold: SELECT ((MAX(Rate) - MIN(Rate)) / MIN(Rate)) * 100 AS PercentageIncrement FROM EmployeePayHistory WHERE BusinessEntityID = (SELECT BusinessEntityID FROM Person WHERE FirstName = 'Rob' AND LastName = 'Walters')

question: Calculate the average length of employment for employee working in the Research and Development deparment.
evidence: average length of employment = AVG(subtract(2022, year(HireDate)))
SQL: SELECT AVG(STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', T1.HireDate)) FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Department AS T3 ON T2.DepartmentID = T3.DepartmentID WHERE T3.Name = 'Research and Development'
gold: SELECT AVG(2022 - CAST(strftime('%Y', E.HireDate) AS INTEGER)) AS AvgLengthOfEmployment FROM Employee E JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory EDH ON E.BusinessEntityID = EDH.BusinessEntityID JOIN Department D ON EDH.DepartmentID = D.DepartmentID WHERE D.Name = 'Research and Development';

question: What is the average age of employee in Adventure Works?
evidence: average age = AVG(subtract(year(now), year(HireDate)))
SQL: SELECT AVG(STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', BirthDate)) FROM Employee
gold: SELECT AVG(2023 - strftime('%Y', BirthDate)) AS AverageAge FROM Employee WHERE CurrentFlag = 1;

question: Among the employees in Adventure Works, calculate the percentage of them working as sales representatives.
evidence: percentage of sales representatives = divide(count(JobTitle = 'Sales Representative'), count(JobTitle))*100%
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN JobTitle = 'Sales Representative' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(BusinessEntityID) FROM Employee
gold: SELECT (COUNT(CASE WHEN JobTitle = 'Sales Representative' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS PercentageOfSalesReps FROM Employee;

question: Calculate the average age of employee in each department and state which department has the youngest employees.
evidence: Average = Divide(Sum(Substract(year(@today),year(BirthDate))),Count(BusinessEntityID) by each Department ID; youngest employee refers to Min(BirthDate);
SQL: SELECT STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', T1.BirthDate) + 1 , T3.Name FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 USING (BusinessEntityID) INNER JOIN Department AS T3 USING (DepartmentID) ORDER BY T1.BirthDate DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T3.Name, MIN(T1.avg_age) FROM (SELECT T2.DepartmentID, AVG(strftime('%Y', 'now') - strftime('%Y', T1.BirthDate)) AS avg_age FROM Employee AS T1 JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID GROUP BY T2.DepartmentID) AS T1 JOIN Department AS T3 ON T1.DepartmentID = T3.DepartmentID GROUP BY T3.Name ORDER BY MIN(T1.avg_age) ASC LIMIT 1;

question: What is the difference in percentage between the product descriptions written in Arabic and Thai?
evidence: Arabic and Thai are language names refers to name = 'Arabic'and name = 'Thai'; Differencce in percentage = Subtract(((Count(CultureID(name = 'Arabic'))/Count(CultureID))*100),((Count(CultureID(name = 'Thai'))/Count(CultureID))*100)));
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.Name = 'Arabic' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN T1.Name = 'Thai' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM Culture AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductModelProductDescriptionCulture AS T2 ON T1.CultureID = T2.CultureID
gold: SELECT ABS((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ProductModelProductDescriptionCulture WHERE CultureID = (SELECT CultureID FROM Culture WHERE Name = 'Arabic')) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ProductModelProductDescriptionCulture) - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ProductModelProductDescriptionCulture WHERE CultureID = (SELECT CultureID FROM Culture WHERE Name = 'Thai')) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ProductModelProductDescriptionCulture)) AS PercentageDifference;

question: What percentage of businesses in the Northwest US have forecasted annual sales of above 300,000?
evidence: Northwest refers to Name = 'Northwest'; US refers to CountryRegionCode = 'US'; forecasted annual sales of above 300,000 refers to SalesQuota >300000; Percentage = Divide(Count(TerritoryID(SalesQuota >300000)),Count(TerritoryID))*100
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T1.SalesQuota > 300000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.BusinessEntityID) FROM SalesPerson AS T1 INNER JOIN SalesTerritory AS T2 ON T1.TerritoryID = T2.TerritoryID WHERE T2.CountryRegionCode = 'US' AND T2.Name = 'Northwest'
gold: SELECT (COUNT(*) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SalesPerson SP JOIN SalesTerritory ST ON SP.TerritoryID = ST.TerritoryID WHERE ST.Name = 'Northwest' AND ST.CountryRegionCode = 'US')) AS Percentage FROM SalesPerson SP JOIN SalesTerritory ST ON SP.TerritoryID = ST.TerritoryID WHERE ST.Name = 'Northwest' AND ST.CountryRegionCode = 'US' AND SP.SalesQuota > 300000;

question: How much profit can the company gained from selling two high class black Road Bikes with a size of 58?

question: For all the employees that have left the Engineering Department, what is the average time of their stay?
evidence: employees who left a department refers to EndDate NOT null; average stay = AVG(SUBTRACT(year(EndDate)), (year(T1.StartDate)));
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(365 * (STRFTIME('%Y', T1.EndDate) - STRFTIME('%Y', T1.StartDate)) + 30 * (STRFTIME('%m', T1.EndDate) - STRFTIME('%m', T1.StartDate)) + STRFTIME('%d', T1.EndDate) - STRFTIME('%d', T1.StartDate)) AS REAL) / COUNT(T1.BusinessEntityID) FROM EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T1 INNER JOIN Department AS T2 ON T1.DepartmentID = T2.DepartmentID WHERE T2.Name = 'Engineering' AND T1.EndDate IS NOT NULL
gold: SELECT AVG((strftime('%Y', T1.EndDate) - strftime('%Y', T1.StartDate))) AS AverageStay FROM EmployeeDepartmentHistory T1 INNER JOIN Department T2 ON T1.DepartmentID = T2.DepartmentID WHERE T2.Name = 'Engineering' AND T1.EndDate IS NOT NULL;

question: What is the average pay rate of the employees who worked in the Engineering Departmentin 2007?
evidence: average pay rate = AVG(Rate); work in 2007 refers to year(StartDate)<2007 AND year(EndDate)>2007;
SQL: SELECT AVG(T3.Rate) FROM EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T1 INNER JOIN Department AS T2 ON T1.DepartmentID = T2.DepartmentID INNER JOIN EmployeePayHistory AS T3 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID WHERE T2.Name = 'Engineering' AND STRFTIME('%Y', EndDate) > '2007' AND STRFTIME('%Y', T1.StartDate) < '2007'
gold: SELECT AVG(Rate) FROM EmployeePayHistory WHERE BusinessEntityID IN (SELECT BusinessEntityID FROM EmployeeDepartmentHistory WHERE DepartmentID = (SELECT DepartmentID FROM Department WHERE Name = 'Engineering') AND StartDate < '2007-01-01' AND (EndDate > '2007-12-31' OR EndDate IS NULL));

question: How much more expensive in percentage is the product with the highest selling price from the product with the lowest selling price in the Clothing category?

SQL: SELECT (MAX(T1.ListPrice) - MIN(T1.ListPrice)) * 100 / MIN(T1.ListPrice) FROM Product AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductSubcategory AS T2 ON T1.ProductSubcategoryID = T2.ProductSubcategoryID INNER JOIN ProductCategory AS T3 ON T2.ProductCategoryID = T3.ProductCategoryID WHERE T3.Name = 'Clothing'

question: What is the average profit of all the products from the Clothing category?
evidence: average profit = DIVIDE(SUM(SUBTRACT(ListPrice, StandardCost))), (COUNT(ProductSubcategoryID))));
SQL: SELECT SUM(T1.ListPrice - T1.StandardCost) / COUNT(T1.ProductID) FROM Product AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductSubcategory AS T2 ON T1.ProductSubcategoryID = T2.ProductSubcategoryID INNER JOIN ProductCategory AS T3 ON T2.ProductCategoryID = T3.ProductCategoryID WHERE T3.Name = 'Clothing'

question: Who is the youngest goalie among those who had more than 150 goal againsts in 2002 season?

question: In the history of team id NJD, which goalie saved the most goal attempts? Give his full name.

question: Which teams had the most postseason empty net goals in 2010 season? List their team names.
evidence: most postseason empty net goals refers to max(PostENG)
SQL: SELECT T2.name FROM Goalies AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID WHERE T1.year = 2010 GROUP BY T2.name ORDER BY SUM(PostENG) DESC LIMIT 1

question: For the team which had the most postseason shutouts in 1995, how many points did they have that year?

question: Which coach had the highest winning rates in the 2009 season? What's coach's nickname.
evidence: the highest winning rate refer to divide(W, sum(W, L))
SQL: WITH WinningRates AS (SELECT coachID, CAST(w AS REAL) / (w + l) AS rate FROM Coaches WHERE year = 2009 AND w IS NOT NULL AND l IS NOT NULL) SELECT M.nameNick FROM WinningRates WR JOIN Master M ON WR.coachID = M.coachID WHERE WR.rate = (SELECT MAX(rate) FROM WinningRates);
gold: WITH WinningRates AS (SELECT coachID, CAST(w AS REAL) / (w + l) AS rate FROM Coaches WHERE year = 2009 AND w IS NOT NULL AND l IS NOT NULL) SELECT M.nameNick FROM WinningRates WR JOIN Master M ON WR.coachID = M.coachID WHERE WR.rate = (SELECT MAX(rate) FROM WinningRates);

question: For the team had the biggest power play percentage in 2011, who was their coach that season? Give the full name.

SQL: SELECT M.firstName || ' ' || M.lastName AS fullName FROM (SELECT T.tmID FROM TeamsPost T WHERE T.year = 2011 AND T.PPG IS NOT NULL AND T.PPC IS NOT NULL ORDER BY CAST(T.PPG AS FLOAT) / CAST(T.PPC AS FLOAT) DESC LIMIT 1) AS MaxTeam JOIN Coaches C ON MaxTeam.tmID = C.tmID AND C.year = 2011 JOIN Master M ON C.coachID = M.coachID;
gold: SELECT M.firstName || ' ' || M.lastName AS fullName FROM (SELECT T.tmID FROM TeamsPost T WHERE T.year = 2011 AND T.PPG IS NOT NULL AND T.PPC IS NOT NULL ORDER BY CAST(T.PPG AS FLOAT) / CAST(T.PPC AS FLOAT) DESC LIMIT 1) AS MaxTeam JOIN Coaches C ON MaxTeam.tmID = C.tmID AND C.year = 2011 JOIN Master M ON C.coachID = M.coachID;

question: For he who had the highest plus / minus on the court in the 1981 season, what's his full name?
evidence: highest Plus/minus refers to MAX(+/-); full name refers to firstName, lastName; 1981 season refers to year = '1981'
SQL: SELECT T1.firstName, T1.lastName FROM Master AS T1 INNER JOIN Scoring AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.year = 1981 GROUP BY T2.playerID ORDER BY SUM(T2.`+/-`) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT firstName, lastName FROM Master WHERE playerID IN (SELECT playerID FROM Scoring WHERE year = 1981 AND CAST("+/-" AS INTEGER) = (SELECT MAX(CAST("+/-" AS INTEGER)) FROM Scoring WHERE year = 1981))

question: What's the weight of the player who had the most Power Play Goals in the 21st century?
evidence: 21st century refers to year >2000; Power play goals refers to PPG
SQL: SELECT M.weight FROM Master M, (SELECT playerID, SUM(CAST(PPG AS INTEGER)) AS TotalPPG FROM Scoring WHERE year > 2000 GROUP BY playerID) S WHERE M.playerID = S.playerID ORDER BY S.TotalPPG DESC LIMIT 1;
gold: SELECT T2.weight FROM (SELECT playerID, SUM(CAST(PPG AS INTEGER)) AS TotalPPG FROM Scoring WHERE year > 2000 GROUP BY playerID ORDER BY TotalPPG DESC LIMIT 1) T1 JOIN Master T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID;

question: For the player who scored 7 shorthanded goals in 1989, what's his dominant hand?
evidence: 1989 refers to the year of scoring; "dominant hand" and "shooting hand" are synonyms which refers to shootCatch
SQL: SELECT T1.shootCatch FROM Master AS T1 INNER JOIN Scoring AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.year = 1989 GROUP BY T2.playerID HAVING SUM(T2.SHG) = 7
gold: SELECT shootCatch FROM Master WHERE playerID IN (SELECT playerID FROM Scoring WHERE SHG = '7' AND year = 1989);

question: Who was the most clutch player in 1986? Give his full name.
evidence: clutch player' and 'trustworthy player in the critical moment' are synonyms; most clutch player refers to the most trustworthy player which refers to MAX(GWG); 1986 is the year played
SQL: SELECT T1.firstName, T1.lastName FROM Master AS T1 INNER JOIN Scoring AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.year = 1986 GROUP BY T2.playerID ORDER BY SUM(T2.GWG) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T2.firstName, T2.lastName FROM Scoring T1 JOIN Master T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T1.year = 1986 GROUP BY T1.playerID ORDER BY SUM(T1.GWG) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: How many shots on goal did Cam Neely had in the year of 1990?
evidence: 1990 refers to the year played; Shot on goal refers to SOG
SQL: SELECT T2.SOG FROM Master AS T1 INNER JOIN Scoring AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T1.firstName = 'Cam' AND T1.lastName = 'Neely' AND T2.year = '1990'
gold: SELECT SUM(SOG) FROM Scoring WHERE playerID IN (SELECT playerID FROM Master WHERE firstName = 'Cam' AND lastName = 'Neely') AND year = 1990;

question: Who was the coach for the team which had the most bench minors penalty in 2003？
evidence: Coach of the team refers to firstName+lastName; 2003 refers to the year
SQL: SELECT M.firstName || ' ' || M.lastName AS coachName FROM Teams T1 JOIN Coaches T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year JOIN Master M ON T2.coachID = M.coachID WHERE T1.year = 2003 AND T1.BenchMinor = (SELECT MAX(BenchMinor) FROM Teams WHERE year = 2003);
gold: SELECT M.firstName || ' ' || M.lastName AS coachName FROM Teams T1 JOIN Coaches T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year JOIN Master M ON T2.coachID = M.coachID WHERE T1.year = 2003 AND T1.BenchMinor = (SELECT MAX(BenchMinor) FROM Teams WHERE year = 2003);

question: For the goalies whose weight are above 190, who had most goal againsts in 1978 season?
evidence: Weight of above 190 refers to weight >190; 1978 season refers to the year played
SQL: SELECT T1.playerID FROM Master T1 JOIN Goalies T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.year = 1978 AND CAST(T1.weight AS INTEGER) > 190 GROUP BY T1.playerID ORDER BY SUM(CAST(T2.GA AS INTEGER)) DESC LIMIT 1;
gold: SELECT T1.playerID FROM Master T1 JOIN Goalies T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.year = 1978 AND CAST(T1.weight AS INTEGER) > 190 GROUP BY T1.playerID ORDER BY SUM(CAST(T2.GA AS INTEGER)) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: What is the percentage of winning rate of improvement since Alain Vigneault became the coach of Vancouver Canucks in 2006 season?
evidence:
winning rate refers to DIVIDE (w, SUM(w, l)); Vancouver Canucks is name of team where tmID = 'VAN'
Winning rate refers to DIVIDE(wins in year = '2005/2006'(ADD(wins+loses); improvement refers to SUBTRACT(DIVIDE(wins in year = '2005'(ADD(wins+loses), DIVIDE(wins in year = '2006'(ADD(wins+loses))
SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T1.year = 2006 THEN CAST(T1.W AS REAL) * 100 / (T1.W + T1.L) ELSE 0 END) - ( SELECT CAST(W AS REAL) * 100 / (W + L) FROM Teams WHERE year = '2005' AND name = 'Vancouver Canucks' ) FROM Teams AS T1 INNER JOIN Coaches AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year INNER JOIN Master AS T3 ON T2.coachID = T3.coachID WHERE T1.name = 'Vancouver Canucks' AND T3.firstName = 'Alain' AND T3.lastName = 'Vigneault'
gold: SELECT ((SELECT CAST(W AS FLOAT) / (W + L) FROM Teams WHERE tmID = 'VAN' AND year = 2006) - (SELECT CAST(W AS FLOAT) / (W + L) FROM Teams WHERE tmID = 'VAN' AND year = 2005)) * 100 AS improvement_percentage;

question: For the goalie who had the highest defensive success rate in the postseason of 2011, what's his legends ID ?
evidence:
Post season of 2011 refers to year = ’2011’
defensive success rate refers to (SUBTRACT(1 (DIVIDE(PostGA/PostSA)), *100%)
SQL: SELECT T2.legendsID FROM Goalies AS T1 INNER JOIN Master AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T1.year = 2011 ORDER BY 1 - CAST(T1.PostGA AS REAL) / T1.PostSA DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT legendsID FROM Master WHERE playerID = (SELECT playerID FROM Goalies WHERE year = 2011 AND PostGA IS NOT NULL AND PostSA IS NOT NULL ORDER BY (1 - CAST(PostGA AS FLOAT) / CAST(PostSA AS FLOAT)) DESC LIMIT 1)

question: How many former athletes go on to become coaches after retiring?
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT playerID) FROM Master WHERE playerID IS NOT NULL AND coachID IS NOT NULL;
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT playerID) FROM Master WHERE playerID IS NOT NULL AND coachID IS NOT NULL;

question: Among the teams with the most number of ties, how many penalty was committed by a player or coach that is not on the ice? Indicate the name of the team.
evidence: penalty refers to BenchMinor; Ties refer to T
SQL: SELECT BenchMinor, name FROM Teams ORDER BY T DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T1.name, T1.BenchMinor FROM Teams T1 WHERE T1.T = (SELECT MAX(T) FROM Teams) AND T1.BenchMinor IS NOT NULL;

question: Which NHL award was most frequently won by the coach with the most wins?
SQL: SELECT award FROM Teams AS T1 INNER JOIN AwardsCoaches AS T2 ON T1.lgID = T2.lgID WHERE T1.lgID = 'NHL' GROUP BY T2.coachID, T2.award ORDER BY COUNT(T2.award) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT award FROM AwardsCoaches WHERE coachID IN (SELECT coachID FROM Coaches WHERE lgID = 'NHL' GROUP BY coachID HAVING SUM(w) = (SELECT MAX(total_wins) FROM (SELECT SUM(w) AS total_wins FROM Coaches WHERE lgID = 'NHL' GROUP BY coachID))) GROUP BY award ORDER BY COUNT(award) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: What is the power play percentage of the team with the most number of loses?
evidence: Power play percentage refers to PPG, most number of loses refers to MAX(L)
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(PPG) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(PPC) FROM Teams GROUP BY tmID ORDER BY SUM(L) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT CAST(PPG AS INTEGER) * 1.0 / CAST(PPC AS INTEGER) AS PP_Percentage FROM Teams WHERE L = (SELECT MAX(L) FROM Teams) AND PPG IS NOT NULL AND PPC IS NOT NULL;

question: How many players were included in the Hall of Fame on average between 1950 and 1980?
evidence: year BETWEEN 1950 and 1980; average = DIVIDE(COUNT(hofID)), 30)
SQL: SELECT AVG(count) FROM (SELECT COUNT(hofID) AS count FROM HOF WHERE year BETWEEN 1950 AND 1980 AND category = 'Player' GROUP BY year);
gold: SELECT COUNT(hofID) / 31.0 AS average_players FROM HOF WHERE year >= 1950 AND year <= 1980 AND category = 'Player';

question: Which country produced the most number of hockey players? Identify which year was most of the hockey players are born.
evidence: Year most hockey players were born refers to MAX(birthYear); birthCountry refers to the country where a player was born
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT birthCountry, birthYear FROM Master GROUP BY birthCountry, birthYear ORDER BY COUNT(birthCountry) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT birthYear FROM Master GROUP BY birthYear ORDER BY COUNT(birthYear) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: How many wins does the team have whose goaltender have the most number of successfully stopping the other team from scoring during the entire game?
evidence: Number of wins refers to W; Shutout refers to SHO; a shutout is credited to a goaltender who successfully stops the other team from scoring during the entire game.
SQL: SELECT T2.W FROM Teams T2 WHERE T2.tmID = (SELECT T1.tmID FROM (SELECT G.tmID, SUM(CAST(G.SHO AS INTEGER)) AS TotalSHO FROM Goalies G GROUP BY G.tmID) T1 ORDER BY T1.TotalSHO DESC LIMIT 1);
gold: SELECT T.W FROM Teams T INNER JOIN (SELECT G.year, G.tmID, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(CAST(G.SHO AS INTEGER)) DESC) AS rank FROM Goalies G GROUP BY G.year, G.tmID) Ranked ON T.year = Ranked.year AND T.tmID = Ranked.tmID WHERE Ranked.rank = 1

question: Which team recorded the most number of road victories in 2005? Indicate the team ID.
evidence: road victories refers to rW; team id refers to tmID; victories and wins are synonyms
SQL: SELECT T.tmID FROM TeamSplits T WHERE T.year = 2005 AND T.rW = (SELECT MAX(rW) FROM TeamSplits WHERE year = 2005 AND rW IS NOT NULL);
gold: SELECT T.tmID FROM TeamSplits T WHERE T.year = 2005 AND T.rW = (SELECT MAX(rW) FROM TeamSplits WHERE year = 2005 AND rW IS NOT NULL);

question: What is the position of the 9th oldest hockey player?
evidence: position refers to pos; date of birth refers to birthDay + birthMon + birthYear
SQL: SELECT pos FROM Master WHERE birthYear IS NOT NULL AND birthMon IS NOT NULL AND birthDay IS NOT NULL ORDER BY CAST(birthYear AS INTEGER), CAST(birthMon AS INTEGER), CAST(birthDay AS INTEGER) LIMIT 1 OFFSET 8
gold: SELECT pos FROM Master WHERE birthYear IS NOT NULL AND birthMon IS NOT NULL AND birthDay IS NOT NULL ORDER BY CAST(birthYear AS INTEGER), CAST(birthMon AS INTEGER), CAST(birthDay AS INTEGER) LIMIT 1 OFFSET 8

question: How many goals were scored while the goalkeeper was on the ice in the 1924 WCHL by the goalie with the most goals scored?

SQL: SELECT MAX(CAST(PostGA AS INTEGER)) FROM Goalies WHERE year = 1924 AND lgID = 'WCHL';
gold: SELECT MAX(CAST(PostGA AS INTEGER)) FROM Goalies WHERE year = 1924 AND lgID = 'WCHL';

question: In 2006, what is the overall number of october defeats for the team with the most October defeats? Indicate the team ID.
