SQL: SELECT OctL, tmID FROM TeamSplits WHERE year = '2006' ORDER BY OctL DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T.tmID, MAX(T.OctL+0) AS HighestLosses FROM TeamSplits T WHERE T.year = 2006 GROUP BY T.tmID HAVING HighestLosses = (SELECT MAX(CAST(OctL AS INTEGER)) FROM TeamSplits WHERE year = 2006);

question: How many players, whose shooting/catching hand is both left and right, debuted their first NHL in 2011?
evidence: shooting/catching hand is both left and right refers to shootCatch is NULL, debuted their first NHL in 2011 refers to firstNHL = 2011
SQL: SELECT COUNT(playerID) FROM Master WHERE shootCatch IS NULL AND firstNHL = '2011'
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Master WHERE shootCatch IS NULL AND firstNHL = '2011';

question: Which year recorded the most number of goals by a player and how old was the player at the time the most number of goals was achieved by him?
evidence: most number of goals refers to max(G); how old refers to age = subtract(year(max(G)), birthYear)
SQL: SELECT T1.year, T1.year - T2.birthYear FROM Scoring AS T1 INNER JOIN Master AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID GROUP BY T1.year, T1.year - T2.birthYear ORDER BY SUM(T1.G) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T1.year, T1.year - T2.birthYear AS age FROM Scoring T1 JOIN Master T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T1.G = (SELECT MAX(G) FROM Scoring) AND T1.year IS NOT NULL AND T2.birthYear IS NOT NULL;

question: What is the total amount of assists of the NHL player with the most assists in history? Please indicate his/her full name.
evidence: NHL refers to lgID = 'NHL'; most assists refers to max(A); full name = nameGiven + lastName; total amount of assists = sum(A(playerID(max(A))))
SQL: SELECT M.nameGiven || ' ' || M.lastName AS fullName, MAX(totalAssists) FROM (SELECT S.playerID, SUM(S.A) AS totalAssists FROM Scoring S WHERE S.lgID = 'NHL' GROUP BY S.playerID) AS SubQuery JOIN Master M ON SubQuery.playerID = M.playerID;
gold: SELECT M.nameGiven || ' ' || M.lastName AS fullName, totalAssists FROM (SELECT playerID, SUM(A) AS totalAssists FROM Scoring WHERE lgID = 'NHL' GROUP BY playerID) AS PlayerAssists JOIN Master M ON PlayerAssists.playerID = M.playerID WHERE totalAssists = (SELECT MAX(totalAssists) FROM (SELECT SUM(A) AS totalAssists FROM Scoring WHERE lgID = 'NHL' GROUP BY playerID) AS MaxAssists);

question: What is the power play percentage of the team with the least number of penalty kill chances and to which team were they playing against? Indicate whether the team lost or victorious.
evidence: least number of penalty kill chances refers to min(PKC); power play percentage refers to (PP%) = divide(PPG, PPC); team playing refers to tmID; victorious team refers to tmIDWinner; team victorious refers to tmID = tmIDWinner and vice versa
SQL: SELECT SUM(T1.A), T2.firstName, T2.lastName FROM Scoring AS T1 INNER JOIN Master AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T1.lgID = 'NHL' GROUP BY T2.firstName, T2.lastName ORDER BY SUM(T1.A) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: WITH MinPKCTeam AS (SELECT tmID, year FROM TeamsPost WHERE PKC = (SELECT MIN(PKC) FROM TeamsPost)) SELECT T.tmID, T.PPG / T.PPC AS PP_Percentage, CASE WHEN SP.tmIDWinner = T.tmID THEN 'Victorious' ELSE 'Lost' END AS Result FROM Teams T JOIN MinPKCTeam M ON T.tmID = M.tmID AND T.year = M.year LEFT JOIN SeriesPost SP ON SP.year = T.year AND (SP.tmIDWinner = T.tmID OR SP.tmIDLoser = T.tmID);

question: What are the awards won by the coach who coached the team with the most number of victories of all time? Indicate the choach ID.
evidence: victories' and 'wins' are synonyms; most number of victories refers to max(w)
SQL: SELECT AC.coachID, AC.award FROM AwardsCoaches AC WHERE AC.coachID IN (SELECT C.coachID FROM Coaches C WHERE (C.year, C.tmID) IN (SELECT year, tmID FROM Teams WHERE W = (SELECT MAX(W) FROM Teams)));
gold: SELECT AC.coachID, AC.award FROM AwardsCoaches AC WHERE AC.coachID IN (SELECT C.coachID FROM Coaches C WHERE (C.year, C.tmID) IN (SELECT year, tmID FROM Teams WHERE W = (SELECT MAX(W) FROM Teams)));

question: How long has the NHL player been playing during the year when he recorded the least number of times being on the ice when a goal is scored for the team versus against the team? Indicate his full name.
evidence: NHL refers to lgID = 'NHL'; least number of times being on the ice when a goal is scored for the team versus against the team refers to min(+/-); duration the player's been playing = subtract(year(playerID(min(+/-))), firstNHL(playerID(min(+/-)))); full name = nameGiven + lastName
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT T3.firstNHL - T1.year, T3.nameGiven , T3.firstName, T3.lastName FROM Scoring AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T2.tmID = T1.tmID INNER JOIN Master AS T3 ON T1.playerID = T3.playerID GROUP BY T3.firstName, T3.lastName, T3.nameGiven, T3.firstNHL - T1.year, T3.firstName, T3.lastName ORDER BY SUM(T1.`+/-`) ASC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT M.firstName || ' ' || M.lastName AS fullName, (S.year - M.firstNHL) AS playingDuration FROM Scoring S JOIN Master M ON S.playerID = M.playerID WHERE S.lgID = 'NHL' AND S."+/-" = (SELECT MIN("+/-") FROM Scoring WHERE lgID = 'NHL')

question: Between 2003 to 2005, what are the given names of the players with the most number of games played whose Penalty minutes is between 200 to 250?
evidence: penalty minutes refers to PIM; year of scoring BETWEEN 2003 AND 2005; most number of games played refers to max(GP)
SQL: SELECT T2.nameGiven FROM Scoring AS T1 INNER JOIN Master AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID AND T1.PIM BETWEEN 200 AND 250 AND T1.year BETWEEN 2003 AND 2005 ORDER BY T1.GP DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T2.firstName FROM (SELECT playerID, SUM(GP) AS totalGames FROM Scoring WHERE year BETWEEN 2003 AND 2005 AND PIM BETWEEN 200 AND 250 GROUP BY playerID) AS T1 JOIN Master AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T1.totalGames = (SELECT MAX(totalGames) FROM (SELECT SUM(GP) AS totalGames FROM Scoring WHERE year BETWEEN 2003 AND 2005 AND PIM BETWEEN 200 AND 250 GROUP BY playerID))

question: How old was the goaltender who scored the fewest goals while on the ice when he retired from the NHL?
evidence: goaltender' and 'goalie' are synonyms; fewest goals while on the ice refers to min(GA); How old = subtract(lastNHL(playerID(min(GA))), birthYear(playerID(min(GA)))))
SQL: SELECT (CAST(T2.lastNHL AS INTEGER) - CAST(T2.birthYear AS INTEGER)) AS Age FROM Master T2 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Goalies T1 WHERE T1.playerID = T2.playerID AND T1.GA = (SELECT MIN(GA) FROM Goalies WHERE GA IS NOT NULL));
gold: SELECT (CAST(T2.lastNHL AS INTEGER) - CAST(T2.birthYear AS INTEGER)) AS Age FROM Master T2 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Goalies T1 WHERE T1.playerID = T2.playerID AND T1.GA = (SELECT MIN(GA) FROM Goalies WHERE GA IS NOT NULL));

question: Which position has won the most awards and who is the most recent player that was awarded with an award in that position? Indicate the name of the award and the full name of the player.
evidence: position has won the most awards refers to pos(max(count(award))); most recent player refers to playerID(pos(max(count(award)))& max(year)); full name = nameGiven + lastName
SQL: SELECT T1.pos, T2.award, T1.nameGiven, T1.lastName FROM Master AS T1 INNER JOIN AwardsCoaches AS T2 ON T2.coachID = T1.coachID GROUP BY T1.pos, T2.award, T1.nameGiven, T1.lastName ORDER BY COUNT(T2.award) LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T2.nameGiven || ' ' || T2.lastName AS fullName, T1.award FROM AwardsPlayers T1 JOIN Master T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T1.pos = (SELECT pos FROM (SELECT pos, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM AwardsPlayers GROUP BY pos ORDER BY cnt DESC LIMIT 1)) AND T1.year = (SELECT MAX(year) FROM AwardsPlayers WHERE pos = (SELECT pos FROM (SELECT pos, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM AwardsPlayers GROUP BY pos ORDER BY cnt DESC LIMIT 1)))

question: How many games did the coach who received the first-ever Second Team All-Star award play before receiving such award?
evidence: first-ever Second Team All-Star award refers to min(year(award = 'Second Team All-Star')); How many games before receiving such award = sum(g(coachID(min(year(award = 'Second Team All-Star')))): g(min(year)))
SQL: SELECT SUM(T1.g) FROM Coaches AS T1 INNER JOIN ( SELECT coachID, year FROM AwardsCoaches WHERE award = 'Second Team All-Star' ORDER BY year LIMIT 1 ) AS T2 ON T1.coachID = T2.coachID AND T1.year < T2.year
gold: SELECT SUM(C.g) FROM Coaches C WHERE C.coachID IN (SELECT A.coachID FROM AwardsCoaches A WHERE A.award = 'Second Team All-Star' AND A.year = (SELECT MIN(year) FROM AwardsCoaches WHERE award = 'Second Team All-Star')) AND C.year < (SELECT MIN(year) FROM AwardsCoaches WHERE award = 'Second Team All-Star');

question:
How many teams did the team with the most victories in 1915 play against?
Indicate the name of the team who won the most games in 1915, as well as the names of the opposing team.
evidence: team playing refers to tmID; oppositng team refers to oppID; victories' and 'wins' are synonyms; most victories refers to max(w)
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT oppID), T2.tmID, T2.oppID FROM Teams AS T1 INNER JOIN TeamVsTeam AS T2 ON T1.year = T2.year AND T1.tmID = T2.tmID WHERE T2.year = 1915 GROUP BY T2.tmID, T2.oppID ORDER BY SUM(T2.W) DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T.tmID, COUNT(DISTINCT T2.oppID) FROM Teams T JOIN TeamVsTeam T2 ON T.tmID = T2.tmID AND T.year = T2.year WHERE T.year = 1915 AND T.W = (SELECT MAX(W) FROM Teams WHERE year = 1915) GROUP BY T.tmID;

question: Among the teams whose shorthanded goals are between 1 to 5, which player is the most trustworthy in the critical moment?
evidence: shorthanded goals refers to SHG; SHG BETWEEN 1 AND 5; most trustworthy in the critical moment refers to max(GWG)
SQL: SELECT T2.nameGiven, T2.lastName FROM Scoring AS T1 INNER JOIN Master AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T1.SHG BETWEEN 1 AND 5 ORDER BY T1.GWG DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT S.playerID FROM Scoring S JOIN Teams T ON S.year = T.year AND S.tmID = T.tmID WHERE T.SHF BETWEEN 1 AND 5 GROUP BY S.playerID ORDER BY SUM(S.GWG) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: In 1997, how many loss did the coach have who temporary coached Tampa Bay Lightning? Indicate his/her coach ID.
evidence: temporary coached refers to notes = 'interim'; number of loss refers to L (to add)
SQL: SELECT SUM(T1.l), T1.coachID FROM Coaches AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year WHERE T1.notes = 'interim' AND T1.year = '1997' AND T2.name = 'Tampa Bay Lightning' GROUP BY T1.coachID
gold: SELECT C.coachID, SUM(C.l) AS total_losses FROM Coaches C JOIN Teams T ON C.tmID = T.tmID WHERE T.name = 'Tampa Bay Lightning' AND C.year = 1997 AND C.notes = 'interim' GROUP BY C.coachID;

question: Among the players whose short handed assists are greater or equal to 7, what is the final standing of the team with the most number of assists? Indicate the year to which the most number of assists was achieved and the name of the team.
evidence: short handed assists refers to SHA; SHA> = 7; final standing refers to rank; the final standing of the team with the most number of assists refers to max(A)
SQL: SELECT T2.rank, T2.year, T2.name FROM Scoring AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year WHERE T1.SHA >= 7 ORDER BY T1.A DESC LIMIT 1
gold: SELECT T.year, T.name, T.rank FROM Teams T JOIN (SELECT year, tmID, MAX(TotalSHA) AS MaxSHA FROM (SELECT year, tmID, SUM(SHA) AS TotalSHA FROM Scoring WHERE SHA >= 7 GROUP BY year, tmID) GROUP BY year, tmID) S ON T.year = S.year AND T.tmID = S.tmID

question: What is the name of the coach whose team placed 4th in the 1969 game? Indicate their coachID.
evidence: name of coach refers to coachID; placed 4th refers to rank = 4; 1969 game refers to year = 1969
SQL: SELECT T1.coachID FROM Coaches AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year WHERE T1.year = 1969 AND T2.rank = 4
gold: SELECT DISTINCT C.coachID FROM Coaches C, Teams T WHERE C.year = T.year AND C.tmID = T.tmID AND T.year = 1969 AND T.rank = 4;

question: Between 1917 to 1920, what are the names of the team who ranked first in the first half of the season each year?
evidence: year BETWEEN 1917 AND 1920; first half of season refers to half = 1
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT T2.name FROM TeamsHalf AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year WHERE T1.half = 1 AND T1.rank = 1 AND T1.year BETWEEN 1917 AND 1920
gold: SELECT T2.name FROM TeamsHalf T1 JOIN Teams T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year WHERE T1.year BETWEEN 1917 AND 1920 AND T1.half = 1 AND T1.rank = 1;

question: How many Canadian players, between the ages of 18 and 24 when they initially played their first NHL, had a cumulative goal total of no more than 5? Indicate their complete names, the year, and the team for which they scored the specified amount of goals.
evidence: Canadian players mean player whose birthCountry = Canada; ages of 18 and 24 refers to SUBTRACT(firstNHL, birthYear) BETWEEN 18 AND 24; cumulative goal total of no more than 5 refers to G < 5; complete name = nameGiven + lastName
SQL: SELECT M.nameGiven || ' ' || M.lastName AS fullName, S.year, S.tmID FROM Master M JOIN Scoring S ON M.playerID = S.playerID WHERE M.birthCountry = 'Canada' AND (M.firstNHL - M.birthYear) BETWEEN 18 AND 24 GROUP BY M.playerID HAVING SUM(S.G) <= 5;
gold: SELECT M.nameGiven || ' ' || M.lastName AS fullName, S.year, S.tmID FROM Master M JOIN Scoring S ON M.playerID = S.playerID WHERE M.birthCountry = 'Canada' AND (M.firstNHL - M.birthYear) BETWEEN 18 AND 24 GROUP BY M.playerID HAVING SUM(S.G) <= 5;

question: Which team got the most bench minor penalties in 2006?

question: What is the percentage of reviews added each year of the total reviews added?

SQL: SELECT MIN(tmin) FROM weather AS T1 INNER JOIN relation AS T2 ON T1.station_nbr = T2.station_nbr WHERE T2.store_nbr = 16 AND T1.`date` LIKE '%2012-01%'
gold: SELECT MIN(tmin) FROM weather WHERE station_nbr IN (SELECT station_nbr FROM relation WHERE store_nbr = 16) AND strftime('%Y-%m', date) = '2012-01'

question: How many units of item 7 have been sold by store 7 when the snow is less than 5 inches?
evidence: item 7 refers to item_nbr = 7; store 7 refers to store_nbr = 7; snow is less than 5 inches refers to snowfall < 5
SQL: SELECT SUM(units) FROM weather AS T1 INNER JOIN relation AS T2 ON T1.station_nbr = T2.station_nbr INNER JOIN sales_in_weather AS T3 ON T2.store_nbr = T3.store_nbr WHERE T2.store_nbr = 7 AND T3.item_nbr = 7 AND T1.snowfall < 5
gold: SELECT TOTAL(units) FROM sales_in_weather AS S JOIN relation AS R ON S.store_nbr = R.store_nbr JOIN weather AS W ON R.station_nbr = W.station_nbr AND S.date = W.date WHERE S.item_nbr = 7 AND S.store_nbr = 7 AND W.snowfall < 5;

question: How many items were sold by store 9 during a snowy day?
evidence: store 9 refers to store_nbr = 9; snowy day refers to snowfall < > 0 and snowfall is not null; item refers to item_nbr
SQL: SELECT TOTAL(units) FROM sales_in_weather AS S JOIN relation AS R ON S.store_nbr = R.store_nbr JOIN weather AS W ON R.station_nbr = W.station_nbr WHERE S.store_nbr = 9 AND W.snowfall > 0 AND W.snowfall IS NOT NULL AND S.date = W.date;
gold: SELECT TOTAL(units) FROM sales_in_weather AS S JOIN relation AS R ON S.store_nbr = R.store_nbr JOIN weather AS W ON R.station_nbr = W.station_nbr WHERE S.store_nbr = 9 AND W.snowfall > 0 AND W.snowfall IS NOT NULL AND S.date = W.date;

question: List out stations number and items sold by store 17.

gold: SELECT T1.station_nbr, T2.item_nbr FROM relation T1 JOIN sales_in_weather T2 ON T1.store_nbr = T2.store_nbr WHERE T1.store_nbr = 17;

question: What is the sea level and average speed for store number 3 and store number 4?

SQL: SELECT T1.sealevel, T1.avgspeed FROM weather AS T1 INNER JOIN relation AS T2 ON T1.station_nbr = T2.station_nbr WHERE T2.store_nbr = 3 OR T2.store_nbr = 4
gold: SELECT sealevel, avgspeed FROM weather WHERE station_nbr IN (SELECT station_nbr FROM relation WHERE store_nbr = 3 OR store_nbr = 4);

question: Which items from store 1 have the highest units sold during rainy day?
evidence: store 1 refers to store_nbr = 1; highest unit sold refers to Max(units); during rainy day refers to codesum like '%'||'RA'||'%'; item refers to item_nbr
SQL: SELECT item_nbr FROM (SELECT item_nbr, SUM(units) AS total_units FROM sales_in_weather WHERE store_nbr = 1 AND date IN (SELECT date FROM weather WHERE codesum LIKE '%RA%') GROUP BY item_nbr) ORDER BY total_units DESC LIMIT 1;
gold: SELECT item_nbr FROM (SELECT item_nbr, SUM(units) AS total_units FROM sales_in_weather WHERE store_nbr = 1 AND date IN (SELECT date FROM weather WHERE codesum LIKE '%RA%') GROUP BY item_nbr) ORDER BY total_units DESC LIMIT 1;

question: What is the ratio of the highest and lowest temperature in store 11?
evidence: store 11 refers to store_nbr = 11; highest temperature refers to Max(tmax); lowest temperature refers to Min(tmin); ration = Divide (Max(tmax), Min(tmin))
SQL: SELECT CAST((MAX(T1.tmax) - MIN(T1.tmin)) AS REAL) / MIN(T1.tmin) FROM weather AS T1 INNER JOIN relation AS T2 ON T1.station_nbr = T2.station_nbr WHERE T2.store_nbr = 11
gold: SELECT MAX(W.tmax) / MIN(W.tmin) AS temperature_ratio FROM relation R JOIN weather W ON R.station_nbr = W.station_nbr WHERE R.store_nbr = 11;

question: What was the difference of number of units sold in station number 1 and number 2 on year 2012?
evidence: station 1 refers to station_nbr = 1; station 2 refers to station_nbr = 2; on year 2012 refers to substring (date, 1, 4) = '2012'; difference = Subtract (Sum(units where station_nbr = 1), Sum(units where station_nbr = 2))
SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T1.station_nbr = 1 THEN units ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN T1.station_nbr = 2 THEN units ELSE 0 END) FROM relation AS T1 INNER JOIN sales_in_weather AS T2 ON T1.store_nbr = T2.store_nbr WHERE T2.`date` LIKE '%2012%'
gold: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T2.station_nbr = 1 THEN T1.units ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN T2.station_nbr = 2 THEN T1.units ELSE 0 END) AS difference FROM sales_in_weather T1 JOIN relation T2 ON T1.store_nbr = T2.store_nbr WHERE strftime('%Y', T1.date) = '2012';

question: What was the average temperature difference between store number 18 and 19 on 16 September 2022?
evidence: store number 18 refers to store_nbr = 18; store number 19 refers to store_nbr = 19; on 16 September 2022 refers to date = '2022-09-16'; average temperature difference = Subtract(tavg where store_nbr = 18, tavg where store_nbr = 19)
SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T1.store_nbr = 18 THEN T2.tavg ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN T1.store_nbr = 19 THEN T2.tavg ELSE 0 END) FROM relation AS T1 INNER JOIN weather AS T2 ON T1.station_nbr = T2.station_nbr WHERE T2.`date` = '2012-09-16'
gold: SELECT ABS((SELECT tavg FROM weather WHERE station_nbr = (SELECT station_nbr FROM relation WHERE store_nbr = 18) AND date = '2022-09-16') - (SELECT tavg FROM weather WHERE station_nbr = (SELECT station_nbr FROM relation WHERE store_nbr = 19) AND date = '2022-09-16')) AS temperature_difference;

question: How many units are being sold for item 1 when the average temperature is 83?
evidence: item 1 refers to item_nbr = 1; when the average temperature is 83 refers to tavg = 83
SQL: SELECT SUM(units) FROM weather AS T1 INNER JOIN sales_in_weather AS T2 ON T1.`date` = T2.`date` INNER JOIN relation AS T3 ON T2.store_nbr = T3.store_nbr WHERE T2.item_nbr = 1 AND T1.tavg = 83
gold: SELECT SUM(T1.units) FROM sales_in_weather T1 JOIN relation T2 ON T1.store_nbr = T2.store_nbr JOIN weather T3 ON T2.station_nbr = T3.station_nbr WHERE T1.item_nbr = 1 AND T3.tavg = 83;

question: What is the difference between the units sold for item 1 when the sunset was the earliest and the latest?
evidence: item 1 refers to item_nbr = 1; when the sunset earliest refers to Min(sunset); latest sunset refers to Max(sunset); difference unit sold refers to Subtract(Sum(units where Min(sunset)), Sum(units where Max(sunset)))
SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN W.sunset = MinSunset THEN S.units ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN W.sunset = MaxSunset THEN S.units ELSE 0 END) AS difference FROM sales_in_weather S JOIN weather W ON S.date = W.date, (SELECT MIN(sunset) AS MinSunset, MAX(sunset) AS MaxSunset FROM weather) AS SunExtremes WHERE S.item_nbr = 1;
gold: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN W.sunset = MinSunset THEN S.units ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN W.sunset = MaxSunset THEN S.units ELSE 0 END) AS difference FROM sales_in_weather S JOIN weather W ON S.date = W.date, (SELECT MIN(sunset) AS MinSunset, MAX(sunset) AS MaxSunset FROM weather) AS SunExtremes WHERE S.item_nbr = 1;

question: What was the total unit sold for item 10 when the average temperature was below the median temperature?
evidence: item 10 refers to item_nbr = 10; average temperature below median temperature refers to tavg < avg(tavg); total units refers to Sum(units)
SQL: SELECT SUM(T5.units) FROM weather AS T4 INNER JOIN sales_in_weather AS T5 ON T4.`date` = T5.`date` INNER JOIN relation AS T6 ON T5.store_nbr = T6.store_nbr WHERE T5.item_nbr = 10 AND T4.tavg < ( SELECT AVG(T1.tavg) FROM weather AS T1 INNER JOIN sales_in_weather AS T2 ON T1.`date` = T2.`date` INNER JOIN relation AS T3 ON T2.store_nbr = T3.store_nbr WHERE T2.item_nbr = 10 )
gold: SELECT SUM(S.units) FROM sales_in_weather S JOIN relation R ON S.store_nbr = R.store_nbr JOIN weather W ON R.station_nbr = W.station_nbr AND S.date = W.date WHERE S.item_nbr = 10 AND W.tavg < (SELECT AVG(tavg) FROM weather);

question: What was the average temperature differences during May 2012 for store number 6 and 7?
evidence: during May 2012 refers to SUBSTR(date, 1, 7) = '2012-05'; store number 6 refers to store_nbr = 6; store number 7 refers to store_nbr = 7; average temperature difference = Subtract (Divide (Sum(tavg), Count (date) where the store_nbr = 6), Divide (Sum(tavg), Count(date) where store_nbr = 7))
SQL: SELECT ( SELECT CAST(SUM(tavg) AS REAL) / COUNT(`date`) FROM weather AS T1 INNER JOIN relation AS T2 ON T1.station_nbr = T2.station_nbr AND T1.`date` LIKE '%2012-05%' AND T2.store_nbr = 6 ) - ( SELECT CAST(SUM(tavg) AS REAL) / COUNT(`date`) FROM weather AS T1 INNER JOIN relation AS T2 ON T1.station_nbr = T2.station_nbr WHERE T1.`date` LIKE '%2012-05%' AND T2.store_nbr = 7 )
gold: SELECT AVG(T1.tavg) - AVG(T2.tavg) AS avg_temp_difference FROM (SELECT W.tavg FROM sales_in_weather S JOIN relation R ON S.store_nbr = R.store_nbr JOIN weather W ON R.station_nbr = W.station_nbr WHERE S.store_nbr = 6 AND SUBSTR(W.date, 1, 7) = '2012-05') T1, (SELECT W.tavg FROM sales_in_weather S JOIN relation R ON S.store_nbr = R.store_nbr JOIN weather W ON R.station_nbr = W.station_nbr WHERE S.store_nbr = 7 AND SUBSTR(W.date, 1, 7) = '2012-05') T2

question: Calculate the percentage of population in Edmonton city to the population of its province.

question:
Which federal republic country in Europe has the most provinces, and what proportion of GDP is devoted to services?

SQL: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.arrest = 'TRUE' THEN T2.report_no END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T2.report_no) FROM Community_Area AS T1 INNER JOIN Crime AS T2 ON T2.community_area_no = T1.community_area_no WHERE T1.community_area_name = 'West Pullman' AND T2.domestic = 'TRUE'
gold: SELECT (COUNT(CASE WHEN T1.arrest = 'TRUE' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(T1.report_no)) AS arrest_percentage FROM Crime T1 JOIN Community_Area T2 ON T1.community_area_no = T2.community_area_no WHERE T1.domestic = 'TRUE' AND T2.community_area_name = 'West Pullman';

question: Calculate the percentage of the domestic violence cases handled by Christopher Taliaferro. Among them, list report numbers of cases that happened in the bank.

SQL: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T1.domestic = 'TRUE' THEN T1.report_no END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T1.report_no), COUNT(CASE WHEN T1.domestic = 'TRUE' AND T1.location_description = 'BANK' THEN T1.report_no END) AS "number" FROM Crime AS T1 INNER JOIN Ward AS T2 ON T2.ward_no = T1.ward_no WHERE T2.alderman_first_name = 'Christopher' AND T2.alderman_last_name = 'Taliaferro'
gold: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Crime T1 JOIN Ward T2 ON T1.ward_no = T2.ward_no WHERE T2.alderman_first_name = 'Christopher' AND T2.alderman_last_name = 'Taliaferro' AND T1.domestic = 'TRUE') * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Crime T1 JOIN Ward T2 ON T1.ward_no = T2.ward_no WHERE T2.alderman_first_name = 'Christopher' AND T2.alderman_last_name = 'Taliaferro') AS percentage, (SELECT report_no FROM Crime T1 JOIN Ward T2 ON T1.ward_no = T2.ward_no WHERE T2.alderman_first_name = 'Christopher' AND T2.alderman_last_name = 'Taliaferro' AND T1.domestic = 'TRUE' AND T1.location_description = 'BANK') AS report_numbers;

question: Calculate the difference in the average number of vehicular hijackings and aggravated vehicular hijackings in the districts.
evidence: "VEHICULAR HIJACKING" and "AGGRAVATED VEHICULAR HIJACKING" are both secondary_description; difference in average = Subtract (Divide(Count(secondary_description = 'VEHICULAR HIJACKING'), Count(district_name)), Divide(Count(secondary_description = "AGGRAVATED VEHICULAR HIJACKING"), Count(district_name)))
SQL: SELECT AVG(COUNT_VH) - AVG(COUNT_AVH) AS difference FROM (SELECT T1.district_no, COUNT(NULLIF(T2.secondary_description, 'VEHICULAR HIJACKING')) AS COUNT_VH, COUNT(NULLIF(T2.secondary_description, 'AGGRAVATED VEHICULAR HIJACKING')) AS COUNT_AVH FROM Crime T1 JOIN IUCR T2 ON T1.iucr_no = T2.iucr_no GROUP BY T1.district_no);
gold: SELECT (SUM(CASE WHEN T2.secondary_description = 'VEHICULAR HIJACKING' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(DISTINCT T1.district_no)) - (SUM(CASE WHEN T2.secondary_description = 'AGGRAVATED VEHICULAR HIJACKING' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(DISTINCT T1.district_no)) AS difference FROM Crime T1 INNER JOIN IUCR T2 ON T1.iucr_no = T2.iucr_no INNER JOIN District T3 ON T1.district_no = T3.district_no;

question: What is the weekly average number of fraud incidents that were reported in January 2018? Provide the description of the location where the majority of fraud incidents occurred in the said month.
evidence: fraud incident refers to title = 'Fraud'; reported in January 2018 refers to Substr(date, 1, 1) = '1' AND Substr(date, 5, 4) = '2018'; description of location refers to location_description; weekly average refers to Divide (Count(report_no), 4); majority of incidents occurred refers to Max(Count(location_description))
SQL: SELECT CAST(COUNT(T1.fbi_code_no) AS REAL) / 4 FROM FBI_Code AS T1 INNER JOIN Crime AS T2 ON T1.fbi_code_no = T2.fbi_code_no WHERE SUBSTR(T2.date, 1, 1) = '1' AND SUBSTR(T2.date, 5, 4) = '2018'

SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employee AS T1  INNER JOIN location AS T2  ON T1.locationID = T2.locationID INNER JOIN position AS T3  ON T3.positionID = T1.positionID WHERE T3.positiontitle = 'Account Representative' AND T1.performance = 'Good' AND T2.state = 'IL'
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employee AS T1 JOIN position AS T2 ON T1.positionID = T2.positionID JOIN location AS T3 ON T1.locationID = T3.locationID WHERE T2.positiontitle = 'Account Representative' AND T3.state = 'IL' AND T1.performance = 'Good';

question: What is the average salary of the worst performing managers?
evidence: the worst performing refers to performance = 'Poor'; manager is a positiontitle; average salary refers to AVG(salary)
SQL: SELECT AVG(CAST(REPLACE(SUBSTR(T1.salary, 4), ',', '') AS REAL)) FROM employee AS T1 INNER JOIN position AS T2  ON T1.positionID = T2.positionID WHERE T1.performance = 'Poor' AND T2.positiontitle = 'Manager'
gold: SELECT AVG(CAST(T1.salary AS INTEGER)) FROM employee T1 JOIN position T2 ON T1.positionID = T2.positionID WHERE T2.positiontitle = 'manager' AND T1.performance = 'Poor'

question: In which state can you find the highest amount of good performing Account Representatives?

question: Calculate the monthly average salary of the employee with highest salary. Mention his name, position title and location city.
evidence: highest salary refers to MAX(salary); name = firstname, lastname; calculation = DIVIDE(MAX(salary), 12)
SQL: SELECT SUM(CAST(REPLACE(SUBSTR(T1.salary, 4), ',', '') AS REAL)) / 12 AS avg, T1.firstname, T1.lastname , T2.positiontitle, T3.locationcity FROM employee AS T1  INNER JOIN position AS T2  ON T1.positionID = T2.positionID INNER JOIN location AS T3  ON T1.locationID = T3.locationID WHERE CAST(REPLACE(SUBSTR(T1.salary, 4), ',', '') AS REAL) = ( SELECT MAX(CAST(REPLACE(SUBSTR(T1.salary, 4), ',', '') AS REAL)) FROM employee AS T1  INNER JOIN position AS T2  ON T1.positionID = T2.positionID INNER JOIN location AS T3  ON T1.locationID = T3.locationID )
gold: SELECT T1.firstname || ' ' || T1.lastname AS name, T2.positiontitle, T3.locationcity, MAX(T1.salary)/12 AS monthly_average_salary FROM employee T1 JOIN position T2 ON T1.positionID = T2.positionID JOIN location T3 ON T1.locationID = T3.locationID WHERE T1.salary = (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employee) GROUP BY T1.firstname, T1.lastname, T2.positiontitle, T3.locationcity

question: For all trips which took less 5 minutes, state the station name where the bike were borrowed and returned. Indicate mean temperature of the day.

question: Among all the trips, which day had the most bikes borrowed? What was the average coldest temperature on that day?

SQL: SELECT SUBSTR(T1.start_date, 1, INSTR(T1.start_date, ' ') - 1) AS trip_date, AVG(T2.min_temperature_f) AS avg_min_temp FROM trip T1 JOIN weather T2 ON SUBSTR(T1.start_date, 1, INSTR(T1.start_date, ' ') - 1) = T2.date GROUP BY trip_date ORDER BY COUNT(T1.id) DESC LIMIT 1;
gold: SELECT SUBSTR(T1.start_date, 1, INSTR(T1.start_date, ' ') - 1) AS trip_date, AVG(T2.min_temperature_f) AS avg_min_temp FROM trip T1 JOIN weather T2 ON SUBSTR(T1.start_date, 1, INSTR(T1.start_date, ' ') - 1) = T2.date GROUP BY trip_date ORDER BY COUNT(T1.id) DESC LIMIT 1;

question: On 10/20/2014, what is the duration of the fastest trip which started from the station with latitude and longitudes of 37.789625 and -122.400811, respectively? Indicate the bike id.

question: Which day in the month of November, 2014 have a foggy weather in the zip code 94301 and in total, how many bikes were borrowed by subscribers from all of the stations in the said day?

SQL: SELECT SUBSTR(T1.start_date, 1, 9) AS day, COUNT(T1.id) AS total_bikes FROM trip T1 JOIN weather T2 ON SUBSTR(T1.start_date, 1, 9) = T2.date WHERE T2.events = 'Fog' AND T2.zip_code = '94301' AND T1.subscription_type = 'Subscriber' AND T1.start_date LIKE '11/%/2014%' GROUP BY day;

SQL: SELECT T1.rental_rate FROM film AS T1 INNER JOIN film_category AS T2 ON T1.film_id = T2.film_id INNER JOIN category AS T3 ON T2.category_id = T3.category_id WHERE T3.name = 'Children' ORDER BY T1.rental_rate / T1.rental_duration DESC LIMIT 1

question: How much percentage of the film did Mary Keitel perform more than Angela Witherspoon?

SQL: SELECT COUNT(customer_id) FROM rental WHERE return_date - rental_date > ( SELECT AVG(return_date - rental_date) FROM rental )
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM rental WHERE (julianday(return_date) - julianday(rental_date)) > (SELECT AVG(julianday(return_date) - julianday(rental_date)) FROM rental WHERE return_date IS NOT NULL AND rental_date IS NOT NULL);

question: Among the movies, what percentage are horror?
evidence: horror is a name of film category; calculation = DIVIDE(COUNT('horror'), COUNT(category_id)) * 100
SQL: SELECT CAST(SUM(IIF(T2.name = 'horror', 1, 0)) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T2.category_id) FROM film_category AS T1 INNER JOIN category AS T2 ON T1.category_id = T2.category_id
gold: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT T2.film_id) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM film)) AS percentage FROM category T1 JOIN film_category T2 ON T1.category_id = T2.category_id WHERE T1.name = 'Horror';

question: What is the difference in the average number of films rented each day in Australia and Canada?
evidence: 'Australia' AND 'Canada' are country; average number of films refers to AVG('Australia') AND AVG('Canada'); calculation = SUBTRACT(AVG('Australia'), AVG('Canada'))
SQL: SELECT AVG(IIF(T4.country = 'Australia', 1, 0)) - AVG(IIF(T4.country = 'Canada', 1, 0)) AS diff FROM customer AS T1 INNER JOIN address AS T2 ON T1.address_id = T2.address_id INNER JOIN city AS T3 ON T2.city_id = T3.city_id INNER JOIN country AS T4 ON T3.country_id = T4.country_id
gold: SELECT AVG(Australia.rentals_per_day) - AVG(Canada.rentals_per_day) AS difference FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) / COUNT(DISTINCT DATE(rental_date)) AS rentals_per_day FROM rental JOIN inventory ON rental.inventory_id = inventory.inventory_id JOIN store ON inventory.store_id = store.store_id JOIN address ON store.address_id = address.address_id JOIN city ON address.city_id = city.city_id JOIN country ON city.country_id = country.country_id WHERE country.country = 'Australia') AS Australia, (SELECT COUNT(*) / COUNT(DISTINCT DATE(rental_date)) AS rentals_per_day FROM rental JOIN inventory ON rental.inventory_id = inventory.inventory_id JOIN store ON inventory.store_id = store.store_id JOIN address ON store.address_id = address.address_id JOIN city ON address.city_id = city.city_id JOIN country ON city.country_id = country.country_id WHERE country.country = 'Canada') AS Canada;

question: Give the total amount of rent for the movie Clockwork Paradice.
evidence: 'Clockwork Paradice' is a title of a film
SQL: SELECT SUM(T1.amount) FROM payment AS T1 INNER JOIN rental AS T2 ON T1.rental_id = T2.rental_id INNER JOIN inventory AS T3 ON T2.inventory_id = T3.inventory_id INNER JOIN film AS T4 ON T3.film_id = T4.film_id WHERE T4.title = 'CLOCKWORK PARADICE'
gold: SELECT SUM(P.amount) FROM film F JOIN inventory I ON F.film_id = I.film_id JOIN rental R ON I.inventory_id = R.inventory_id JOIN payment P ON R.rental_id = P.rental_id WHERE F.title = 'Clockwork Paradice';

question: Find and list the full name of customers who rented more than five types of movies.
evidence:
full name refers to first_name, last_name; types of movies means category of movies; 
rented more than five types of movies refers to COUNT(film_category) > 5
SQL: SELECT T.first_name, T.last_name FROM ( SELECT T1.first_name, T1.last_name, COUNT(T1.customer_id) AS num FROM customer AS T1 INNER JOIN rental AS T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id INNER JOIN inventory AS T3 ON T2.inventory_id = T3.inventory_id INNER JOIN film AS T4 ON T3.film_id = T4.film_id INNER JOIN film_category AS T5 ON T4.film_id = T5.film_id GROUP BY T1.first_name, T1.last_name ) AS T WHERE T.num > 5
gold: SELECT T1.first_name || ' ' || T1.last_name AS full_name FROM customer T1 JOIN rental T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id JOIN inventory T3 ON T2.inventory_id = T3.inventory_id JOIN film T4 ON T3.film_id = T4.film_id JOIN film_category T5 ON T4.film_id = T5.film_id GROUP BY T1.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT T5.category_id) > 5;

question: Calculate the percentage of customers who paid more than the average rent amount in store 1.
evidence: store 1 refers to store_id = 1; average rent amount refers to AVG(amount); calculation = DIVIDE(amount > AVG(amount), COUNT(customer_id)) * 100
SQL: SELECT CAST(( SELECT COUNT(T1.customer_id) FROM customer AS T1 INNER JOIN payment AS T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id WHERE T2.amount > ( SELECT AVG(amount) FROM payment ) ) AS REAL) * 100 / ( SELECT COUNT(customer_id) FROM customer )
gold: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT T2.customer_id) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM customer WHERE store_id = 1)) AS percentage FROM payment T1 JOIN customer T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id WHERE T2.store_id = 1 AND T1.amount > (SELECT AVG(amount) FROM payment JOIN customer ON payment.customer_id = customer.customer_id WHERE customer.store_id = 1);

SQL: SELECT COUNT(T2.customer_id) FROM address AS T1 INNER JOIN customer AS T2 ON T1.address_id = T2.address_id INNER JOIN city AS T3 ON T1.city_id = T3.city_id WHERE T2.active = 1 AND T3.city = 'Arlington'
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.customer_id) FROM customer T1 JOIN address T2 ON T1.address_id = T2.address_id JOIN city T3 ON T2.city_id = T3.city_id WHERE T1.active = 1 AND T3.city = 'Arlington';

question: Please list the full names of all the customers who live in Italy.
evidence: full name refers to first_name, last_name; Italy refers to country = 'Italy'
SQL: SELECT T4.first_name, T4.last_name FROM address AS T1 INNER JOIN city AS T2 ON T1.city_id = T2.city_id INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T2.country_id = T3.country_id INNER JOIN customer AS T4 ON T1.address_id = T4.address_id WHERE T3.country = 'Italy'
gold: SELECT first_name || ' ' || last_name AS full_name FROM customer T1 JOIN address T2 ON T1.address_id = T2.address_id JOIN city T3 ON T2.city_id = T3.city_id JOIN country T4 ON T3.country_id = T4.country_id WHERE T4.country = 'Italy';

question: What is the biggest amount of payment for a rental made by Mary Smith?
evidence: the biggest amount refers to max(amount)
SQL: SELECT MAX(T2.amount) FROM customer T1 JOIN payment T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id WHERE T1.first_name = 'Mary' AND T1.last_name = 'Smith';
gold: SELECT MAX(T2.amount) FROM customer T1 JOIN payment T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id WHERE T1.first_name = 'Mary' AND T1.last_name = 'Smith';

question: How many times has Mary Smith rented a film?
SQL: SELECT COUNT(T1.customer_id) FROM payment AS T1 INNER JOIN customer AS T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id WHERE T2.first_name = 'MARY' AND T2.last_name = 'SMITH'
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rental WHERE customer_id = (SELECT customer_id FROM customer WHERE first_name = 'Mary' AND last_name = 'Smith');

question: What is the total amount of money Mary Smith has spent on film rentals?
evidence: the total amount = sum(amount)
SQL: SELECT SUM(T2.amount) FROM customer T1 JOIN payment T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id WHERE T1.first_name = 'Mary' AND T1.last_name = 'Smith';
gold: SELECT SUM(T2.amount) FROM customer T1 JOIN payment T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id WHERE T1.first_name = 'Mary' AND T1.last_name = 'Smith';

question: Among the times Mary Smith had rented a movie, how many of them happened in June, 2005?
evidence: in June 2005 refers to year(payment_date) = 2005 and month(payment_date) = 6
SQL: SELECT COUNT(T1.customer_id) FROM payment AS T1 INNER JOIN customer AS T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id WHERE T2.first_name = 'MARY' AND T2.last_name = 'SMITH' AND STRFTIME('%Y',T1.payment_date) = '2005' AND STRFTIME('%Y', T1.payment_date) = '6'
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rental AS T1 JOIN customer AS T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id WHERE T2.first_name = 'Mary' AND T2.last_name = 'Smith' AND strftime('%Y', T1.rental_date) = '2005' AND strftime('%m', T1.rental_date) = '06'

question: How much in total had the customers in Italy spent on film rentals?
evidence: total = sum(amount); Italy refers to country = 'Italy'
SQL: SELECT SUM(T5.amount) FROM address AS T1 INNER JOIN city AS T2 ON T1.city_id = T2.city_id INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T2.country_id = T3.country_id INNER JOIN customer AS T4 ON T1.address_id = T4.address_id INNER JOIN payment AS T5 ON T4.customer_id = T5.customer_id WHERE T3.country = 'Italy'
gold: SELECT SUM(P.amount) FROM payment P JOIN customer C ON P.customer_id = C.customer_id JOIN address A ON C.address_id = A.address_id JOIN city CI ON A.city_id = CI.city_id JOIN country CO ON CI.country_id = CO.country_id WHERE CO.country = 'Italy';

question: Among the payments made by Mary Smith, how many of them are over 4.99?
evidence: over 4.99 refers to amount > 4.99
SQL: SELECT COUNT(T1.amount) FROM payment AS T1 INNER JOIN customer AS T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id WHERE T2.first_name = 'MARY' AND T2.last_name = 'SMITH' AND T1.amount > 4.99
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM payment AS T1 JOIN customer AS T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id WHERE T2.first_name = 'Mary' AND T2.last_name = 'Smith' AND T1.amount > 4.99;

question: What is the average amount of money spent by a customer in Italy on a single film rental?
evidence: Italy refers to country = 'Italy'; average amount = divide(sum(amount), count(customer_id)) where country = 'Italy'
SQL: SELECT AVG(T5.amount) FROM address AS T1 INNER JOIN city AS T2 ON T1.city_id = T2.city_id INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T2.country_id = T3.country_id INNER JOIN customer AS T4 ON T1.address_id = T4.address_id INNER JOIN payment AS T5 ON T4.customer_id = T5.customer_id WHERE T3.country = 'Italy'
gold: SELECT AVG(T1.amount) AS average_spent FROM payment T1 JOIN customer T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id JOIN address T3 ON T2.address_id = T3.address_id JOIN city T4 ON T3.city_id = T4.city_id JOIN country T5 ON T4.country_id = T5.country_id WHERE T5.country = 'Italy';
